jon-rahm:2025-05-13.lede: Jon Rahm is a Spanish professional golfer, a former world number one, and a two-time major champion, having won the 2021 U.S. Open at Torrey Pines and the 2023 Masters Tournament. He moved to LIV Golf in December 2023. The Odyssey Rossie S head has been a constant through every Callaway-era snapshot, first as a White Hot OG and now in Ai-ONE dress. The Apex TCB blades in the 5-iron through pitching wedge slot have been in the bag since the earliest 2021 record, with an Apex Pro 4-iron and an Apex UT 21-degree driving iron rounding out the top of the set. The driver line has cycled through the Triple Diamond family on schedule, Epic Speed to Rogue ST to Paradym to Paradym Ai Smoke and now the Elyte, all sleeved with a Fujikura Ventus Black 7 X. The Chrome Soft X gave way to the Chrome Tour after the 2023 ball relaunch.
jon-rahm:2025-05-13.history_narrative: Rahm's late-2019 and 2020 snapshots show a full TaylorMade setup, SIM driver, P750 irons, Spider X, and TP5. The record then jumps to March 2021 with the bag already fully Callaway and Odyssey, anchored by the Apex TCB irons, an X Forged UT, and a 2-Ball Ten prototype putter. The Rossie S took over later in 2021 and has stayed in the bag since, while the driver progressed through Epic Speed, Rogue ST, Paradym, Paradym Ai Smoke, and now the Elyte Triple Diamond. The current build adds an Apex Pro 4-iron and the Apex UT at 21 degrees, with the Chrome Tour replacing the long-running Chrome Soft X.

scottie-scheffler:2025-12-09.lede: Scottie Scheffler is an American professional on the PGA Tour, a multiple major champion with Masters titles in 2022 and 2024, the 2025 PGA Championship, and the gold medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics. He was named PGA Tour Player of the Year in 2022, 2023, and 2024, and reached world number one in March 2022. The current setup runs a TaylorMade Qi4D driver at 8 degrees on a Fujikura Ventus Black 7 X, the latest step in a driver lineage that moved from PING G400 LST in 2021 to TaylorMade Stealth Plus, Stealth 2 Plus, Qi10, and now Qi4D. The TaylorMade P7TW blades from 5-iron through pitching wedge with True Temper Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 shafts have been in the bag across every snapshot on record, paired with Srixon Z U85 utilities at the top of the set and a Titleist Pro V1 ball that has never changed.
scottie-scheffler:2025-12-09.history_narrative: Across 15 snapshots dating to March 2021, the P7TW blades and Pro V1 ball are constants. The driver progression runs PING G400 LST to TaylorMade Stealth Plus in early 2022, Stealth 2 Plus through 2023, Qi10 across 2024 and into 2025, and Qi4D in the current build. The long irons shifted from Srixon ZX7 to Srixon Z U85 utilities during the 2022 season, and the putter moved from a Scotty Cameron Super Rat to a Scotty Cameron Timeless Tourtype GSS prototype, then briefly to a Logan Olson prototype in late 2023, before settling on the TaylorMade Spider Tour X that remains in play.

collin-morikawa:2026-05-04.lede: Collin Morikawa turned pro in 2019 after a decorated career at California, won the 2020 PGA Championship in his major debut at Harding Park, and added the 2021 Open Championship at Royal St George's to become the first player to win two different majors on debut. He also captured the 2021 WGC-Workday and has anchored multiple U.S. Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup squads. The current setup leans hard into TaylorMade's muscleback work, with the P730 carrying 7-iron through pitching wedge, P7CB in the mid-irons, and a P-DHY utility plugging the 4-iron slot behind the Qi4D LS driver. Across all 14 snapshots in the data the driver, irons, putter, and ball have come from TaylorMade, with no brand departures recorded at any point. The visible churn lives inside the TaylorMade catalog, most recently the move from the TP Soto family into the Spider Tour X and the swap from TP5 to TP5x.
collin-morikawa:2026-05-04.history_narrative: Every snapshot from August 2020 forward shows a full TaylorMade bag, with no outside brands appearing in driver, irons, putter, or ball. The iron stack evolved from a P750/P730 pairing into the long-running P770/P7MC/P730 blend, then shifted to P7CB in the mid-irons during 2024 and added a P-DHY utility by early 2026. The putter cycled through TP Soto Prototype, Spider FCG, TP Juno, TP Soto, and Spider ZT before landing on the Spider Tour X, and the ball moved from TP5 to TP5x across the 2023 to 2024 window.

jordan-spieth:2025-01-31.lede: Jordan Spieth turned pro in 2012 and won the Masters and U.S. Open in 2015, then added the Open Championship in 2017 to sit one leg shy of the career Grand Slam. He has logged more than a dozen PGA Tour wins and multiple Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup appearances for the United States. The bag is a Titleist build top to bottom, and it has been that way across every snapshot on file. Driver has moved within the family, from TS3 in 2020 to TSi3 through 2022 and into the current TSR2 at 10 degrees with a D1 SureFit setting and a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 X. Irons have cycled around the T100 chassis, with stretches running T100 only, splits with U-500, T200, or T150 long irons, and the current setup back to a straight T100 3-9 on Project X 125 6.5. The Scotty Cameron Circle T 009 and Pro V1x have not moved.
jordan-spieth:2025-01-31.history_narrative: Across nine snapshots from June 2020 to January 2025, Spieth has played Titleist exclusively. The driver progressed TS3 to TSi3 to TSR2, with the TSR2 in place since the March 2023 snapshot. Iron setups have rotated combinations around the T100, pairing it at various points with U-500, T200, and T150 long irons before returning to a full T100 3-9 in the current bag. The Scotty Cameron Circle T 009 putter and Pro V1x ball appear in every snapshot.

brooks-koepka:2025-05-15.lede: Brooks Koepka is a five-time major champion, with back-to-back U.S. Open titles in 2017 and 2018 and three PGA Championships in 2018, 2019, and 2023. A former world number one, he joined LIV Golf in 2022 and captains Smash GC, while continuing to tee it up in the majors. The driver in the current bag is a Titleist GT3 at 10 degrees, the third different brand at the top of the bag across these snapshots after TaylorMade and Srixon stints. Below the driver, the constants are loud. The Nike Vapor Fly Pro 3-iron has held its slot across every snapshot dating to 2021, a Srixon ZX7 or ZX7 MKII has filled out the mid and short irons throughout, and a Scotty Cameron has been the putter in every bag, with the Teryllium TNP2 returning after a one-year detour to a T5.5 in 2024.
brooks-koepka:2025-05-15.history_narrative: Driver is where the movement lives: TaylorMade SIM2 in early 2021, a run through Srixon ZX5, ZX7, and ZX5 MKII from late 2021 into 2023, back to TaylorMade with the Qi10 in 2024, and now the Titleist GT3. The Nike Vapor Fly Pro 3-iron and Srixon ZX7/ZX7 MKII irons have been fixtures across all seven snapshots. The putter has stayed a Scotty Cameron throughout, cycling from a T10 Select Newport 2 to the Teryllium TNP2, briefly to a T5.5 in 2024, and back to the Teryllium TNP2 in the current setup.

cameron-young:2026-05-03.lede: Cameron Young turned professional in 2019, earned PGA Tour Rookie of the Year honors for the 2021-22 season after finishing runner-up at The Open Championship at St Andrews, and broke through for his first PGA Tour win at the 2025 Wyndham Championship with a closing 59. He has represented the United States at the Presidents Cup. The bag reads Titleist top to bottom and has for every snapshot on file. The driver line traces TSi3 to TSR2 to TSR3 to GT2 to the current GT3 at 11 degrees with a Mitsubishi Diamana PD 60 TX, a steady march through Titleist's release cycle. The iron stack has settled into a T200 long iron, T100 at the 5, and the 631.CY blades from the 6 through 9, all on Dynamic Gold X7. The Scotty Cameron Phantom shape has been a constant since 2022, currently the 9.5R Tour Prototype. Ball is the Pro V1x Double Dot.
cameron-young:2026-05-03.history_narrative: Every snapshot from February 2022 forward shows a full Titleist setup, with no brand deviation across driver, irons, putter, or ball. The driver progressed through TSi3, TSR2, TSR3, GT2, and now GT3, tracking each new Titleist release. The iron makeup has rotated through T200, T150, T100, 620 MB, U-505, and the 631.CY blades, with the 631.CY present in every bag since November 2023. The putter has been a Scotty Cameron Phantom prototype throughout, moving from the T5 and T5.5 shapes to the current 9.5R, while the ball has cycled between Pro V1, Pro V1 Left Dot, and the current Pro V1x Double Dot.

rory-mcilroy:2026-04-12.lede: Rory McIlroy is a Northern Irish professional on the PGA Tour with five major championships to his name, including the 2025 Masters that completed the career Grand Slam. He has held the world number one ranking across multiple stints since first reaching it in 2012 and has compiled more than two dozen PGA Tour victories alongside Ryder Cup appearances dating back to 2010. The current build runs a TaylorMade Qi4D at nine degrees with a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 X, paired with a P760 4-iron and Rors Proto blades from five through nine on Project X 7.0 shafts. Every snapshot in the dataset, going back to early 2021, shows a full TaylorMade setup across driver, irons, putter, and ball. The Rors Proto irons have been a fixture throughout, and the Spider platform has carried the putter slot since the TP Juno was set aside after the March 2021 snapshot.
rory-mcilroy:2026-04-12.history_narrative: Across sixteen snapshots from March 2021 to April 2026, the bag has been entirely TaylorMade at every check. Drivers move from SIM2 to Stealth Plus to Stealth 2 Plus, then through Qi10 LS, Qi10, and into the current Qi4D. Iron setups cycle between P7MB, P770, P760, and unspecified protos around the constant Rors Proto blades, while the putter shifts from the TP Juno to the Spider X Hydro Blast, then Spider Tour X3, and settles on the Spider Tour X. The ball was TP5x through early 2024 before TP5 took over in the more recent snapshots.

justin-thomas:2025-04-20.lede: Justin Thomas is a two-time major champion, claiming the PGA Championship in 2017 and again in 2022, and a former World No. 1 on the PGA Tour. He has stacked more than a dozen Tour wins alongside a FedExCup title and multiple Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup appearances. The bag has been a Titleist build top to bottom across every snapshot on file, from the 917 D2 in 2017 through the current GT2 at 10 degrees in a D2 SureFit setting with a Mitsubishi Diamana Prototype shaft. The iron stack reads as a Thomas signature: a T200 utility at the 4, a T100 at the 5, and the 621.JT players cavity from 6 through 9, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. The Scotty Cameron rotation has been the only moving piece of real interest, cycling through X5 variants and Phantom tour prototypes before settling on the Phantom T5 Tour Prototype currently in play. Pro V1x throughout.
justin-thomas:2025-04-20.history_narrative: Across 13 snapshots dating back to 2017, every club logged has carried a Titleist stamp, with Pro V1x as the constant on the ball. Drivers progressed 917 D2 to TS3 to TSi3 to TSR3 to the current GT2. Irons moved from the 716 CB and 718 AP2/MB era into the T100 build, with the 620 MB giving way to the 621.JT and the T200 long iron and T100 5-iron layering in by 2024. The putter slot has churned the most, working through Circle T and X5 prototypes, a Phantom X 5, and the Phantom 9.2 and 9.5 tour builds before landing on the Phantom T5 Tour Prototype.

bryson-dechambeau:2026-05-14.lede: Bryson DeChambeau won the 2020 US Open at Winged Foot and the 2024 US Open at Pinehurst No. 2, the latter sealed by a bunker save on the 72nd hole. He turned professional out of SMU after claiming the 2015 NCAA individual title and US Amateur in the same season, and now plays LIV Golf as captain of Crushers GC. The driver slot tracks a four-brand path across the snapshots: Cobra through 2022, TaylorMade Stealth 2 Plus and BRNR Mini in 2023, and the Krank Formula Fire Pro from 2024 forward, with an LA Golf head also logged alongside the Krank in the May 2025 entry. The Avoda prototype irons have anchored the set since the April 2024 snapshot, currently shafted in LA Golf BAD prototypes. The SIK Pro C-Series armlock putter, now built on an LA Golf C2L-180, is the only club shape present in every snapshot back to March 2021.
bryson-dechambeau:2026-05-14.history_narrative: Drivers move from Cobra King LTD Pro and LTDx (2021 through mid-2022) to a TaylorMade pairing of the Stealth 2 Plus and BRNR Mini (2023) and then to the Krank Formula Fire Pro from April 2024 onward, with an LA Golf driver added in the May 2025 snapshot. Irons run through Cobra One Length builds in 2021 and 2022, a 2023 detour to PING i230 with a G410 Crossover, then the Avoda prototype from April 2024 to the present. The SIK Pro C-Series armlock putter shape is the single constant across all nine snapshots, gaining an LA Golf shaft along the way. Ball usage shifts from Bridgestone Tour B X (2021-2022) to Titleist Pro V1x Left Dash (2023-2024) and Pro V1x in the 2025 entry.

matthew-fitzpatrick:2026-04-19.lede: Matt Fitzpatrick is an English professional who won the 2022 U.S. Open at The Country Club, a course where he also took the 2013 U.S. Amateur, making him one of the few players to win both titles at the same venue. He has multiple PGA Tour and DP World Tour victories, including the 2023 RBC Heritage, and has been a fixture on European Ryder Cup teams. The driver in the bag now is a Titleist GT3 at 9 degrees, the first model change observed in the snapshot history, which had logged a Titleist TSi3 from 2021 through 2025. Titleist is the only driver brand on record across every snapshot. The PING i210 4-iron has held its slot the entire run, with the longer irons cycling between PING S55 and PING Blueprint S before S55 returned for the 5-9. The Bettinardi BB1 and the Pro V1x have never left.
matthew-fitzpatrick:2026-04-19.history_narrative: Across nine snapshots from 2021 to 2026, the driver stayed Titleist throughout, with the TSi3 logged from 2021 through May 2025 before the current GT3 replaced it. The PING i210 has been constant, paired first with PING S55 from 2022 through 2023, then PING Blueprint S in the 2024 and 2025 snapshots, and back to S55 in the current bag. The Bettinardi BB1 has been the only putter on record, shifting from the DASS BB1 Flow Tour Dept stamp to the BB1 Fitz build, and the Titleist Pro V1x has been the ball in every snapshot.

justin-rose:2026-04-27.lede: Rose is the 2013 U.S. Open champion, 2016 Olympic gold medalist, and a former World No. 1 who captured the FedExCup in 2018. The Englishman has been a fixture on European Ryder Cup teams since 2008, with a professional career that began after his amateur finish at the 1998 Open Championship at Birkdale. The current setup pairs a Callaway Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond Max driver with McLaren Golf CB and MB prototype irons, a combination that landed after a stretch on Miura TC-502 and MC-502 blades. The driver lineage across snapshots traces a clean arc from TaylorMade to Titleist to Callaway. The Scotty Cameron T-5 Tour Prototype has held the putter slot since taking over from the Axis1 Rose Prototype that ran through the 2021 to 2023 snapshots, and the ball has settled on Pro V1x after stops through TP5 and Pro V1 Left Dot.
justin-rose:2026-04-27.history_narrative: Driver brand moves TaylorMade to Titleist to Callaway across the eight historical snapshots, with M1 440 and M3 440 builds giving way to the TSi4, TSR3, GT3, and GT2 before the Paradym and Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond Max took the slot. Putter shows the longest single-model run, with the Axis1 Rose Prototype in the bag from 2021 through late 2023 before the Scotty Cameron T-5 Tour Prototype took over in 2024 and stayed. Iron rotation has been the busiest category, cycling through Mizuno MP-20, Srixon ZX, Cobra King CB and MB, TaylorMade P7MC, Titleist T100 and 620 MB, Miura TC-502 and MC-502, and now McLaren Golf CB and MB prototypes. Ball moved from TaylorMade TP5 to Titleist Pro V1, then Pro V1 Left Dot, and currently Pro V1x.

xander-schauffele:2025-01-03.lede: Xander Schauffele is a two-time major champion, claiming the 2024 PGA Championship at Valhalla and the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon. He also owns the 2020 Olympic gold medal from Tokyo and has been a fixture on US Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup squads since 2021. The Callaway relationship runs through every snapshot on file. Driver head has cycled through the Epic Speed Triple Diamond, Rogue ST Triple Diamond S, Paradym Triple Diamond, Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond, and now the Elyte Triple Diamond, but the Triple Diamond profile itself has never left the bag. The Apex TCB irons have been a constant since the earliest 2021 snapshot, with a brief Mizuno MP-20 and MP-20 HMB long-iron pairing showing up in 2024 before the set returned to a full Callaway block. The Odyssey Toulon Las Vegas 7CH prototype replaced the longtime O-Works #7 CH Red in 2024 and remains the gamer.
xander-schauffele:2025-01-03.history_narrative: Across eleven snapshots from February 2021 to January 2025, the bag stays inside the Callaway family at every position. Driver progresses through Epic Speed, Rogue ST, Paradym, Paradym Ai Smoke, and Elyte, all in Triple Diamond builds. The Apex TCB irons hold from 2021 forward, interrupted only by Mizuno MP-20 and MP-20 HMB long irons appearing in the January and July 2024 snapshots. Putter shifts from the O-Works #7 CH Red to the Odyssey Toulon Las Vegas 7CH prototype in 2024, and the ball moves through Chrome Soft X variants before settling on Chrome Tour.

j-j-spaun:2026-04-05.lede: J.J. Spaun is a PGA Tour professional who broke through at the 2022 Valero Texas Open for his first Tour title, then won the 2025 U.S. Open at Oakmont in a Monday finish that ended with a 64-foot putt on 18. He played his college golf at San Diego State and earned his Tour card via the Korn Ferry route. The Srixon iron lineage is the throughline here, every snapshot on file shows a Srixon set in the bag, currently a ZXi5 long iron paired with ZXi7s from 5 through pitching wedge, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. The driver chair has rotated, PING G425 LST in 2022, Callaway Paradym Triple Diamond in 2023, then Titleist GT3 by mid-2025 and still in play. The putter swap from a Scotty Cameron Newport 2 GSS Prototype to the L.A.B. Golf DF3 is the other meaningful move, and the Z-Star Diamond ball has been a constant where logged.
j-j-spaun:2026-04-05.history_narrative: Across five snapshots from 2022 forward, the driver brand has moved PING to Callaway to Titleist, landing on the GT3 with a Ventus Black VeloCore+ 6 X. Irons have been Srixon throughout, evolving from ZX/Z U65 through ZX7 and ZX Utility to the current ZXi5 and ZXi7 build. The putter changed from a Scotty Cameron Newport 2 GSS Prototype, briefly a different Scotty prototype in 2023, to the L.A.B. Golf DF3 by early 2025. Srixon Z-Star Diamond shows up as the ball in every snapshot that logs one.

chris-gotterup:2026-02-08.lede: Chris Gotterup is an American professional on the PGA Tour who broke through in 2024 with his maiden Tour win at the Myrtle Beach Classic, then followed up in 2025 with a win at the Genesis Scottish Open and a runner-up finish at the Open Championship at Royal Portrush the next week. He played his college golf at Rutgers and Oklahoma, earning the Haskins Award as the top collegiate player in 2022. The bag tells a tidy story. PING sits at the front with the G440 LST at 9 degrees, shafted in a Project X HZRDUS Smoke Black RDX 70 TX. Bridgestone handles the irons with the 220 MB blades from 4 through 9, paired with KBS C-Taper 130 X. The TaylorMade Spider X Tour rolls the Bridgestone Tour B X MindSet. Every anchor piece, driver, irons, putter, ball, matches the July 2025 snapshot.
chris-gotterup:2026-02-08.history_narrative: Across both snapshots in the dataset, the bag has not moved. PING G440 LST at the top, Bridgestone 220 MB irons in the middle, TaylorMade Spider X Tour on the greens, and the Bridgestone Tour B X MindSet in play. No brand turnover is visible in the available data.

russell-henley:2026-04-12.lede: Russell Henley is a PGA Tour veteran out of Macon, Georgia, who won in his Tour debut at the 2013 Sony Open and has added wins at the Honda Classic, Houston Open, Wyndham Championship, World Wide Technology Championship, and the 2024 Arnold Palmer Invitational. The University of Georgia product has represented the United States at the Presidents Cup. The bag reads as a full Titleist build, with the TSi3 driver returning to play after a 2025 stretch in the GT3. Irons have run T100 across every snapshot on file, now paired with a T250 driving iron at the top of the set and a brief 2025 detour through the T200. The Scotty Cameron T5 Prototype has been the gamer since 2024, following a longer run with the Special Select Timeless Tour Prototype and, before that, a Phantom X 12 Prototype in 2021. Pro V1x throughout.
russell-henley:2026-04-12.history_narrative: Across seven snapshots from 2021 to 2026, the bag has been Titleist top to bottom, with Pro V1x as the constant ball. Driver was TSi3 from 2021 through 2024, moved to GT3 in the 2025 snapshot, and is back to TSi3 in the current build. Irons have centered on T100 throughout, with T200 appearing in 2025 and a T250 4-iron now sitting at the top of the set. The putter progressed from a Phantom X 12 Prototype in 2021, to the Special Select Timeless Tour Prototype through 2023, to the Scotty Cameron T5 Prototype from 2024 onward.

ludvig-aberg:2026-03-15.lede: Ludvig Aberg turned professional in June 2023 after a decorated career at Texas Tech and earned PGA Tour status without ever playing a Korn Ferry event. He won the RSM Classic months into his rookie season, was selected to the European Ryder Cup team in Rome, finished runner-up at the 2024 Masters, and added the Genesis Invitational in early 2025. The bag has been Titleist from the driver down across every snapshot on file, with a Pro V1x in play throughout. The driver line tells the more interesting story: TSR2 through 2024, a move into the GT2 across the 2024-2025 stretch, then back to a TSR2 head at 9 degrees with the Ventus Black 6 X by March 2026. The T100 has been a constant in the iron set, with the 718 T-MB long irons dropped in favor of a straight 4-PW T100 block. The putter has stayed Odyssey, most recently the Ai-ONE #1.
ludvig-aberg:2026-03-15.history_narrative: Across six snapshots from June 2023 to March 2026, Aberg has stayed entirely inside the Titleist driver, iron, and ball ecosystem, with every putter logged as an Odyssey. The driver moved from TSR2 to GT2 and back to TSR2, while the iron set gradually consolidated, dropping the 718 T-MB long irons and a brief T200 appearance in favor of a single-model T100 build. The putter progressed through the White Hot Versa 1 lineage before the switch to the Ai-ONE #1 in the current bag, and the Pro V1x has not moved.

aaron-rai:2026-05-17.lede: Aaron Rai is an English professional who came up through the Asian Tour before establishing himself on the DP World Tour, where he picked up the Hong Kong Open and the Scottish Open among his early wins. He earned PGA Tour status and broke through with a win at the 2024 Wyndham Championship, building a reputation as one of the straightest drivers on tour. The TaylorMade M6 driver at 9 degrees is the headline carryover, still in the bag with an Aldila Synergy Blue 70 TX shaft despite being multiple model cycles old. The P7TW blades on Dynamic Gold S300 have been a fixture across every snapshot on file, as has the Pro V1. The flatstick is the recent change, a Spider Tour V replacing the HydroBlast TP DuPage that ran through the 2024 and early 2025 snapshots. A brief look at a Titleist GT2 driver shows up in the February 2025 data, but the M6 won out.
aaron-rai:2026-05-17.history_narrative: Across four snapshots the irons, driver, and ball have not moved: P7TW, M6, Pro V1. The February 2025 bag logged a Titleist GT2 alongside the M6, the only deviation from TaylorMade at the top of the bag, and it did not stick. The putter transitioned from the HydroBlast TP DuPage, present in 2024 through mid-2025, to the Spider Tour V by the May 2026 snapshot.

robert-macintyre:2025-08-17.lede: Robert MacIntyre is a left-handed Scottish professional who came up through the DP World Tour and now plays a full PGA Tour schedule. His breakthrough stretch in 2024 produced a Canadian Open title with his father on the bag and a Scottish Open win the following month, and he anchored the European side at the 2023 Ryder Cup in Rome. The Titleist 620 CB irons have been in the bag across every snapshot since early 2024, paired with Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 shafts, and the TSR2 driver has held the same slot just as long. The putter is the moving part. MacIntyre carried a TaylorMade Spider Tour through the 2024 wins, swapped to an Odyssey Ai-ONE #7S into early 2025, then went back to a Spider, now the Tour X. The Pro V1 has been the ball since the move to Titleist.
robert-macintyre:2025-08-17.history_narrative: The 2021 and 2023 snapshots show a full TaylorMade setup, SIM2 Max driver, P7MC irons, Spider putter, TP5x ball, with a Scotty Cameron and a TSi3 briefly appearing in 2023. By February 2024 the bag had shifted to Titleist across driver, irons and ball, with the 620 CB and TSR2 locking in from that point forward. The putter has cycled between TaylorMade Spider models and Odyssey Ai-ONE shapes across 2024 and 2025, settling on the Spider Tour X in the current build.

ben-griffin:2025-11-09.lede: Ben Griffin is an American professional on the PGA Tour who took a well-documented detour into mortgage lending before returning to competitive golf and earning his card. He broke through with his first PGA Tour win at the 2025 Charles Schwab Challenge, then followed it up with a victory at the Rocket Classic weeks later, establishing himself as a multiple-time winner on Tour. The driver has not moved. Across both snapshots on file, Griffin has stayed in the PING G430 Max 10K at 9 degrees, now built with a UST Mamiya Lin-Q Powercore White V1 7 TX shaft. The iron setup has consolidated around Mizuno, with the Pro S-3 blades present in May and now running the full 4-PW set on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100, replacing the JPX 923 longer irons that filled out the earlier bag. The putter is the more recent change, a TaylorMade Spider Tour X in for the Scotty Cameron Concept 2 Tour Prototype.
ben-griffin:2025-11-09.history_narrative: Two snapshots, one driver brand throughout: PING, specifically the G430 Max 10K at 9 degrees. Mizuno irons carry across both bags, with Griffin moving from a Pro S-3 and JPX 923 combo set to a straight 4-PW run of the Pro S-3. The clearest swap is at the putter, from a Titleist Scotty Cameron Concept 2 Tour Prototype to a TaylorMade Spider Tour X, while the Maxfli Tour X ball stays in play.

sepp-straka:2025-05-11.lede: Sepp Straka is an Austrian professional on the PGA Tour, the first player from his country to win on tour and a fixture in recent Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup conversations after multiple wins, including the 2022 Honda Classic and the 2023 John Deere Classic. His résumé also includes a runner-up finish at The Open Championship and consistent top finishes in big events. The driver tells the story of the current setup: a Callaway Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond Max at 9 degrees on a Fujikura Ventus VeloCore+ Blue 6 X, a Callaway head where TaylorMade lived for years. The irons stayed in the Srixon family but moved forward to the ZXi5 long irons and ZXi7 mid-to-short irons on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100, replacing the ZX7 MKII blades that carried the bag through 2024. The Odyssey Tuttle Stroke Lab putter has not moved, and the ball is back to the Z-Star XV.
sepp-straka:2025-05-11.history_narrative: Across six snapshots, the through-lines are Srixon irons, an Odyssey Tuttle Stroke Lab putter, and a Srixon ball that has alternated between Z-Star XV and Z-Star Diamond. The driver arc runs TaylorMade to Callaway, with Stealth Plus and Stealth 2 Plus giving way to Qi10 LS in early 2024 before the move to the Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond and Triple Diamond Max heads. The iron progression goes ZX7 to ZX7 MKII and now into the ZXi5 and ZXi7 combo seen in the current bag.

siwoo-kim:2024-08-26.lede: Siwoo Kim came out of Virginia as a decorated college player and has spent his early professional career grinding through the Korn Ferry Tour, working toward a PGA Tour card. He plays a full Callaway iron set and a Callaway driver, the kind of staff bag setup that points to a deep equipment relationship rather than a piecemeal build. The headline in the current bag is the Odyssey 2-Ball Ten Broomstick, a long putter swap from the conventional-length 2-Ball Ten that ran through every prior snapshot on file. The driver has moved forward generationally inside the Triple Diamond line, Epic Speed to Rogue ST to Paradym to Paradym Ai Smoke, with a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 X handling shaft duty in the current build. The irons have evolved from a full Apex Pro '19 set into the current X Forged UT, Apex CB 4, Apex MB 5-PW combo, all on KBS Tour-V 125.
siwoo-kim:2024-08-26.history_narrative: Across five snapshots dating to January 2021, Kim has stayed entirely in Callaway on driver and iron, cycling through Epic Speed, Rogue ST, Paradym, and Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond heads. The iron build progressed from Apex Pro '19 Dot to X Forged CB, then added an X Forged UT long iron by August 2023, and arrived at the current Apex CB 4, Apex MB 5-PW split. The putter line ran Odyssey throughout, Toulon Madison in 2021 before settling into the 2-Ball Ten for three straight snapshots, then moving to the 2-Ball Ten Broomstick in the current bag.

hideki-matsuyama:2025-12-07.lede: Hideki Matsuyama turned professional in 2013 and became the first Japanese man to win a major championship at the 2021 Masters. He has collected multiple PGA Tour wins since his rookie season, including the 2024 Genesis Invitational, and represented Japan at the Tokyo and Paris Olympics. The bag tells a single-brand story on the long stuff. Srixon has been the driver across every snapshot on file, moving from the ZX5 in April 2021 to the ZX7 later that year, then the ZX5 MKII and ZX5 MKII LS through 2024, and now the ZXi LS at 9 degrees with a Graphite Design Tour AD DI 8 TX. The Z-Forged irons have been a fixture since 2021, updated to the Z-Forged II by early 2024 and still in play. Scotty Cameron has handled putter duty throughout, cycling from a Newport 2 GSS through several prototypes to the current GSS Prototype. Srixon Z-Star XV is the only ball listed across nine snapshots.
hideki-matsuyama:2025-12-07.history_narrative: Across nine snapshots dating to April 2021, Matsuyama has stayed entirely with Srixon for driver, irons, and ball, while Scotty Cameron has been the constant in the putter slot. The driver line moved ZX5 to ZX7 to ZX5 MKII to ZX5 MKII LS and now ZXi LS, and the irons stepped from Z-Forged to Z-Forged II. The putter rotated among a Newport 2 GSS and several Scotty Cameron prototypes before landing on the current GSS Prototype, with Srixon Z-Star XV holding the ball spot the entire stretch.

alex-noren:2025-06-04.lede: Alex Noren is a Swedish professional who built his résumé on the DP World Tour before taking up PGA Tour membership, with multiple European Tour wins through the mid-2010s and a Ryder Cup appearance for Europe in 2018. He has been a fixture inside the world's top tier of players for stretches of his career without yet adding a major championship. The bag tells a single-brand story. Every snapshot on file shows a Callaway driver, Callaway Apex irons, an Odyssey O-Works 1W putter, and a Callaway ball. The current build runs a Paradym Ai Smoke Max D at 9 degrees in the draw setting with a Graphite Design Tour AD VF 6 X, Apex TCB blades from 4 through 9 on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100, and a Chrome Tour ball. The Odyssey O-Works 1W has not moved across any recorded snapshot dating to 2021.
alex-noren:2025-06-04.history_narrative: Across five snapshots from 2021 forward, Noren has stayed entirely inside the Callaway and Odyssey ecosystem. The driver has cycled through the Callaway model line from Epic Max LS to Rogue ST Max LS to Paradym and now Paradym Ai Smoke Max D. The irons moved from Apex Pro to Apex TCB by mid-2023 and have held there, while the ball shifted from Chrome Soft X to Chrome Tour. The Odyssey O-Works 1W putter is the lone constant across every snapshot.

harris-english:2025-01-25.lede: Harris English is a PGA Tour veteran out of the University of Georgia with multiple Tour wins, a Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup appearance on his ledger, and a runner-up at the 2021 U.S. Open. His 2021 season included victories at the Sentry Tournament of Champions and the Travelers Championship, the latter requiring eight playoff holes against Kramer Hickok. The bag is a PING clinic from tee to green. The G430 LST sits up top with a Ventus TR Blue, replacing the G400 that anchored the 2021 snapshots, and the Blueprint T irons (4-9) now follow the G410 Crossover at the 3, an update from the standard Blueprint heads carried through 2022. The Scottsdale Hohum putter has not moved across any snapshot on file, and the Pro V1 has been the ball of record throughout. Across five snapshots, every club in the bag carries a PING headcover.
harris-english:2025-01-25.history_narrative: Across all five snapshots from January 2021 forward, English has played PING from driver through irons, with the Scottsdale Hohum putter and Titleist Pro V1 ball as constants. The driver moved from the G400 in the 2021 snapshots to the G430 LST by the end of 2022 and has held through 2025. The iron set updated from PING Blueprint to Blueprint T between the 2022 and 2024 snapshots, while the G410 Crossover 3 has stayed in the bag throughout.

patrick-reed:2025-05-14.lede: Patrick Reed is a nine-time PGA Tour winner whose résumé includes the 2018 Masters and a 3-1-2 record as a rookie at the 2014 Ryder Cup at Gleneagles. He has since moved his primary competitive base to LIV Golf, where he plays for the 4Aces GC. The driver slot tells the brand story. Reed opened 2021 with a Titleist TSi3, moved to a PXG 0811X GEN4 by January 2022, was in a PING G400 by May 2024, and is now back inside Titleist with a GT3 at 8 degrees on a Mitsubishi Tensei 1K Red 70 TX. The irons have been the constant. Grindworks PR-202 and PR-101A have anchored the set across multiple snapshots, currently a PR-202 4-iron into PR-101A 5-PW, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. Putter work has cycled through a Scotty Cameron Tour Rat and two Odyssey White Hot builds before landing on a Scotty Cameron Timeless 2.5+ Tour Prototype. Pro V1 throughout.
patrick-reed:2025-05-14.history_narrative: The driver has rotated through four brands across the four snapshots: Titleist TSi3 in 2021, PXG 0811X GEN4 in 2022, PING G400 in 2024, and now back to Titleist with the GT3. The Grindworks irons have been the through-line, with the PR-202 and PR-101A present in every snapshot since 2022 and a Grindworks prototype set listed in 2021. The putter has moved from a Scotty Cameron Tour Rat to two different Odyssey White Hot models and back to a Scotty Cameron, the Timeless 2.5+ Tour Prototype. Titleist Pro V1 is in play across all four bags.

kristoffer-reitan:2026-05-10.lede: Kristoffer Reitan is a Norwegian professional who came up through the Nordic Golf League and Challenge Tour before earning DP World Tour status. His path has been the standard European grind, stage school, Challenge Tour graduations, and the steady climb that defines most careers out of Scandinavia rather than headline amateur pedigree. The current setup leans on PING from tee through green, with a G440 Max driver at 9 degrees running a Mitsubishi Tensei 1K White 60 TX, Blueprint S blades from 4 through 9 with KBS Tour X, and a PLD Custom Ally Blue H on the greens. Blueprint S in a full 4-iron through 9-iron run is the detail worth flagging, a true muscleback set with no combo break, paired with the Tour X profile in KBS. The ball is a Pro V1. With only one snapshot on file, the bag reads as a committed PING build rather than a mixed bag stitched together from sponsor leftovers.
kristoffer-reitan:2026-05-10.history_narrative: The 2026-05-10 build is the only snapshot DORMIED has on record for Reitan, so there is no prior configuration to compare against. What stands out is the commitment to PING across driver, irons, and putter, with the Blueprint S blades running uninterrupted from 4 through 9.

akshay-bhatia:2026-03-08.lede: Akshay Bhatia turned professional in 2019 straight out of high school, skipping college to chase status through the Korn Ferry Tour. He broke through on the PGA Tour with a win at the 2023 Barracuda Championship and added the 2024 Valero Texas Open in a playoff, locking in a Masters invite the same week. The bag reads full Callaway top to bottom, anchored by a Rogue ST driver at 9 degrees on a Ventus Black 7 X, an X Forged UT at 22 degrees feeding into Apex TCB Raw blades from 5 through pitching wedge, all on KBS $-Taper 125 S+. The Odyssey Jailbird 380 has held the putter slot since early 2024, replacing the Tri-Hot 5K #7 that ran through the 2023 season. Chrome Tour has been the ball across every snapshot on file, and Callaway has been the driver brand at every checkpoint going back to 2023.
akshay-bhatia:2026-03-08.history_narrative: Every snapshot from July 2023 forward shows a Callaway driver, with the head model cycling through the Rogue ST family: base Rogue ST in 2023, Rogue ST Max in January 2024, Rogue ST Max LS in April 2024, and back to a Rogue ST at 9 degrees in the current build. The X Forged UT and Apex TCB Raw iron pairing has been untouched across all four bags. The putter is the only non-driver change on record, with the Tri-Hot 5K #7 in 2023 giving way to the Jailbird 380 by January 2024 and staying since.

tyrrell-hatton:2025-05-19.lede: Tyrrell Hatton is an English professional who turned pro in 2011 and has won on the PGA Tour, the DP World Tour, and LIV Golf, where he competes for Legion XIII. His résumé includes the 2020 Arnold Palmer Invitational, multiple BMW PGA Championship titles at Wentworth, and Ryder Cup appearances for Team Europe. The throughline in his bag is PING. Every snapshot on file, going back to 2021, shows a PING driver, PING irons, a PING Oslo-shape putter, and a Titleist Pro V1x. The current setup runs a G440 Max at nine degrees with a Ventus TR Red 6 X, a split iron set of i230 long irons into Blueprint S scoring clubs on Modus3 Tour 120 X, and the PLD Oslo Prototype that has been with him since at least 2023. The driver head has moved from G425 LST to G430 LST to G440 Max, but the architecture around it has barely shifted.
tyrrell-hatton:2025-05-19.history_narrative: Across four snapshots from 2021 to 2025, Hatton has stayed entirely in PING from tee to green, with Titleist Pro V1x as the constant ball. The driver progression tracks PING's release cadence: G425 LST in 2021, G430 LST through 2023 and 2024, then the G440 Max in 2025. Irons moved from i210 in 2021 to i230 by 2023, with a Blueprint S short-iron split added by 2024. The putter shifted from a Vault Oslo to a PLD Oslo Prototype, an Oslo head shape carried throughout.

nicolai-hojgaard:2025-04-23.lede: Nicolai Hojgaard is a Danish professional on the DP World Tour with multiple Rolex Series wins to his name, including the 2023 DP World Tour Championship in Dubai. He earned a spot on the 2023 European Ryder Cup team in Rome as a rookie, where Europe reclaimed the cup. His twin brother Rasmus plays the same circuit, and the two have been fixtures in European team golf since turning pro. The current setup runs Callaway from tee to green, anchored by the Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond at 10.5 degrees with a Mitsubishi Tensei 1K Blue 60 TX. The irons have moved from the Apex MB blades seen in early 2024 to the X Forged build with KBS $-Taper 130, a small step toward a more forgiving forged head while keeping the heavy shaft. The putter has also turned over, from the O-Works Jailbird Mini to the Odyssey Ai-ONE Milled Eight T DB. Chrome Tour X stays in play.
nicolai-hojgaard:2025-04-23.history_narrative: Across both snapshots Hojgaard has stayed entirely within the Callaway and Odyssey families, with Chrome Tour X as the constant ball. The driver lineage runs Paradym Triple Diamond into Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond, a same-line update. The bigger changes sit in the irons, Apex MB to X Forged, and at the putter, Jailbird Mini to Ai-ONE Milled Eight T DB.

kurt-kitayama:2025-07-01.lede: Kurt Kitayama is an American professional who built his early career on the Asian and European tours before earning PGA Tour status, breaking through with his maiden Tour win at the 2023 Arnold Palmer Invitational. He has represented the United States in the Walker Cup and remains a fixture in the FedEx Cup field, with multiple top-ten finishes in major championships. The current build leans Titleist at the long end, a GT3 at 11 degrees with a Graphite Design Tour AD VF 7 TX, paired with a Scotty Cameron Newport 2 Prototype on the greens. The iron stack stays TaylorMade, a P7CB 4-iron leading into P7MB blades through pitching wedge, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. Compared to the 2023 snapshot, the driver moved from a Stealth 2 Plus to the GT3, the putter swapped from a Spider X Hydro Blast to the Newport 2, and the ball changed from TaylorMade TP5x to Bridgestone Tour B XS. The TaylorMade blades stayed.
kurt-kitayama:2025-07-01.history_narrative: The two snapshots show a player who has held onto TaylorMade muscleback irons while overhauling the rest of the bag around them. In 2023 the setup was a full TaylorMade build through the driver, irons, putter and ball. By mid-2025 the driver had moved to a Titleist GT3, the putter to a Scotty Cameron Newport 2 Prototype, and the ball to Bridgestone Tour B XS, leaving the P7MB blades, now joined by a P7CB 4-iron, as the lone TaylorMade carryover.

min-woo-lee:2026-02-17.lede: Min Woo Lee is the Australian professional who broke through on the DP World Tour with the 2021 Scottish Open and added a PGA Tour victory at the 2025 Houston Open. He is a former Junior Open champion, the younger brother of major winner Minjee Lee, and has represented the International side at the Presidents Cup. The current setup leans staff-shop Callaway from tee to green: the Quantum Triple Diamond at 10.5 sits on Ventus Black 7 X, the irons run a split set of X Forged long sticks into a Forged Prototype mid-and-short package, both on Modus 125 X, and the ball remains Chrome Tour X. The driver lineage across six snapshots reads Epic Max LS, Rogue ST Triple Diamond, Paradym Triple Diamond, Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond, Elyte Triple Diamond, and now Quantum Triple Diamond. Callaway has been the driver brand at every checkpoint, and Odyssey has held the putter slot throughout.
min-woo-lee:2026-02-17.history_narrative: Across six snapshots dating back to early 2021, the driver has been Callaway at every check, moving through Epic Max LS, Rogue ST Triple Diamond, Paradym Triple Diamond, Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond, Elyte Triple Diamond, and the current Quantum Triple Diamond. The iron rotation has stayed inside the Callaway forged family, with X Forged UT and Apex variants giving way to the present X Forged plus Forged Prototype combination. Putters have been Odyssey throughout, from the O-Works 1W to the Tri-Hot 5K Double Wide, the Ai-ONE Double Wide, back to an O-Works 1W, and now an Odyssey Prototype. Chrome Soft X and Chrome Tour X have filled the ball slot wherever it was logged.

viktor-hovland:2025-03-23.lede: Viktor Hovland is a Norwegian professional on the PGA Tour, the first player from Norway to win on Tour and a multiple-time winner including the 2023 BMW Championship and the 2023 Tour Championship, where he claimed the FedEx Cup. He was the low amateur at the 2019 Masters and 2019 US Open before turning professional. The PING G425 LST driver has been in the bag across every recorded snapshot dating back to late 2020, currently built at 9 degrees set to 8.5 with a Fujikura Speeder 661 TR X shaft. The PING i210 irons are equally entrenched, anchoring the set from 4 through pitching wedge on KBS Tour-V 120 X shafts. The long-iron slot is where movement has occurred: a Callaway X Forged UT gave way to a Titleist T200, then a U-510, and now a U505 3-iron on a Graphite Design Tour AD DI Hybrid 85 X. The PLD DS 72 putter and Pro V1 ball round out a setup that has barely moved in years.
viktor-hovland:2025-03-23.history_narrative: Across ten snapshots stretching from December 2020 to March 2025, the PING G425 LST driver, PING i210 irons, PING PLD DS 72 putter, and Titleist Pro V1 ball have remained constant fixtures. The driving iron slot is the only spot with real turnover, cycling from a Callaway X Forged UT in 2020 to a Titleist T200 in 2021, then to a Titleist U-510 through 2023, and to the current Titleist U505 by early 2024. The putter line traces from a PLD Prototype 'Hovi' to the PLD DS 72 and then to the current DS 72 Prototype. Driver brand loyalty to PING is unbroken across every recorded bag.

patrick-cantlay:2025-08-25.lede: Patrick Cantlay turned pro in 2012 after a record run as the world's top-ranked amateur and 2011 Jack Nicklaus Award winner. He has compiled multiple PGA Tour wins including back-to-back Memorial titles in 2021 and 2022, captured the 2021 FedEx Cup, and was named PGA Tour Player of the Year that same season, with regular appearances on US Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup rosters. The Pro V1x has been in the bag through every snapshot on file, and the Titleist 718 AP2 irons have anchored the set the entire window. The driver line tells a different story: a Titleist TS3 ran for years before a PING G430 surfaced alongside it in the January 2023 snapshot, after which the bag returned to Titleist alone and now sits on a GT2 at 9 degrees with a Mitsubishi Diamana ZF 60 TX. The putter has stayed Scotty Cameron throughout, cycling from a GSS Prototype to the current Phantom X 7.2 Tour prototype.
patrick-cantlay:2025-08-25.history_narrative: Across all ten snapshots, Cantlay has played a Titleist Pro V1x and a Scotty Cameron putter, with the Titleist 718 AP2 irons present in every bag on file. The driver was a Titleist TS3 from January 2021 through February 2024, with a PING G430 appearing alongside it in the January 2023 snapshot, before the current bag moved to a Titleist GT2. Putter shape has progressed from a Scotty Cameron GSS Prototype to the Phantom X 5, then the Phantom X T5 Proto, and now a Phantom X 7.2 Tour prototype. A Srixon ZX5 MKII 4-iron joined the long end in the current bag, the first non-Titleist iron in the dataset.

maverick-mcnealy:2025-01-08.lede: Maverick McNealy is a Stanford product who arrived on the PGA Tour with one of the more decorated amateur résumés of his generation, sharing the Haskins Award conversation with Jon Rahm and finishing his college career tied with Tiger Woods on Stanford's all-time wins list. He broke through for his first PGA Tour victory at the 2024 RSM Classic after multiple runner-up finishes earlier in his pro career. The current setup leads with a TaylorMade Qi10 driver in the 'Dot' build at 10.5 degrees on a Graphite Design Tour AD XC 6 TX, paired with TaylorMade P7CB blades from 4 through 9 on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. That driver and iron pairing marks a full migration from the Callaway frame he carried through 2023, when the bag ran Paradym Triple Diamond up top and Apex MB through the set. The Odyssey Toulon putter family and a Titleist Pro V1x have stayed put through the brand change.
maverick-mcnealy:2025-01-08.history_narrative: The 2021 and 2022 snapshots are nearly identical: Callaway Epic Speed driver, Callaway X Forged UT paired with Nike VR Pro MB blades, and a Chrome Soft ball. By June 2023 the driver moved to Paradym Triple Diamond and the irons consolidated into Apex MB, still inside the Callaway frame. The February 2024 snapshot shows the move to TaylorMade at the driver with Qi10 and P7TW irons, and a switch to the Pro V1x. The current bag keeps the TaylorMade driver and shifts the irons to P7CB blades, while the Odyssey Toulon Stanford lineage on the putter is the one constant across all five snapshots.

keegan-bradley:2025-06-22.lede: Keegan Bradley is a PGA Tour veteran, 2011 PGA Championship winner, and the captain selected to lead the United States at the 2025 Ryder Cup at Bethpage Black. He turned pro in 2008, broke through at the Byron Nelson, and has stayed a fixture in the FedExCup conversation through wins at the BMW Championship and Travelers, with multiple Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup appearances on the résumé. The PING G430 LST up top has been the constant since late 2022, bracketed by a TaylorMade SIM stretch in 2021 and a brief TaylorMade Stealth 2 Plus look in 2023 before the PING returned and stayed. Srixon irons run the set from 3-iron through pitching wedge, currently a ZX5 MKII, ZX7 MKII, Z-Forged II combination on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100, and the Z-Star Diamond ball has been in play across every recent snapshot. The Odyssey Jailbird shape is the through line at the putter, with the Ai-ONE Cruiser back in the bag after a Versa interlude.
keegan-bradley:2025-06-22.history_narrative: The driver line moves TaylorMade SIM in 2021 to PING G430 LST in late 2022, a one-snapshot return to TaylorMade with the Stealth 2 Plus in August 2023, then back to the G430 LST from May 2024 through the current bag. Srixon irons have been the constant across all seven snapshots, evolving from the original ZX5 and ZX7 pairing into the ZX5 MKII and ZX7 MKII, with a Z-Forged II pitching wedge added by January 2025. The Z-Star Diamond ball shows up in every snapshot that records a ball since 2022. At the putter, an Odyssey Jailbird shape carries through, alternating between the Versa Jailbird and the Ai-ONE Jailbird Cruiser, which is what is in the bag now.

sam-burns:2026-04-09.lede: Sam Burns is an American professional on the PGA Tour with multiple Tour victories, a WGC Match Play title from 2023, and Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup appearances representing the United States. He played his college golf at LSU and turned pro in 2017, building a reputation as one of the stronger putters on Tour. The current setup runs Callaway from tee to green: a Quantum Triple Diamond S driver at 9 degrees with a Ventus Blue 7 TX, Apex MB blades 4-PW on Project X 6.5, an Odyssey Ai-ONE #7S, and a Chrome Tour X ball. The Apex line has been the constant across every snapshot on file, with TCB serving as the long-running iron of choice before the move back to MB. Driver has cycled through Callaway's flagship platforms across the years, and the #7-shape Odyssey has anchored the putting end the entire stretch.
sam-burns:2026-04-09.history_narrative: Across nine historical snapshots and the current bag, Burns has stayed inside the Callaway and Odyssey families end to end. Driver progression runs Mavrik to Epic Speed to Rogue ST Triple Diamond to Paradym Triple Diamond and Paradym Triple Diamond S, then to the current Quantum Triple Diamond S. Irons sat on Apex TCB from 2021 through 2025 before the current Apex MB build, and the putter line moves from Odyssey O-Works 7S through the Ai-ONE #7 variants, with the ball stepping from Chrome Soft X to Chrome Tour X.

rickie-fowler:2025-05-06.lede: Rickie Fowler turned pro in 2009 after a standout amateur career at Oklahoma State and has won six times on the PGA Tour, including the 2015 Players Championship. He represented the United States at multiple Ryder Cups and Presidents Cups, and ended a four-year winless stretch at the 2023 Rocket Mortgage Classic. The current setup leans fully into Cobra on the long end, with a DS-ADAPT X driver at 10.5 degrees on a Mitsubishi Diamana WB 73 TX and King Tour blades from 4 through pitching wedge. Cobra has been the driver brand across every snapshot on file, dating back to the King F9 Speedback in 2020. The notable shifts sit at the other ends of the bag. The putter moved from a Scotty Cameron Newport 2 prototype through a Cobra Stingray and an Odyssey Versa Jailbird before settling on the L.A.B. Golf DF3, and the ball flipped from TaylorMade TP5 variants to Titleist Pro V1 in the most recent snapshot.
rickie-fowler:2025-05-06.history_narrative: Across the ten snapshots, Cobra is the through line, supplying the driver in every bag and the irons in all but the earliest mixed sets. The putter carousel is the busiest slot, running from a Scotty Cameron Newport 2 prototype and X5 prototype, into the Cobra King Stingray-20 and Vintage Sport-45, then an Odyssey Versa Jailbird, and now the L.A.B. Golf DF3. The ball stayed in the TaylorMade TP5 family from 2020 through late 2024 before switching to Titleist Pro V1 in the current setup.

jake-knapp:2025-03-04.lede: Jake Knapp is an American professional on the PGA Tour who broke through with his maiden win at the 2024 Mexico Open at Vidanta, a result that locked in full status after years grinding through the Korn Ferry Tour and mini-tour circuits. He followed that with a 59 in the opening round of the 2025 Cognizant Classic, the 14th sub-60 round in PGA Tour history. The current bag leans heavily Texas, with a TaylorMade Qi35 up top on a Fujikura Ventus TR Black 7 X and a PXG iron set split between 0311 Gen4 X at the 4 and 0317 ST blades from 5 through pitching wedge, all built on KBS Tour C-Taper 130 X. The 2024 setup ran a PING G425 LST alongside a TaylorMade BRNR Mini, so the driver arc moves PING to TaylorMade across the two snapshots. The Pro V1 Left Dot has not moved.
jake-knapp:2025-03-04.history_narrative: Across the two snapshots, the driver brand shifts from PING G425 LST in early 2024 to TaylorMade Qi35 in 2025, with the BRNR Mini that rode shotgun in the 2024 bag no longer present. The iron setup stays in the PXG family but reshuffles, with the 0211 ST and Srixon Z U85 utility giving way to a 0311 Gen4 X long iron and 0317 ST blades. The putter moves from a TaylorMade Spider Tour Double Bend to a Scotty Cameron Phantom 9.2 Tour Prototype. The Titleist Pro V1 Left Dot is the lone constant.

shane-lowry:2026-03-01.lede: Shane Lowry is an Irish professional whose career breakthrough came as an amateur at the 2009 Irish Open, with the defining result arriving a decade later when he won the 2019 Open Championship at Royal Portrush by six strokes. He has carried multiple Ryder Cup appearances for Europe and competes across the PGA Tour and DP World Tour. The bag is a Srixon build from tee through approach, with the ZXi LS driver running a Mitsubishi Diamana D+ White 70 TX, a ZXiU 3-iron utility on Ventus VeloCore+ Blue, and a ZXi5/ZXi7 combo set on KBS Tour 130 X shafts. Every driver snapshot on file traces back to Srixon, moving from the Z 585 in 2020 through the ZX5 family and the ZXi before settling on the ZXi LS. The non-Srixon constants are the TaylorMade Spider Tour Z putter, in play since the 2025 snapshots, and the Z-Star XV ball across every entry.
shane-lowry:2026-03-01.history_narrative: Across eight snapshots from 2020 forward, every driver and iron set belongs to Srixon, moving Z 585 to ZX5 to ZX5 MKII to ZXi to the current ZXi LS, with the iron lineage shifting from Z 585/785 to ZX5/ZX7 to the present ZXi5/ZXi7 combo. The utility slot has tracked the same generational path from Z U85 to ZX U to ZX U MKII to ZXiU. The putter ran as an Odyssey 2-Ball through 2024, beginning with the Stroke Lab Exo and moving to the White Hot OG, before the TaylorMade Spider Tour Z took over by the May 2025 snapshot. The Srixon Z-Star XV ball is present in every entry.

jason-day:2025-06-11.lede: Jason Day is an Australian professional who won the 2015 PGA Championship at Whistling Straits and held the world number one ranking for 51 weeks across 2015 and 2016. He has collected more than a dozen PGA Tour titles and represented the International Team in multiple Presidents Cup appearances. The PING driver has been a constant. Every snapshot on file shows a PING head at the top of the bag, currently the G440 LST at 10.5 degrees on a Fujikura Ventus VeloCore+ Black 6 X. The iron story is less settled. Day moved off Mizuno blades after early 2021 and has cycled through TaylorMade's P-series since, P790 and P7MC in 2022, P770 and P7MC in 2023, P760 in early 2024, P7TW by late 2024, and a P790 top end with P7CB through the scoring clubs in the current build. The Bridgestone Tour B X has been the ball through every snapshot since 2022.
jason-day:2025-06-11.history_narrative: PING has held the driver slot across all seven snapshots, running G425 LST, G410 LST, G430, G430 LST, and now G440 LST. Irons shifted from a Mizuno MP-20 HMB and JPX921 Tour pairing in 2021 to a rotating series of TaylorMade P-series builds from 2022 onward. The putter moved from an Odyssey 2-Ball to a Toulon Daytona, then a Scotty Cameron TourType SSS, before settling into TaylorMade's Itsy Bitsy Spider line, Ghost in 2023 and Limited from early 2024 forward. Ball was Bridgestone Tour B XS in 2021 and Bridgestone Tour B X every snapshot since.

daniel-berger:2026-04-14.lede: Daniel Berger is a four-time PGA Tour winner whose résumé includes back-to-back Rookie titles at the FedEx St. Jude in 2016 and 2017, the 2020 Charles Schwab Challenge in a playoff over Collin Morikawa, and the 2021 AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am. He was a 2017 Presidents Cup pick for the United States and spent multiple seasons inside the top 20 in the world before a back injury cost him the better part of two years. The current setup leans PING heavy at both ends of the bag, with the G430 LST driver on a Ventus TR Black 6 X and a full set of Blueprint S blades from 4 through pitching wedge. The driver brand has flipped once across the snapshot record, TaylorMade through 2022 and PING from 2024 forward. The Pro V1 has stayed in play through every recorded bag, the one constant while the irons and putter have moved around him.
daniel-berger:2026-04-14.history_narrative: The driver arc runs TaylorMade SIM in 2021, Stealth Plus in early 2022, then PING G430 LST from January 2024 through the current bag. Irons cycled from Callaway Apex Forged and TaylorMade TP MC blends in 2021 and 2022 to a Mizuno Pro 245 and PING Blueprint S split in early 2025, with the current bag now a full Blueprint S set. The putter moved from a TaylorMade Spider Tour family through a Scotty Cameron Phantom prototype, briefly back to a TaylorMade Ghost Tour Corza in 2025, and into a PING PLD Oslo Prototype now. Titleist Pro V1, in standard or Left Dot, has been the ball in every snapshot.

wyndham-clark:2024-09-26.lede: Wyndham Clark is an American professional on the PGA Tour who broke through in 2023, winning the Wells Fargo Championship and then the U.S. Open at Los Angeles Country Club for his first major. He added the 2024 AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am to his card and has represented the United States in Ryder Cup competition. The driver line has stayed inside Titleist across every snapshot, moving from the TSi3 through to the current TSR3 at 9 degrees in a D1 SureFit setting, built with a Project X HZRDUS Smoke Green 60 6.5 TX. The iron setup is where the real movement shows. The Titleist 620 CB blades that anchored the set through 2023 and into early 2024 have given way to Titleist T100s from 4 through 9, with a Mizuno Pro Fli-Hi 2-iron riding above them. The Odyssey Jailbird putter and Pro V1x ball round out a bag that has held its core identity while quietly reshaping the scoring clubs.
wyndham-clark:2024-09-26.history_narrative: Across the five snapshots, Clark has stayed entirely within Titleist at the driver, working from the TSi3 in 2023 to the TSR3 by early 2024 and holding that platform through September. The iron blueprint evolved in stages: T200 long irons paired with 620 CB blades through most of 2023 and into January 2024, then a Mizuno Pro Fli-Hi 2-iron joining the 620 CBs by February, then a full move to T100s from 4-9 alongside the Fli-Hi by the current bag. The Jailbird shape has been a constant on the green, swapping from the Versa to the Ai-ONE version, and the Pro V1x has never left the bag.

gary-woodland:2026-03-29.lede: Gary Woodland is a PGA Tour winner with four Tour titles and a major championship at the 2019 U.S. Open at Pebble Beach, where he closed out Brooks Koepka down the stretch. He returned to competition in 2024 following surgery to remove a brain lesion, a comeback that drew widespread attention inside the locker room. The current setup leans fully into Cobra, with the OPTM MAX-K driver up top and a split iron set pairing King Tour long irons with King MB blades from 6 through pitching wedge, all on KBS Tour C-Taper 130 X. The driver lineage in the snapshot record moves PING to Callaway to Cobra, with the Cobra relationship locked in from late 2022 forward across the Aerojet, Darkspeed, DS-ADAPT and OPTM platforms. Titleist Pro V1 or Pro V1x has been in play across every snapshot on record, and Scotty Cameron has handled putter duties in six of seven.
gary-woodland:2026-03-29.history_narrative: The snapshot record opens in 2020 with a PING G410 LST driver, Wilson Staff Model blades and a Scotty Cameron Newport prototype. Callaway took over at the top of the bag in early 2022 with a Rogue ST Triple Diamond S before Cobra arrived in late 2022 and stayed, running through Aerojet LS, Darkspeed LS, DS-ADAPT X and the current OPTM MAX-K. Irons shifted from Wilson Staff blades to Cobra by 2024, with the current split of King Tour long irons and King MB scoring clubs. Titleist balls run through every snapshot, and a brief Odyssey Jailbird detour in late 2024 sits as the only break from Scotty Cameron at the putter.

michael-kim:2025-09-22.lede: Michael Kim is an American professional on the PGA Tour, best known for his eight-shot wire-to-wire victory at the 2018 John Deere Classic, his first and to date only PGA Tour title. A former Pac-12 Player of the Year at Cal and 2013 Haskins Award winner, Kim spent several seasons grinding through Korn Ferry status before re-establishing himself as a full-time Tour member. The current setup is Titleist-heavy from tee to green, built around a GT2 driver at 11 degrees with a Graphite Design Tour AD DI 6 X, an unusually high-lofted look for a player at this level. The iron stack splits a T250 4-iron into a T100 run from 5 through pitching wedge, all on Modus3 Tour 120 S, a fairly standard players-distance blend. The only non-Titleist club in play is the TaylorMade Spider 5K-ZT putter, paired with a Pro V1x.
michael-kim:2025-09-22.history_narrative: The 2025-09-22 build is the only snapshot on record for Kim in the database, so there is no movement to track yet. What stands out is the 11-degree driver loft and the T250-to-T100 combo set, both choices that lean toward launch and forgiveness rather than the lower-spin, full-blade setups common among his peers.

adam-scott:2026-04-30.lede: Adam Scott turned professional in 2000 and won the 2013 Masters, becoming the first Australian to claim a green jacket. He reached world number one in 2014 and has compiled 14 PGA Tour victories across a career stretching into a third decade, with a long-running Presidents Cup résumé for the International side. The Callaway Apex MB blades covering 5 through 10 are the headline of the current setup, paired with a Titleist T250 3-iron on a Graphite Design Tour AD VF 105 X. The Titleist GT2 driver at 9 degrees with a Mitsubishi Diamana WB 63 TX has held the slot across the most recent snapshots, and the L.A.B. MEZZ.1 Max Proto continues a putter line Scott moved to in 2022 and has not left since. The Pro V1 is in every snapshot on file going back to 2020.
adam-scott:2026-04-30.history_narrative: Across nine snapshots the Pro V1 is the only piece that never changes. The driver runs Titleist (TS4, TSi4), then a Callaway and TaylorMade stretch from 2022 through early 2024 (Rogue ST Triple Diamond S, Stealth 2 Plus, Qi10, BRNR), then back to Titleist with the GT2. The putter shifted from a Scotty Cameron Xperimental prototype to the L.A.B. MEZZ.1 family in 2022 and has stayed there through the Max Proto. Irons have rotated the most, cycling through Titleist 680/716/681, Mizuno Pro Fli-Hi, Miura AS-1, Srixon ZX MKII, and now Callaway Apex MB blades with a T250 utility on top.

corey-conners:2025-06-02.lede: Corey Conners is a Canadian PGA Tour pro out of Kent State, best known for his ball-striking and a pair of Valero Texas Open wins in 2019 and 2023. He finished runner-up at the 2014 U.S. Amateur and has represented the International side at multiple Presidents Cups. The bag tells a single-brand story. Every snapshot on file, going back to 2021, shows a PING driver, PING irons, a PING PLD putter, and a Titleist Pro V1. The current setup pairs the G440 LST with a split iron set, i230 in the long irons and Blueprint T from the 6 through pitching wedge, a combo that replaced the Blueprint S/Blueprint T split seen in late 2024. The driver has moved through the PING line over time, G400 LST to G400 to G430 LST and now G440 LST, while the PLD Prime Tyne shape has been the through-line in the putter slot since 2021, with a brief detour to an Anser 2 prototype in early 2023.
corey-conners:2025-06-02.history_narrative: Across six snapshots from 2021 to 2025, every club in the bag carries a PING stamp and every ball is a Titleist Pro V1. The driver has tracked the PING release cycle from G400 LST through G400, G430 LST, and into the current G440 LST. Irons have rotated through iBlade, i210/i59, a prototype/iBlade split, and the current i230 over Blueprint T pairing, while the PLD Prime Tyne putter shape has been the standard with a short Anser 2 prototype window in March 2023.

andrew-novak:2025-04-21.lede: Andrew Novak is an American professional on the PGA TOUR who turned pro in 2017 and worked his way up through the Korn Ferry Tour. He has posted multiple runner-up finishes at the top level, including a playoff loss at the 2024 Barracuda Championship, and represented the United States at the 2025 Zurich Classic team event. The current setup leans Srixon through the irons, with a ZX7 MKII muscleback split at the 4-6 paired to the Z-Forged II blades from 7-PW, both built on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. Off the tee, the PING G440 LST sits at a strong 7.5 degrees with a HZRDUS Smoke Green RDX 75 TX, a low-spin, low-launch combination aimed at flighting the ball down. The Odyssey Ai-ONE Milled Seven T S handles the putter slot, and Novak plays the Srixon Z-Star Diamond, keeping the ball in the same family as the irons.
andrew-novak:2025-04-21.history_narrative: The 2025-04-21 build is the only snapshot on file for Novak in the database. What stands out is the split-iron setup, ZX7 MKII long irons into Z-Forged II blades, a config more common among ball-strikers who want a touch of forgiveness only at the top of the set.

brian-harman:2025-04-06.lede: Brian Harman is a left-handed PGA Tour professional from Savannah, Georgia, who broke through at the 2023 Open Championship at Royal Liverpool, winning by six strokes for his first major title. He has multiple PGA Tour wins to his name and represented the United States at the 2023 Ryder Cup. The TSi2 driver has been the constant up top, present in every snapshot dating back to 2021, currently built at 9 degrees in a B3 SureFit setting with a Graphite Design Tour AD IZ 5 S. The iron stack stays Titleist throughout, with U-500 utility irons in the 4 and 5 slots feeding into 620 CB blades, and a T100 has been slotted in at the 6 to bridge the transition. The notable recent change sits on the green, where the long-running TaylorMade Spider OS CB has given way to the Spider 5K-ZT. Pro V1 has never left the bag.
brian-harman:2025-04-06.history_narrative: Across four snapshots from 2021 to 2025, the Titleist TSi2 driver and Pro V1 ball have been fixtures. The Titleist U-500 utility irons appear in every snapshot, with the 620 CB blades joining the build by 2022 and a T100 6-iron showing up in the current setup. The clearest move is at the putter, where the TaylorMade Spider OS CB carried through the 2021, 2022, and 2023 snapshots before being replaced by the TaylorMade Spider 5K-ZT in the current bag.

ryan-fox:2025-06-08.lede: Ryan Fox is a New Zealand professional who plays primarily on the PGA Tour and DP World Tour, with a career built on the European circuit. He won the DP World Tour's Order of Merit in 2023 after a two-win season that included the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship and the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth, and he broke through on the PGA Tour with a victory at the 2025 Myrtle Beach Classic. The bag is a Srixon build from tee to green. A ZXi driver at 10.5 degrees runs a Fujikura Ventus Black 7 TX, and the iron stack is a full Srixon progression: a ZXiU 2-iron on a graphite Ventus Black, ZXi5 long irons at the 4 and 5, and ZXi7s from the 6 through pitching wedge, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. The only non-Srixon piece in the long game is the putter, a PING PLD Anser 2D prototype, with a Z-Star XV in play.
ryan-fox:2025-06-08.history_narrative: The current build is the only snapshot on record for Fox in the database. What stands out is the commitment to a single OEM through the bag, with Srixon covering driver, irons, and ball, and only the PING PLD prototype putter sitting outside that umbrella.

nick-taylor:2025-01-12.lede: Nick Taylor is a Canadian professional on the PGA Tour whose 2023 RBC Canadian Open playoff win made him the first Canadian to take the national title in 69 years. He added the WM Phoenix Open and the Sony Open to his card over a career that now includes four PGA Tour victories. The bag underneath that résumé reads Titleist from tee to green, with a TSi3 driver at 10 degrees on a Fujikura Atmos Blue Tour Spec 6 X, T100 irons from 4 through 9 on Dynamic Gold S400, and a Pro V1x in play. The notable shift across the tracked snapshots is in the irons. Earlier bags carried a T200 and T100 combo set, and the current build moves to a straight T100 block through the long irons. The TaylorMade Spider Tour Red putter has not moved across any snapshot on file.
nick-taylor:2025-01-12.history_narrative: Across all three snapshots Taylor has stayed in a Titleist TSi3 driver, a Pro V1x ball, and a TaylorMade Spider Tour Red putter. The 2023 and 2024 bags paired Titleist T200 long irons with T100 scoring irons. The 2025 bag drops the T200s and runs T100 from 4-iron down.

max-greyserman:2024-08-11.lede: Max Greyserman is an American professional on the PGA Tour, a Northwestern product who earned his card through the Korn Ferry Tour after turning pro in 2017. The 2024 season turned him into a fixture on weekend leaderboards, with multiple runner-up finishes including the Wyndham Championship and the John Deere Classic. The bag is a full Callaway build from tee to green. The Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond Max sits at 9 degrees with a Ventus TR Black 6 X, a stiff, low-spin pairing that fits a player who launches it high and needs the front of the head to behave. The iron stack runs Apex UT at the 2, Apex Pro at the 4, and Apex TCB from 5 through pitching wedge, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. The putter is an Odyssey Triple Track Jailbird, mallet alignment for a player who lives on mid-range looks. Ball is the Chrome Soft X.
max-greyserman:2024-08-11.history_narrative: The 2024-08-11 snapshot is the only build on record for Greyserman in the database. What stands out is the wall-to-wall Callaway commitment, driver, irons, putter, and ball all under one roof, with no mixed-brand wedges or third-party shafts in the lineup outside the True Temper iron shafts and the Fujikura driver shaft.

thomas-detry:2025-02-09.lede: Thomas Detry is a Belgian professional who turned pro in 2016 after a college career at Illinois, where he was a teammate of Dylan Frittelli and an All-American. He built his resume on the DP World Tour with multiple runner-up finishes before earning PGA Tour status, and broke through with his first PGA Tour victory at the 2025 WM Phoenix Open. The current setup is Callaway from tee to green, anchored by a Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond at 9 degrees with a Mitsubishi Tensei CK Pro Blue 70 TX. The iron build is a split set, a Callaway Apex Pro 4-iron paired with Apex MB blades from the 5 through pitching wedge, all on True Temper Project X 125 6.5. The putter is an Odyssey O-Works #7 Black, a winged mallet, and the ball is a Chrome Tour X. Driver brand history on record shows Callaway throughout.
thomas-detry:2025-02-09.history_narrative: The 2025-02-09 build is the only snapshot currently on file for Detry. What stands out is the full Callaway commitment across every category, and the long-iron-blade combo with a Pro 4-iron transitioning into MB heads from the 5 down.

sungjae-im:2026-03-23.lede: Sungjae Im turned professional in 2015, won the Korn Ferry Tour points title in 2018, and was named PGA Tour Rookie of the Year in 2019. He has two PGA Tour victories, a runner-up finish at the 2020 Masters, and has represented the International Team at multiple Presidents Cups. The bag tells a single-brand story. Across six snapshots stretching back to 2020, every driver, iron set, putter, and ball logged has carried a Titleist stamp. The TSi2 driver has been in play since at least 2022, currently spec'd at 8 degrees with a Graphite Design Tour AD DI 7 X, and the T100 irons have anchored the set in every snapshot except a brief 2021 look that paired T200 long irons with T100 scoring clubs. The Scotty Cameron flatstick has cycled through Phantom and Flowback 5 variants before settling on the current F5 Tourtype SSS. Pro V1x has never left the bag.
sungjae-im:2026-03-23.history_narrative: Across six snapshots from 2020 to 2026, every club logged is Titleist. The driver moved from a TS3 in 2020 to the TSi2 by 2021 and has stayed there since. Iron setup briefly mixed T200 and T100 in 2021 before reverting to a full T100 set. Putter work has stayed inside the Scotty Cameron line, rotating from a Phantom T6 STR through Flowback 5 prototypes to the current F5 Tourtype SSS, with Pro V1x as the constant ball.

matt-wallace:2023-03-20.lede: Matt Wallace is an English professional on the PGA Tour with multiple DP World Tour titles to his name, including a 2018 BMW PGA Championship playoff win at Wentworth and a Hero Indian Open victory earlier that same season. He earned a Ryder Cup-adjacent profile through strong European campaigns and broke through stateside with a win at the 2023 Corales Puntacana Championship. The current setup runs a Titleist TSR3 driver at 9 degrees with an Aldila Rogue Black 130 MSI 60 TX shaft, a move that sits at the end of a clear driver arc from Callaway to Titleist across the logged snapshots. The Callaway X Forged CB irons carry over from the 2022 bag, shafted in Nippon Modus3 Tour 120 X, and the putter has shifted into a Scotty Cameron Circle T Prototype after Odyssey work in both prior snapshots.
matt-wallace:2023-03-20.history_narrative: The 2021 bag was full Callaway through the long game, paired with an Odyssey 2-Ball Ten. By February 2022 the driver had moved to a Callaway Rogue ST Triple Diamond and the putter to an Odyssey Toulon Memphis, with the X Forged CB and Apex MB combo in the irons. The March 2023 snapshot marks the driver brand change to Titleist via the TSR3, retains the X Forged CB irons, and swaps the Odyssey putter for a Scotty Cameron Circle T Prototype.

aldrich-potgieter:2025-06-29.lede: Aldrich Potgieter is a South African professional who turned pro in 2022 after winning the 2019 Amateur Championship at Portmarnock, becoming the youngest champion in that event's history. He earned PGA Tour status through the Korn Ferry Tour and broke through with his maiden Tour victory at the 2025 Mexico Open at VidantaWorld, a five-hole playoff that ranks among the longest sudden-death finishes of the season. The current bag is full-bag Titleist, with a GT2 at 9 degrees on a Ventus Black 8 X up top and a T-series iron build that runs T250 at the 2-iron, T150 through the 4 and 5, and T100 from the 6 down to the pitching wedge. The earlier February snapshot showed a GT3 head and a mixed T100/620 MB iron set, so the move since then has been to the lower-spinning GT2 and a more progressive cavity-blade combo. The Scotty Cameron 009M Tour Prototype has not moved.
aldrich-potgieter:2025-06-29.history_narrative: Both snapshots are Titleist across the board, so the brand story is continuity rather than a switch. The driver head changed from GT3 to GT2, and the irons shifted from a T100/620 MB combination to a three-model T250/T150/T100 progression. The 009M Tour Prototype putter carried through unchanged.

sahith-theegala:2025-02-18.lede: Sahith Theegala turned pro in 2020 after a decorated amateur career at Pepperdine, where he swept the Haskins, Nicklaus, and Ben Hogan awards in 2019. He earned his first PGA Tour victory at the 2023 Fortinet Championship and has posted multiple top-tens in major championships since reaching the Tour. The bag is a PING showcase from tee through approach. The G430 LST driver has been in play across the last three snapshots, with a G425 LST preceding it in early 2022. Irons have settled into a Blueprint S build from the 4 through PW, a tighter blade-only setup than the i210 and Blueprint mixed bags he carried through 2024. The TR 1966 Anser 2 Prototype putter has been a constant since late 2022, replacing the PLD Anser seen in the earliest snapshot, and the Pro V1 has been the ball across every snapshot on file.
sahith-theegala:2025-02-18.history_narrative: Across five snapshots, Theegala has stayed entirely in PING for driver, irons, and putter. The driver moved from G425 LST in early 2022 to G430 LST by late 2022 and has held since. Iron setups evolved from a three-model mix of i210, i59, and Blueprint in 2022 to an i210 and Blueprint S pairing through 2024, then consolidated into a full Blueprint S set by February 2025. The putter shifted from a PLD Anser to the TR 1966 Anser 2 Prototype after the first snapshot, with the Pro V1 unchanged throughout.

haotong-li:2025-07-09.lede: Haotong Li is a Chinese professional who came up through the European Tour, with wins at the 2016 Volvo China Open, the 2018 Omega Dubai Desert Classic, and the 2022 BMW International Open. He held the 54-hole lead at the 2017 Open Championship at Royal Birkdale and finished tied for third, still the best major result by a player from China. The current setup is built around a Titleist GT2 at 9 degrees with a Fujikura Ventus TR Black 7 X, a change from the TaylorMade Stealth Plus logged in the 2022 snapshot. Irons moved in the same window, from TaylorMade P7MC blades to Srixon ZXi7 shafted with Nippon Modus3 Tour 120 X. The constants across both snapshots are Odyssey on the putter and a Titleist Pro V1 in play, with the Jailbird 360 now replacing the Stroke Lab 7.
haotong-li:2025-07-09.history_narrative: Across the two snapshots on file, the driver moved from a TaylorMade Stealth Plus in 2022 to a Titleist GT2 in the current build, with irons shifting from TaylorMade P7MC to Srixon ZXi7 in the same window.
