The putter stayed Odyssey throughout, updating from a Stroke Lab 7 to a Jailbird 360. Pro V1 has been the ball in both snapshots.

alex-fitzpatrick:2026-05-11.lede: Alex Fitzpatrick is an English professional, younger brother of 2022 U.S. Open champion Matt Fitzpatrick, who turned pro in 2021 after an All-American career at Wake Forest. He earned his PGA Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour and has played his way into Tour status alongside DP World Tour starts. The driver is a PING G440 LST at 9 degrees with a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 X, a setup built for a low-spin, controlled launch off a stout tip section. The iron set runs Titleist T100 from 5 through 9 on Nippon Modus 120 X, the standard tour-player blade-adjacent profile with a heavier steel shaft. The putter is an Odyssey Ai-ONE 7S, a slant-neck fang style. Ball is Pro V1x. The only recorded brand history in the data is PING at the driver, which lines up with the current build.
alex-fitzpatrick:2026-05-11.history_narrative: The 2026-05-11 setup is the only snapshot on record for Fitzpatrick. What stands out is a multi-brand build that still leans toward tour-standard specs: PING up top, Titleist in the irons and ball, Nippon Modus 120 X through the set, and an Odyssey Ai-ONE 7S on the green.

stephan-jaeger:2025-01-12.lede: Stephan Jaeger is a German professional on the PGA Tour whose 2024 Texas Children's Houston Open win, his first on Tour, came after a long apprenticeship that included a record five Korn Ferry Tour victories and the lowest 18-hole score in PGA Tour-sanctioned history, a 58 on the developmental circuit in 2016. He turned pro in 2010 and has played out of Chattanooga for most of his American career. The G430 LST up top has been the constant, anchoring both the current setup and the March 2024 snapshot with a HZRDUS Black 60 6.5 in the build. The irons tell the real story of the year: the PING S55 blades that were in play in Houston have given way to a split Callaway Apex set, an Ai200 long iron paired with Apex CB from 4 through 9, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. The Odyssey Ai-ONE stays in the putter slot, now a #7 CH rather than the 2-Ball, and the ball moves from Pro V1 to Pro V1x.
stephan-jaeger:2025-01-12.history_narrative: Across the two snapshots the PING G430 LST driver and an Odyssey Ai-ONE putter have remained in the bag, though the putter head shape changed from a 2-Ball to a #7 CH. The clearest shift is in the irons, where the PING S55 blades from March 2024 were replaced by a Callaway Apex combo set, Ai200 in the 4 iron and Apex CB from 4 through 9. The ball also moved from Titleist Pro V1 to Pro V1x.

j-t-poston:2024-10-20.lede: J.T. Poston is a PGA Tour winner out of Western Carolina, with victories at the 2019 Wyndham Championship and the 2022 John Deere Classic, the latter closing out a bogey-free week. He has played his way onto a Presidents Cup roster and built a reputation as one of the steadier ball-strikers on Tour. The bag has been Titleist top to bottom across every snapshot on file, with a Scotty Cameron GoLo 5 the constant since 2020 and a Pro V1x in the pocket throughout. Drivers have moved through the Titleist line in sequence, from TS3 in 2020 to TSR3 by 2022 and 2024, and now the GT3 at 9 degrees with a Mitsubishi Diamana BF 60 TX. The irons tell the more interesting story: a U-500 4-iron returns to the setup in 2024 alongside T100s from 5 through 9, replacing the T100s/T100 combo that ran from 2022 through early 2024.
j-t-poston:2024-10-20.history_narrative: Every snapshot from 2020 forward shows a full Titleist setup, with the Scotty Cameron GoLo 5 Black Tour Prototype carrying since 2022 and a plain GoLo 5 before that. The driver progression tracks the company's release cycle: TS3 in 2020, TSR3 in 2022 and early 2024, GT3 in the current bag. Irons shifted from a U-500/718 AP2 build in 2020 to a T100s/T100 combo through early 2024, then back to a U-500 long iron paired with T100s in the latest snapshot.

taylor-pendrith:2024-05-05.lede: Taylor Pendrith is a Canadian professional on the PGA Tour who broke through for his first Tour victory at the 2024 CJ Cup Byron Nelson, finishing one clear of Ben Kohles after a closing 67. He came up through the Korn Ferry Tour, where he won twice in 2021 and earned his card on the back of one of the longest driving profiles on either circuit. The G430 LST sits at nine degrees with an Accra TZ Six ST in the butt, a heavier, lower-launching combination that fits a player who already carries the ball as far as Pendrith does. The irons split Srixon's ZX5 MKII in the long sticks and ZX7 MKII from the six down, all in Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100, paired with a Z-Star Diamond. The Odyssey Versa Jailbird 380 CS rounds it out, a center-shafted mallet that has become a fixture for him on the greens.
taylor-pendrith:2024-05-05.history_narrative: The May 2024 build is the only snapshot on file in the database. What stands out is the Srixon split-set construction across the irons and the Jailbird 380 CS, a putter Pendrith has leaned on through his recent results.

garrick-higgo:2025-04-24.lede: Garrick Higgo is a South African professional who came up through the Sunshine Tour and the DP World Tour, where he won three times in his first full season in 2021 and earned a PGA Tour card off the back of it. He took his maiden PGA Tour title at the Palmetto Championship that same year as a rookie and added a second at the 2024 Barracuda Championship. The current setup leads with a Titleist GT2 driver at 11 degrees, a Graphite Design Tour AD DI 7 X in the hosel, and a T200 3-iron fronting a T100 4-PW block, all on Project X 6.5. The constants across every snapshot on file are Titleist irons (T100 has been in the bag at every check-in) and a Titleist ball. The driver line has moved through TSi3, TSR4, a brief TaylorMade BRNR Mini pairing in early 2024, and back to a Titleist GT2, while the putter has settled into L.A.B. Golf after years of Scotty Cameron.
garrick-higgo:2025-04-24.history_narrative: Across five snapshots from 2021 to 2025, Titleist irons and a Titleist ball have never left the bag, with the T100 present every time. The driver progression runs Titleist TSi3 in 2021 and 2022, Titleist TSR4 in 2023, a TSR4 plus TaylorMade BRNR Mini pairing in February 2024, and a Titleist GT2 by April 2025. The putter arc moves from a Scotty Cameron Phantom X 5.5 to a Circle T 5.5 Proto, then a T5.5, before shifting to L.A.B. Golf with the DF3 in 2024 and the OZ.1 Pro in the current bag.

christiaan-bezuidenhout:2025-01-06.lede: Christiaan Bezuidenhout is a South African professional who plies his trade primarily on the PGA Tour and DP World Tour. He has won multiple times on the DP World Tour, including back-to-back victories at the Alfred Dunhill Championship and the South African Open in late 2020, and has represented the International side at the Presidents Cup. His Ryder Cup-style steadiness off the tee is built around the PXG 0311 Black Ops Tour-2 at 10.5 degrees with a Fujikura Ventus Black 2024 7 X, paired with PXG 0317 CB irons on KBS Tour 125 S+ shafts. The full PXG setup marks a clear shift from the Callaway driver and iron stack documented in earlier snapshots, with the 2024 bag still running Callaway Paradym Triple Diamond up top and X Forged UT plus Apex TCB through the bag. The Odyssey Works Big T #5 has not moved, anchoring the bag across every snapshot on file, with a Titleist Pro V1 in play.
christiaan-bezuidenhout:2025-01-06.history_narrative: The 2020 snapshot shows a full Callaway build with Epic Flash Sub Zero driver and X Forged '18 irons. By January 2024 the framework was still Callaway, updated to Paradym Triple Diamond with an X Forged UT and Apex TCB iron pairing. The current bag moves the driver and irons to PXG, with the 0311 Black Ops Tour-2 and 0317 CB. The Odyssey Works Big T #5 putter and Titleist Pro V1 are the constants across all three snapshots.

lucas-herbert:2024-05-31.lede: Lucas Herbert is an Australian professional who plays the PGA Tour, with wins at the 2020 Dubai Desert Classic on the DP World Tour, the 2021 Butterfield Bermuda Championship, and the 2023 Sanderson Farms Championship. He turned professional in 2014 and represented the International side at the 2022 Presidents Cup. The TaylorMade footprint runs deep here. Across every snapshot on file, Herbert has played a TaylorMade driver and a TaylorMade iron setup anchored by the P7TW blades, with a P790 UDI handling long iron duty through 2022 before the current bag swaps to a P770 UDI at the 4. The driver has cycled through the TaylorMade release calendar, SIM2 to Stealth Plus to the current Qi10 LS at 10.5 degrees, shafted with a Project X HZRDUS Smoke Green 70 TX. The notable departure sits on the green, where a Scotty Cameron GoLo DB5 has replaced the Spider models that ran through the earlier snapshots.
lucas-herbert:2024-05-31.history_narrative: Across all three snapshots, Herbert has stayed in TaylorMade metalwoods and irons, moving from SIM2 in 2021 to Stealth Plus in 2022 to the Qi10 LS currently. The P7TW blades have been a constant, with the long iron slot shifting from a P790 UDI to a P770 UDI in the current bag. The clearest break is at the putter, where a Spider X Tour and Spider Tour Copper have given way to a Titleist Scotty Cameron GoLo DB5.

keith-mitchell:2025-12-18.lede: Keith Mitchell is an American professional on the PGA Tour, a University of Georgia product whose breakthrough came at the 2019 Honda Classic. He has been a consistent presence in FedExCup competition since, with multiple runner-up finishes adding to the resume. The Mizuno ST-Z 230 remains in the bag at 9.5 degrees with a True Temper Project X HZRDUS T1100 75 6.5 shaft, the same head Mitchell has carried since 2023 and a continuation of an ST-Z driver line that runs through every snapshot on file. The iron setup has tightened to a single Mizuno Pro S-1 build from 4 through 9, replacing the Pro 225 and Pro 221 combo sets that defined the prior bags. The putter is back to the Scotty Cameron J.A.T. Prototype after a stint with the TaylorMade Spider Tour, and the Pro V1 has not moved in any snapshot.
keith-mitchell:2025-12-18.history_narrative: Across six snapshots from 2021 to 2025, Mizuno has been the only driver brand recorded, moving from the original ST-Z to the ST-Z 230 by 2023 and holding there. Irons stayed in the Mizuno family throughout, shifting from MP-20 to Pro 221, Pro 225 and Pro 225 KM-92 combos before consolidating into the current Pro S-1 set. The putter has alternated between Titleist Scotty Cameron models and the TaylorMade Spider Tour, with the J.A.T. Prototype the current and most recent choice. Titleist Pro V1 is the constant in every bag on record.

chris-kirk:2025-06-30.lede: Chris Kirk is a six-time PGA Tour winner out of the University of Georgia, with victories spanning the 2010 Viking Classic, the 2014 Crowne Plaza Invitational, the 2014 Deutsche Bank Championship, the 2023 Honda Classic, and the 2024 Sentry. He returned to full-time competition in 2019 after a public leave from the Tour and has been a fixture in the FedExCup Playoffs since. The driver line through the snapshot record runs entirely Callaway, from the GBB in 2021 through the Rogue ST, two generations of Paradym Triple Diamond, and the Elyte Triple Diamond seen earlier in 2025, with the bag now back on the Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond at 8.5 degrees behind a Fujikura Ventus Blue 6 TX. The iron stack has settled at Callaway Apex MB from the 5-iron down, shafted with Project X LZ 125 6.5. The putter is an Odyssey Ai-ONE #7S.
chris-kirk:2025-06-30.history_narrative: Across eight snapshots the driver has stayed Callaway end to end, moving GBB to Rogue ST Triple Diamond to Paradym Triple Diamond to Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond, with a brief stop on the Elyte Triple Diamond in January 2025 before the current Ai Smoke build. The irons shifted off Titleist in late 2022, ran a Titleist/Mizuno mixed set, then moved fully into Callaway Apex Pro and Apex MB/CB combos from early 2023, with the current bag pared down to Apex MB 5-9. Putter history rotates through Odyssey Proto, Scotty Cameron GoLo, several Odyssey models including White Hot OG #5, White Hot Versa 7, Ai-ONE Milled Six T, and Metal X Milled 9HT, landing on the Odyssey Ai-ONE #7S. Ball was Titleist Pro V1x across every snapshot that recorded one.

lucas-glover:2025-06-17.lede: Lucas Glover is a PGA Tour veteran whose résumé centers on the 2009 U.S. Open at Bethpage Black, a major title that anchors a career now stretching past two decades. He added back-to-back wins at the 2023 Wyndham Championship and FedEx St. Jude Championship, a late-career surge that returned him to the Tour Championship and the Presidents Cup conversation. The driver slot tells the recent story: a Srixon Z 785 carried him through 2023, a Titleist GT2 took over by late 2024, and the current build runs a PING G440 Max with a Fujikura Ventus Blue 7 X. The Srixon iron pairing of a ZX5 MKII long iron into ZX7 MKII mid and short irons has held since 2023, replacing an earlier Mizuno and Titleist combination. The L.A.B. MEZZ.1 Max putter and Srixon Z-Star XV ball have both been in the bag across every snapshot since 2023.
lucas-glover:2025-06-17.history_narrative: The 2020 and 2021 snapshots show a Titleist ball, Mizuno or Titleist irons, and a Scotty Cameron or Argolf putter alongside the Srixon Z 785 driver. By 2023 the bag had consolidated around Srixon ZX MKII irons, the Srixon Z-Star XV ball, and the L.A.B. MEZZ.1 Max putter, and those three pieces have stayed put since. The driver has been the moving part, tracking Srixon to Titleist to PING across the five snapshots.

tom-hoge:2024-08-05.lede: Tom Hoge is an American professional on the PGA Tour, a North Dakota State product whose breakthrough win came at the 2022 AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am. He has built a reputation as one of the better approach players on Tour, consistently ranking near the top in strokes gained on iron shots. The current bag leans hard into that identity, with Titleist 620 MB blades from 5 through 9, a T100 4-iron, and a T200 3-iron handling the long end. Driver duties moved from the TSR3 seen across the 2022 through early 2024 snapshots to a GT3 at 9 degrees with a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 X. The blades have been a fixture since the 2020 snapshot, though the surrounding cast has shifted, with 620 CBs giving way to a T100 and now a mixed long-iron setup. The TaylorMade Spider X Hydro Blast has been in the bag since late 2022, and the Pro V1 has been constant throughout.
tom-hoge:2024-08-05.history_narrative: Across six snapshots Hoge has stayed entirely in Titleist for driver and irons, cycling from TSi2 to TSi3 to TSR3 and now GT3 at the top of the bag. The 620 MB blades have been present in every snapshot, with the longer irons evolving from 620 CBs in the 2020 through 2022 bags to a T100 added in 2023, a Srixon ZX U MKII utility briefly in early 2024, and the current T200 and T100 combination. Putter history shows a TaylorMade Spider Tour, a brief Odyssey White Hot OG 2-Ball stint in early 2022, then the Spider X and Spider X Hydro Blast from late 2022 forward. The Pro V1 has not changed.

tony-finau:2026-02-23.lede: Tony Finau is a PGA Tour veteran with six Tour victories, including back-to-back wins at the 3M Open and Rocket Mortgage Classic in 2022. He has represented the United States at the Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup and has logged multiple top-10 finishes across the major championships, including a runner-up at the 2018 Masters' Augusta debut stretch and contention at the U.S. Open and Open Championship. The equipment side reads as one of the most stable on Tour. PING has held the driver slot across every recorded snapshot, moving from the G425 LST through the G430 LST and now the G440 LST at 9 degrees with a Fujikura Ventus Black VeloCore+ 7 X. The Nike Vapor Fly Pro 3-iron has survived every bag check in the data set, paired with a PING Blueprint blade run that progressed from the original Blueprint to the Blueprint S and into the current Blueprint T with KBS $-Taper 130. The Titleist Pro V1 Left Dot has been the ball of record outside two 2022 snapshots on the standard Pro V1.
tony-finau:2026-02-23.history_narrative: Across eleven snapshots, PING has owned the driver position from the G425 LST era into the G430 LST and the current G440 LST. The Nike Vapor Fly Pro 3-iron and a PING Blueprint blade set have been constants, with the blades cycling through the original Blueprint, the Blueprint S, and now the Blueprint T. The putter shifted off a Piretti Elite Prototype in early 2021 to a long PING PLD Anser 2 prototype run, then to the Scottsdale TEC Ally Blue Onset in the current bag. The Pro V1 Left Dot has been the dominant ball choice throughout.

brian-campbell:2025-07-06.lede: Brian Campbell is an American professional who came up through the Korn Ferry Tour before earning PGA Tour status, breaking through with his maiden Tour victory at the 2025 Mexico Open at VidantaWorld and following it later that season at the John Deere Classic. He spent years grinding between mini-tours, Korn Ferry stops, and Monday qualifiers before the results stuck. The current setup is PING from tee through green, with a G440 LST driver at 10.5 degrees turned down to 9.4, a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 TX up front, and a split iron build pairing a PING iDi 4-iron with Blueprint S blades from 5 through pitching wedge on KBS Tour 120 S shafts. A Redwood Anser 2 handles the putter slot and a Pro V1x is the ball. Only one snapshot is on file, so the PING-heavy lean is what the record reflects rather than a documented arc away from anything else.
brian-campbell:2025-07-06.history_narrative: The 2025-07-06 build is the only bag on record for Campbell in the database. What stands out is the full PING commitment across driver, irons, and putter, with the Blueprint S blades broken up top by an iDi utility and the Redwood Anser 2 anchoring the short stick.

emiliano-grillo:2025-04-04.lede: Emiliano Grillo is an Argentine professional who came up through the Web.com Tour, winning its 2015 money title before taking the Frys.com Open in his rookie PGA Tour season for Rookie of the Year honors. His second Tour victory came at the 2023 Charles Schwab Challenge, and he has represented Argentina at the Olympics and in the World Cup. The bag reads Callaway top to bottom, with a Callaway Elyte Triple Diamond at 9 degrees turned up to 10, a Mitsubishi Diamana BB 63 TX in the butt, and Apex TCB irons from 4 through 9 on Project X 6.5. Those Apex TCBs are the through-line: same heads, same model, present in every snapshot on file going back to 2023. The driver head has cycled through the Callaway release calendar across that stretch, Paradym Triple Diamond to Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond to the current Elyte, while the putter moved off the White Hot OG #5 into an Odyssey Ai-ONE Tuttle DB.
emiliano-grillo:2025-04-04.history_narrative: Across three snapshots from May 2023 to April 2025, Grillo has stayed entirely within Callaway and Odyssey. The Apex TCB irons are the constant. The driver has tracked Callaway's Triple Diamond line through three generations, Paradym to Paradym Ai Smoke to Elyte. The putter is the only meaningful switch in the data, an Odyssey White Hot OG #5 carrying through 2024 before the Ai-ONE Tuttle DB shows up in the current bag.

eric-cole:2024-03-21.lede: Eric Cole is an American professional who plays the PGA Tour, having earned his card through the Korn Ferry Tour. The son of LPGA winner Laura Baugh and tour veteran Bobby Cole, he posted a runner-up finish at the 2023 Honda Classic and has built a steady FedExCup presence since graduating to the main tour. The current setup leans entirely on PXG through the long game, with the 0311 Black Ops driver at 9 degrees running a True Temper Project X Even Flow Riptide LX Proto 70 shaft, and a combo iron build of the 0317 CB in the 4 and the 0317 ST through the rest of the set, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. The flatstick situation is the outlier, with two putters on record: the PXG Battle Ready II Bat Attack alongside an Odyssey O-Works 2 Ball CS. Ball is the Pro V1x.
eric-cole:2024-03-21.history_narrative: This is the only snapshot on file for Cole, captured 2024-03-21. Notable mainly for the dual-putter listing and the full PXG commitment from driver through wedges, with the Odyssey 2 Ball CS as the lone non-PXG club in the bag.

kevin-yu:2024-10-06.lede: Kevin Yu is a Taiwanese professional who played college golf at Arizona State and turned pro in 2021. He earned his PGA Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour and has built his presence on Tour with steady ball-striking and a Walker Cup pedigree from his amateur days. The current setup leans Callaway across the long end and the scoring clubs, with a Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond Max at 8.5 degrees up top and Apex TCB blades from 4 through 9. The gap to the long iron is bridged by a Srixon ZX U MKII at the 3, the lone non-Callaway club in the striking lineup. Shaft work is uniform through the irons with Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100, while the driver runs a Graphite Design Tour AD VF 6 X. Putter is an Odyssey Ai-ONE Milled Six T, ball is the Chrome Tour X.
kevin-yu:2024-10-06.history_narrative: The 2024-10-06 build is the only snapshot on file in the database. What stands out is the blended striking setup, Callaway Apex TCB blades paired with a Srixon utility at the top of the bag, all running the same Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 shaft for consistency in feel.

max-homa:2025-09-12.lede: Max Homa is a six-time PGA Tour winner and a Cal Berkeley product who took the 2013 NCAA individual title before turning pro. He represented the United States at the 2022 Presidents Cup and the 2023 Ryder Cup, with the bulk of his Tour wins coming in a four-season stretch from 2021 through 2023. The Scotty Cameron T5.5 Proto has been in the bag across every snapshot on file, dating back to a Phantom X T5.5 prototype variant in 2021, and the Pro V1 has not moved either. The rest of the bag tells a different story. Driver and irons sat under the Titleist umbrella from 2021 through August 2024, running TSi3 into TSR3 into GT3, paired with T100s and 620 MB blades. The 2025 snapshots show a full move to Cobra up front: DS-ADAPT LS to start the year, DS-ADAPT X by September, with a 3D printed long iron, King CB, and King MB blades behind it.
max-homa:2025-09-12.history_narrative: From 2021 through August 2024, Homa played Titleist drivers (TSi3, TSR3, GT3) and Titleist irons anchored by the 620 MB, with T100 and T100s filling the longer slots. The January 2025 snapshot shows Cobra in the driver and iron slots for the first time in the dataset, with the DS-ADAPT LS and LIMIT3D alongside King CB and MB blades. By September 2025 the driver has moved to the DS-ADAPT X and a Cobra 3D Printed Tour long iron replaces the LIMIT3D. The Scotty Cameron T5.5 Proto putter and the Pro V1 ball are constants across all nine snapshots.

billy-horschel:2025-10-23.lede: Billy Horschel is a seven-time PGA Tour winner whose résumé includes the 2014 FedExCup, captured by taking the BMW Championship and Tour Championship back to back. He added the 2021 WGC-Dell Technologies Match Play and the 2022 BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth, and has represented the United States in the Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup. The driver head is a Titleist GT3 at 9 degrees with a Fujikura Ventus TR Black 6 X, the latest stop on a Titleist driver lineage that runs TSi3 to TSR3 to GT3 across every snapshot on file. The irons have consolidated under the T100 banner, with a 3-iron and 5 through 9 built on True Temper Dynamic Gold 120 X100, after years of mixing 620 CB and 620 MB blades and an earlier run with PING Blueprint. The PING Sigma 2 Tyne 4 putter has been the through line, and the ball is a Pro V1x+ Prototype.
billy-horschel:2025-10-23.history_narrative: Across seven snapshots dating to 2021, the driver has stayed Titleist throughout, moving TSi3 to TSR3 to the current GT3. The iron setup has cycled through PING Blueprint in 2021, a 620 CB and 620 MB combo from 2022 into 2023, a T100 and 620 CB pairing in 2024, a T100 and 620 MB pairing in early 2025, and now a full T100 build. The PING Sigma 2 Tyne 4 has been the dominant putter, with a brief PLD Anser look in 2024, and the ball moved from Pro V1 to the Pro V1x+ Prototype.

brandt-snedeker:2025-04-25.lede: Brandt Snedeker is a nine-time PGA Tour winner whose résumé includes the 2012 FedExCup, the 2007 Rookie of the Year award, and eight Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup appearances combined. His silky tempo and one of the quickest pre-shot routines on Tour have made him one of the more recognizable putting strokes of his era. The Odyssey White Hot XG Rossie has anchored every snapshot on file, a fixed point across every other change in the bag. Up front, the driver has moved through three brands across the data set, from PING G410 Plus in 2020, to TaylorMade SIM2 Max in 2021, to the Titleist TSR2 now in play at nine degrees with a Fujikura Ventus Red 6 X. The iron stack has churned the most, cycling through Srixon Z 785, Miura CB-301, and Srixon ZX MKII before settling on the current PXG 0317 T long iron paired with Bridgestone J15CB mid and short irons on SteelFiber shafts. The ball flipped from Bridgestone Tour B X back to Titleist Pro V1x by 2024 and has stayed there.
brandt-snedeker:2025-04-25.history_narrative: Across four snapshots the Rossie putter never moves. The driver tracks PING to TaylorMade to Titleist, landing on the TSR2. Irons have been the most active slot, running Srixon Z 785, Miura CB-301, Srixon ZX MKII, and now a PXG 0317 T long iron over a Bridgestone J15CB set. The ball returned to Titleist Pro V1x by the 2024 snapshot after a Bridgestone Tour B X stretch.

taylor-moore:2023-03-19.lede: Taylor Moore is an American professional on the PGA Tour who turned pro in 2017 after a college career at Arkansas. He earned his PGA Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour and broke through with his maiden Tour win at the 2023 Valspar Championship. The bag tells a PING story end to end. The G430 LST driver sits at 10.5 degrees with a Mitsubishi Tensei 1K Blue 60 TX, a stout setup for a player who hunts shape over raw distance. The iron stack is the more telling detail: a single i230 utility at the 4, then a full set of S55s from 5 through pitching wedge, all built on True Temper Dynamic Gold Mid Tour Issue X100. The S55 was discontinued years before this snapshot, which makes the loyalty notable. A PLD Oslo 4 Prototype anchors the short stick, and the ball is a Pro V1.
taylor-moore:2023-03-19.history_narrative: Only one snapshot is on record for Moore, captured 2023-03-19. The standout element is the S55 5-PW block, a long-discontinued PING set kept in play well past its release cycle, paired with a current-generation i230 utility and a PLD prototype putter.

cameron-smith:2025-05-17.lede: Cameron Smith is an Australian professional who won the 2022 Open Championship at St Andrews and the 2022 Players Championship, and has carried multiple PGA Tour titles alongside a run of high finishes in majors. He left the PGA Tour for LIV Golf in August 2022 and captains the Ripper GC franchise. The through-line in the bag is Titleist, and it runs deep. The Scotty Cameron 009M Prototype putter and the Pro V1x ball are present in every snapshot on file, and the driver head has stayed inside the Titleist family across every check, moving from TSi3 to TSR2 to the current TSR3 at 10 degrees with a Ventus TR Blue 6 X. The iron setup has shifted around the edges, with Mizuno Pro Fli-Hi long irons sitting alongside Titleist scoring irons that have moved from T100 Black to the current T100 in the 5 through 9.
cameron-smith:2025-05-17.history_narrative: Across the seven snapshots, Titleist holds the driver, putter, and ball slots without interruption, with the 009M Prototype and Pro V1x constant from 2021 forward. The driver progression reads TSi3 in 2021 and early 2022, TSR2 by mid-2022, and TSR3 from 2023 onward. The iron mix has moved more: Titleist U-500 long irons in 2021 gave way to Mizuno Pro Fli-Hi from 2022, the scoring irons ran T100 Black through 2024 with a T200 Black cameo in 2023, and the current build pairs the Fli-Hi 2 and 3 with T100 in the 5 through 9.

joaquin-niemann:2025-05-16.lede: Joaquin Niemann turned professional in 2018 after a decorated amateur career that included a stint at world number one in the amateur ranking. The Chilean has won twice on the PGA Tour, represented the International side at the Presidents Cup, and joined LIV Golf in 2023, where he has added multiple individual victories. PING runs the bag from tee to green. The G430 LST sits in the driver slot with a Graphite Design Tour AD DI 6 X, the Blueprint S blades cover 5 through pitching wedge on Project X 6.5, and the PLD Anser Prototype putter has not moved across any of the five snapshots on file. The notable change in the irons came between 2023 and 2024, when Niemann moved out of the iBlade and into the Blueprint S. The driver progression tracks PING throughout, stepping from the G410 LST through the G430 LST. Ball of choice remains the Titleist Pro V1x.
joaquin-niemann:2025-05-16.history_narrative: Across five snapshots dating to 2021, Niemann has stayed entirely in PING for driver, irons, and putter. The PLD Anser Prototype putter is the constant, present in every bag on record. The driver moved from the G410 LST in the 2021 and 2022 snapshots to the G430 LST by 2023 and forward, and the irons shifted from the iBlade to the Blueprint S between the 2023 and 2024 snapshots, with the Titleist Pro V1x logged as the ball from 2022 on.

mackenzie-hughes:2025-03-14.lede: Mackenzie Hughes is a Canadian professional on the PGA Tour who broke through at the 2016 RSM Classic, winning in a five-man playoff in his rookie season. He has added a runner-up finish at the 2020 US Open at Winged Foot and has represented Canada at the Olympics and Presidents Cup. The bag reads like a PING catalogue. Every snapshot on file shows a PING driver and PING irons, with the S55 long irons holding a permanent seat across four-plus years of data. The current build pairs a G440 LST at 9 degrees with a Mitsubishi Diamana WB 63 TX, with the i210 handling 4-6 and the S55 picking up from 7 through pitching wedge. The Scottsdale TR Piper C putter has not moved in any snapshot logged here, and the Pro V1 has been the ball through every check-in. One OEM, one putter, one ball, going on half a decade.
mackenzie-hughes:2025-03-14.history_narrative: Across all five snapshots from February 2021 forward, Hughes has been in PING drivers and PING irons with no exceptions. The driver progressed from the G425 LST through the 2023 bag and into the current G440 LST. Iron makeup has shifted around the S55, which is the only club present in every snapshot, with the i210 in and out of the long-iron slot and a brief i500 appearance in June 2021. The Scottsdale TR Piper C putter and Pro V1 ball have been constants throughout.

lee-hodges:2023-07-30.lede: Lee Hodges is an Alabama product who turned pro in 2017 and worked his way to the PGA Tour by way of the Korn Ferry Tour, where he posted multiple top finishes in 2021 before earning his card. He has been a full PGA Tour member since the 2021-22 season, building a steady résumé without a major championship to his name yet. The bag on file is fully committed to Titleist on the clubs that matter most: a TSR2 driver at 8.0 degrees with a Fujikura Speeder 757 Evolution VI TX, a split iron set running T100s in the 4-6 and 620 CB blades in the 7-9, all on KBS Tour C-Taper 130 X. A Scotty Cameron GoLo 6 Tour Prototype handles the short stuff, with a Pro V1 in play. The split-set construction, longer irons for forgiveness, blades in the scoring clubs, is the detail worth noting.
lee-hodges:2023-07-30.history_narrative: This is the only snapshot of Hodges' bag currently on record in the database, captured 2023-07-30. What stands out is the consistency of spec across the iron set, identical KBS C-Taper 130 X shafts bridging the T100 and 620 CB heads, and a Tour Prototype GoLo 6 that points to a direct Scotty Cameron relationship rather than a retail pull.

davis-riley:2026-01-18.lede: Davis Riley is an American professional on the PGA Tour. He picked up his first individual PGA Tour win at the 2024 Charles Schwab Challenge, having previously taken the 2022 Zurich Classic of New Orleans in the team format alongside Nick Hardy. He played his college golf at Alabama and turned pro in 2019. The current setup runs full Titleist from tee to green, with a GT2 driver at 9 degrees on a Ventus Black VeloCore+ 6 X, a one-model T100 iron set from 4 through 9 on KBS Tour C-Taper 125 S+, and a Scotty Cameron Phantom 9.2R Tour Prototype on the greens. The Pro V1 has held its spot across every snapshot on file. The iron stack has narrowed from a three-model blend in 2023 and 2024 into a single T100 build, and the putter has moved from the Phantom X 7.2 prototype family into the newer 9.2R Tour Prototype shape.
davis-riley:2026-01-18.history_narrative: Across the three snapshots, the bag has been Titleist throughout, with the Pro V1 a constant. The driver moved from a TSR3 in 2023 and 2024 to the current GT2 at 9 degrees. The irons evolved from a T100, 620 CB, 620 MB combo in 2023 to a T200, T100, 620 MB mix in 2024, and have since been consolidated into a straight T100 set from 4 through 9. The putter tracked through two iterations of the Phantom X 7.2 prototype before the current Phantom 9.2R Tour Prototype.

marcus-armitage:2021-06-07.lede: Marcus Armitage is an English professional who came up through the Challenge Tour before earning his DP World Tour card, breaking through with his maiden Tour win at the 2021 Porsche European Open at Green Eagle. Known on tour as 'The Bullet,' he built his reputation on a punchy ball flight and a willingness to grind out cuts on the European circuit. The current setup leans on a Callaway Epic Speed driver at 9 degrees, shafted with a Mitsubishi Diamana TB 60 X, paired with a full set of Srixon ZX7 blades from 4-iron through pitching wedge. The short game runs through an Odyssey Works 1W putter, with a Pro V1x in play. It is a mixed-OEM bag with no single brand dominating, the kind of build common among DP World Tour players who shop by feel and fit rather than by contract. Driver history on record shows Callaway only.
marcus-armitage:2021-06-07.history_narrative: The 2021-06-07 snapshot is the only WITB on file in the database for Armitage. What stands out is the commitment to Srixon ZX7 muscleback blades across the full iron set, a player's choice that pairs cleanly with the lower-spin Epic Speed head up top.

joe-highsmith:2025-03-02.lede: Joe Highsmith is a PGA Tour pro out of Pepperdine, where he was a multi-time All-American before turning professional in 2022. He earned his Tour card through the Korn Ferry pipeline and broke through with his maiden PGA Tour victory at the 2025 Cognizant Classic, closing with a 62 to win by a stroke. The bag is Titleist top to bottom. The driver is a GT3 at 8 degrees on a Project X HZRDUS Smoke Black RDX 60 6.5, with a matching HZRDUS Smoke Black RDX 80 HY in the T200 utility 2-iron. From the 4-iron down through the 9, it is T100 on Project X LS 6.5, a forged blade-adjacent build that lines up with what most Titleist staffers in his ball-speed range are gaming. Putter is a Scotty Cameron 009M Tour Prototype, ball is a Pro V1, and there is no off-brand presence in the setup.
joe-highsmith:2025-03-02.history_narrative: The 2025-03-02 build is the only snapshot on file for Highsmith. What stands out is the full Titleist commitment from driver through ball, with the T200/T100 combo set and a 009M Tour Prototype putter pointing to standard tour-staff issue rather than anything bespoke.

adam-schenk:2025-11-16.lede: Adam Schenk is an American professional who plays the PGA Tour, having earned his card through the Korn Ferry Tour after a college career at Purdue. His best result on Tour came at the 2023 Valspar Championship, where he finished solo second, and he has logged multiple top-tens since reaching the main circuit. The driver is a PING G400 at 9 degrees, a head several model cycles behind the current release, fitted with a Fujikura Ventus Black 7 X. The irons run a split set, PING i210 long irons from 2 through 5 paired with Mizuno MP-18 SC blades from 6 through pitching wedge, both built on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. An Odyssey Tri-Hot Rossie handles the putter slot and a Pro V1 is the ball. Across the only snapshot on record, the driver brand is PING, consistent with the broader PING presence through the long irons.
adam-schenk:2025-11-16.history_narrative: The 2025-11-16 build is the only bag on file for Schenk in the database. What stands out is the age of the driver head relative to the rest of the market and the split-OEM iron setup, with PING utility-style long irons feeding into Mizuno MP-18 SC blades on the same Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 shaft.

byeong-hun-an:2024-06-04.lede: Byeong Hun An is a South Korean professional who broke through on the European Tour with a wire-to-wire win at the 2015 BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth, an eleven-shot romp that announced him as a full-field force. The former US Amateur champion (2009, the youngest winner at the time) now plies his trade primarily on the PGA Tour, with Presidents Cup appearances for the International side on his card. The current setup leans deep into Titleist, from a GT4 driver at 9 degrees in the B2 SureFit position through a blended iron stack that runs U-505 utility, T200, T150, and 620 MB blades into the short irons, all on Mitsubishi MMT and Project X 6.5 shafts. Across the three snapshots on file the driver lineage stays inside Titleist (TS3 to TSR4 to GT4), the 620 MB blades have never left the bag, and the putter rotation now carries both a L.A.B. MEZZ.1 Max and a Scotty Cameron T11 Prototype.
byeong-hun-an:2024-06-04.history_narrative: The 2020 bag ran a Titleist TS3 driver, a U-500 utility, 716 T-MB long irons into 620 MB blades, and a Scotty Cameron GSS Prototype on the greens. By January 2024 the driver had moved to TSR4, the utility updated to U-505, the long irons shifted to T200 and T150, and the putter swapped to a L.A.B. MEZZ.1, with the 620 MB blades and Pro V1x ball untouched. The current snapshot pushes the driver to GT4 and adds the Scotty Cameron T11 Prototype alongside an upgraded L.A.B. MEZZ.1 Max, keeping every iron and the ball unchanged from the prior snapshot.

austin-eckroat:2025-06-03.lede: Austin Eckroat is a PGA Tour pro out of Oklahoma State, where he was a four-time All-American before turning professional in 2021. He broke through at the 2024 Cognizant Classic for his first Tour win, then backed it up weeks later at the Mexico Open. The bag reads all PING from tee to green. The driver moved from the G430 LST seen in both 2024 snapshots to the G440 LST at 7.5 degrees, fitted with a Project X HZRDUS Smoke Green 70 6.5. The iron setup has not moved across any snapshot on file: Blueprint S in the 3-iron, Blueprint T from 4 through pitching wedge, all on Project X 6.5. The putter situation shifted earlier in 2024, with a Redwood D66 in the March snapshot giving way to a PLD DZB Custom by November, and that PLD has stayed in the bag since. Ball is Pro V1 throughout.
austin-eckroat:2025-06-03.history_narrative: Across the three snapshots on file, Eckroat has played PING shafted with Project X from driver through irons, with Titleist Pro V1 as the ball. The Blueprint S 3-iron and Blueprint T 4-PW block is unchanged across every snapshot. The putter moved from a Redwood D66 in March 2024 to a PLD DZB Custom by November 2024, and the driver stepped from G430 LST to G440 LST between the November 2024 and June 2025 snapshots.

erik-van-rooyen:2025-01-27.lede: Erik van Rooyen is a South African professional who plays primarily on the PGA Tour, with a Korn Ferry Tour title and two DP World Tour victories on his record, including the 2021 Scandinavian Mixed. He has represented South Africa at the Olympics and built a reputation as one of the more colorful dressers in the field. The Callaway Elyte driver, built at 10.5 degrees and turned down to 9.5, sits at the top of a bag that has been Callaway top to bottom across every snapshot on file. The iron stack tells the longer story: an X Forged UT utility has held the 21-degree slot through every recorded build, paired now with an Apex Pro 4-iron and Apex TCB from 5 through pitching wedge on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. The Odyssey Toulon Design San Diego putter has not moved since 2020, making it the single most durable piece in the setup.
erik-van-rooyen:2025-01-27.history_narrative: Across four snapshots dating back to 2020, the driver head has cycled through Callaway models from Epic Flash to Paradym to Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond and now Elyte, with no other brand entering the conversation. The X Forged UT utility and the Toulon San Diego putter have survived every iteration. The mid and short irons have shifted within the Callaway lineup, moving from Apex MB blades in the earlier bags to a TCB-based stack with an Apex Pro 4-iron in the current build. The ball moved from Titleist Pro V1 in 2020 to Chrome Soft X and then to the current Chrome Tour.

carlos-ortiz:2020-11-08.lede: Carlos Ortiz is a Mexican professional who turned pro in 2013 and earned his PGA Tour card through the Web.com Tour, where he won three times in 2014. He broke through on the PGA Tour at the 2020 Houston Open, becoming the first Mexican-born winner on Tour since 1978. The bag built around that win leans old-school Ping, with a G400 Max driver still in play well after newer models hit the market, paired with a Mitsubishi Tensei AV Raw 65 TX. The iron setup is a mixed set, a Titleist U-500 utility at the 3-iron slot feeding into Ping S55 blades from 4 through pitching wedge, all on Project X PXi 6.5 shafts. The putter is an Odyssey Stroke Lab JailBird Mini, the mid-mallet that quietly worked its way into a number of Tour bags through 2020. Ball is the Pro V1x.
carlos-ortiz:2020-11-08.history_narrative: The 2020-11-08 bag is the only snapshot on record for Ortiz in the database. What stands out is the commitment to a four-year-old G400 Max driver head and the split-set irons, with a Titleist utility bridging into a full run of Ping S55 blades.

seamus-power:2023-06-27.lede: Seamus Power is an Irish professional on the PGA Tour, a Walker Cup alum who represented Ireland at the 2016 Rio Olympics before breaking through with his first Tour win at the 2022 Barbasol Championship and adding a second at the 2022 Butterfield Bermuda Championship. He came up through the Korn Ferry route and has been a fixture in the FedExCup field since the breakthrough. The bag reads almost entirely PING. Driver is a G430 LST at 9 degrees on an Accra TZ6 Proto, sitting downstream of the G410 logged in 2021 and the G430 LST already in play by late 2022. The iron setup is a three-model build: an i230 utility at the 3, an iBlade at the 4, and Blueprints from 5 through pitching wedge, with the iBlade and Blueprint pairing carrying through every snapshot on record. The PLD Plus replaces the PLD 3 Mallet seen in 2022, keeping the putter inside PING's custom shop. Ball is a Pro V1x.
seamus-power:2023-06-27.history_narrative: Across all three snapshots Power has driven PING, moving from a G410 in 2021 to the G430 LST that remains in play. The iBlade and Blueprint combination has been constant since 2021, with the long-iron slot cycling from a bare iBlade to a TaylorMade P790 UDI in late 2022 and now a PING i230 utility at the 3. The putter has stayed inside PING's PLD program throughout, progressing from a PLD 3 prototype to a PLD 3 Mallet to the current PLD Plus, and the ball moved from Pro V1 to Pro V1x by the 2022 snapshot and has held there.

matt-kuchar:2023-04-03.lede: Matt Kuchar is an American PGA Tour veteran with nine Tour wins, an Olympic bronze medal from the 2016 Rio Games, and a Players Championship title from 2012. He was the 1997 U.S. Amateur champion out of Georgia Tech and has logged more than two decades of full-time Tour membership, with multiple Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup appearances on his record. The current setup runs Titleist at the top of the bag with a TSR3 driver at 9 degrees, shafted with a Fujikura Ventus TR Blue 6 X, paired with Srixon ZX7 irons on SteelFiber i110cw. That is a notable shift from the 2021 snapshot, when Kuchar was deep into a Bridgestone build with a Tour B JGR Proto driver and J15CB irons. The one constant across both snapshots is the putter brand: Bettinardi DASS, moving from the KM-1 Arm Lock in 2021 to the SS28 Tour Department in the current bag.
matt-kuchar:2023-04-03.history_narrative: Across the two snapshots on file, Kuchar's bag moved off Bridgestone at the top end and into a Titleist driver paired with Srixon irons. The 2021 build was a Bridgestone Tour B JGR Proto driver with J15CB irons and a Bridgestone Tour B X ball; the current build runs a Titleist TSR3 with Srixon ZX7s on SteelFiber shafts. Bettinardi DASS putters carry through both snapshots, with a change in model from the KM-1 Arm Lock to the SS28 Tour Department.

sergio-garcia:2024-06-12.lede: Sergio Garcia is a Spanish professional who turned pro in 1999 and won the 2017 Masters after years of near-misses in majors. He has more than 35 worldwide victories, has represented Europe in ten Ryder Cups, and now plays the LIV Golf League with Fireballs GC. The current setup leans into a long-standing TaylorMade relationship, with a Qi10 Max driver at 9 degrees on a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 X, a P770 utility 3-iron, and P7MB blades from 4 through pitching wedge, all built on LA Golf Prototype shafts. The 2023 snapshot is the outlier in the recent data, with a Titleist TSR3 in the bag alongside a mixed iron setup of TaylorMade P7MC and PING Blueprint and a Scotty Cameron TN3 on the greens. The 2024 bag returns the driver, irons, and putter to a fully non-Titleist configuration, with a Never Compromise Reserve 4 anchoring the short stick.
sergio-garcia:2024-06-12.history_narrative: Across the four snapshots, TaylorMade irons are the through-line, moving from P750 in 2021 to P730 in 2022, P7MC paired with PING Blueprint in 2023, and the current P770 utility and P7MB blade combination. The driver tracked TaylorMade from SIM to Stealth Plus before a one-snapshot detour to Titleist TSR3 in 2023 and a return to TaylorMade with the Qi10 Max. The putter rotated through Scotty Cameron Phantom X 11.5, TaylorMade Spider GT, and Scotty Cameron TN3 before landing on the Never Compromise Reserve 4 seen in the 2024 bag.

antoine-rozner:2022-07-10.lede: Antoine Rozner is a French professional on the DP World Tour with three wins on that circuit, including the 2020 Golf in Dubai Championship and the 2021 Commercial Bank Qatar Masters. He turned pro in 2014 and has represented France in amateur and professional team competition. The bag reads full Titleist through the long game: a TSi3 driver at 10 degrees with a HZRDUS Smoke Black Prototype 62 shaft, a U-500 utility at the 2, a 620 CB at the 3, and 620 MB blades from 4 through 9, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. The putter is an Odyssey Stroke Lab Ten S, mallet shape, and the ball is a Pro V1x. Compared to the 2021 snapshot, the framework holds: same driver model, same iron stack of U-500 into 620 CB into 620 MB, same Ten-shape Odyssey mallet, same ball.
antoine-rozner:2022-07-10.history_narrative: Across the two snapshots from March 2021 and July 2022, Rozner's setup is essentially static. Titleist runs the entire tee-to-green build in both bags, with the TSi3 driver, U-500 long iron, 620 CB transition iron, 620 MB scoring irons, and Pro V1x ball carrying through. The putter remains an Odyssey Ten-shape mallet across both snapshots.

victor-perez:2023-05-01.lede: Victor Perez is a French professional who came up through the Challenge Tour before breaking through on the DP World Tour with a win at the 2019 Alfred Dunhill Links Championship. He added the 2022 Abu Dhabi HSBC Championship, a Rolex Series title, earned Ryder Cup consideration, and has represented France at the Olympics. The current setup runs PING from tee to green, with a G430 LST driver built to 9.5 degrees on a Fujikura Ventus TR Blue 6 X, a i525 utility at the 3, and i59 blades from 4 through 9 on Nippon Modus3 Tour 120 TX. The Sigma 2 ZB 2 on the green is a direct continuation of the Sigma 2 ZB rolled in the 2021 snapshot, and the Pro V1 has not moved. The iron stack is where the change shows: the older iBlade and Blueprint combo has given way to the i525 and i59 pairing, but the brand on the head has not.
victor-perez:2023-05-01.history_narrative: Across both snapshots, Perez has stayed entirely in PING for the long clubs and the putter, with Titleist Pro V1 as the constant ball. The driver moved from the G425 to the G430 LST between 2021 and 2023. The iron setup shifted from an iBlade and Blueprint combo to a i525 utility and i59 blade build, and the Sigma 2 ZB putter was updated to the ZB 2 head.

joel-dahmen:2026-02-27.lede: Joel Dahmen is a PGA Tour pro from Arizona who broke through at the 2021 Corales Puntacana Championship for his first Tour win. He has played his way into multiple major championships, including a T10 at the 2022 U.S. Open at The Country Club, and built a following well beyond his ranking through the Netflix Full Swing series. The driver head is a PING G440 LST at 9 degrees with a Diamana TB 60 TX, the latest step in a PING run that stretches from the G425 LST through the G430 LST across every snapshot on file. The iron setup pairs a PXG 0317 CB 4-iron with 0211 ST from 5 through pitching wedge, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. PXG irons and the Titleist Pro V1x have anchored the bag since the Jailbird era began on the green, with the current Odyssey Ai-ONE Square 2 Square Jailbird the newest version of a mallet he has trusted for years.
joel-dahmen:2026-02-27.history_narrative: Across six snapshots the driver stays PING throughout, moving G425 LST to G430 LST to the current G440 LST. The irons shift from a PXG 0311T Gen2 set in 2021 into the 0211 ST family, with a 0317 ST long iron added by late 2023 and the current build mixing a 0317 CB 4-iron with 0211 ST mid and short irons. The putter path runs from a Scotty Cameron Roundback Prototype through two Odyssey White Hot OG models into the Jailbird family, where it has stayed. The ball is Titleist Pro V1 early, then Pro V1x from 2023 forward.

bernd-wiesberger:2025-07-10.lede: Bernd Wiesberger is an Austrian professional who has spent most of his career on the DP World Tour, where he has collected multiple wins and represented Europe at the 2021 Ryder Cup at Whistling Straits. He has posted top-ten finishes in major championships and built a reputation as one of continental Europe's most consistent ball-strikers of his generation. The current setup runs Titleist from tee to green, anchored by a GT3 driver at 9 degrees with a Graphite Design Tour AD GC 6 X and a deep mixed iron set that pairs T200 and T150 utilities with 620 CB mid-irons and 620 MB short irons, all on Modus3 Tour 120 X. The 620 CB and 620 MB blocks have carried through every snapshot on file, as has the Pro V1. Driver has cycled through the Titleist line from TS3 to TSi3 to GT3, and the Scotty Cameron prototype has moved from a T5W to a T7.2 to the current T-11.
bernd-wiesberger:2025-07-10.history_narrative: Across three snapshots dating to 2020, Wiesberger has stayed entirely within Titleist, with the 620 CB and 620 MB blade combination and the Pro V1 unchanged throughout. The driver has tracked the Titleist release cycle from TS3 in 2020 to TSi3 in 2022 to the current GT3. The long-iron slot and the Scotty Cameron prototype have both evolved over that span, moving from a U-500 utility and T5W putter to a T100s and T7.2, and now to a T200/T150 utility pairing with the T-11 Tour Prototype.

lanto-griffin:2024-02-22.lede: Lanto Griffin is a PGA Tour pro out of Virginia who broke through with a win at the 2019 Houston Open, his first Tour title after a long climb through the mini-tours and the Korn Ferry circuit. He has played his way back onto the Tour after losing most of 2022 to a back injury, with status restored through medical extension and Korn Ferry results. The bag tells a Titleist story top to bottom. Driver, irons, utility, and ball have all carried the script across every snapshot on file, with the TSR2 at 10 degrees now in the slot the 917 D2 held back in 2020. The T100 Black heads run 4 through 9 with a U-505 Black 2-iron up top, all on Modus3 130 S. The SIK Flo C-Series putter is the constant, present in 2020, gone briefly in 2022 in favor of a Scotty Cameron T7 Tour, and back in the bag since.
lanto-griffin:2024-02-22.history_narrative: Across four snapshots from 2020 to 2024, Griffin has stayed entirely in Titleist for driver, irons, utility, and ball. The driver progression runs 917 D2 to TSR2, and the long iron moved from U-510 to U-505. The only real detour is at the putter, where the SIK Flo C-Series was swapped for a Scotty Cameron T7 Tour in the 2022 snapshot before the SIK returned for 2023 and 2024.

branden-grace:2022-02-10.lede: Branden Grace is a South African professional who plays out of the LIV Golf circuit after a long run on the PGA Tour and DP World Tour. He owns multiple PGA Tour wins, a Presidents Cup résumé with the International side, and the distinction of shooting 62 in the third round of the 2017 Open Championship at Royal Birkdale, the lowest single round in men's major history. The current bag leans fully into Callaway across the long stuff and the irons, with a Rogue ST Triple Diamond LS driver at 9 degrees on a Fujikura Vista Pro 65 X and a Callaway Apex TCB set from 4 through pitching wedge built on True Temper Project X LS 125 6.5. The putter is an Odyssey Versa V-Line Prototype, keeping the flatstick under the same roof as the rest of the bag. Across the snapshots on file, every driver logged has carried a Callaway badge.
branden-grace:2022-02-10.history_narrative: Two snapshots are on record, February 2021 and February 2022, and both show a Callaway driver in play, moving from the Epic Speed Triple Diamond to the Rogue ST Triple Diamond LS. The iron setup shifted from a mixed Callaway build of Apex UT long irons and X Forged CB mid and short irons to a full Callaway Apex TCB set across 4 through pitching wedge. The putter stayed inside the Odyssey family, going from a 2-Ball Ten to a Versa V-Line Prototype.

marc-leishman:2022-03-22.lede: Marc Leishman is an Australian professional who turned pro in 2004 and has built a career primarily on the PGA Tour, with multiple Tour victories including the Arnold Palmer Invitational and the BMW Championship. He has represented the International side at the Presidents Cup on several occasions and posted a runner-up finish at the 2015 Open Championship at St Andrews, along with a share of fifth at the 2013 Masters. The bag reads Callaway top to bottom. The driver is a Rogue ST Triple Diamond LS at 10.5 degrees with a Fujikura Ventus Black 7 X, replacing the Epic Speed Triple Diamond DS seen in the 2021 snapshot. The Apex TCB irons carry over from that earlier setup, shafted in Nippon Modus3 Tour 130 X across the 3-PW. The putter moves to an Odyssey Tri-Hot 5K from the White Hot OG #1 Wide S, and the ball remains the Chrome Soft X.
marc-leishman:2022-03-22.history_narrative: Across the two snapshots on file, every category stays inside the Callaway and Odyssey umbrella. The Apex TCB irons and Chrome Soft X ball are the constants. The driver moves from the Epic Speed Triple Diamond DS in April 2021 to the Rogue ST Triple Diamond LS by March 2022, and the putter transitions from the White Hot OG #1 Wide S to the Tri-Hot 5K over the same window.

luke-clanton:2025-02-07.lede: Luke Clanton turned professional in 2025 after a decorated amateur career at Florida State, where he posted multiple top-15 finishes on the PGA Tour as an amateur, including a runner-up at the 2024 John Deere Classic. He earned PGA Tour membership through PGA Tour University Accelerated, becoming one of the first players to graduate via that pathway. The TSR2 driver runs hot at 8 degrees in the B1 SureFit setting, paired with a Mitsubishi Kai'li White 70 TX, a stiff-tipped profile that suits a player chasing a flatter launch window. The iron build is a three-model TaylorMade blend: P770 at the 3-iron for launch and forgiveness up top, P760 through the middle, and P7MB blades from 7 through 9. The full set runs Nippon Modus3 Tour 130 X. A Scotty Cameron T-9 Tour Prototype and a Pro V1 round out a bag that reads entirely Titleist on the long end and entirely TaylorMade through the irons.
luke-clanton:2025-02-07.history_narrative: The 2025-02-07 build is the only snapshot on record for Clanton, so no switches can be tracked yet. What stands out is the split-OEM construction: Titleist driver and short game, TaylorMade irons across three different models, with a single Nippon Modus3 shaft spec unifying the iron set.

thomas-pieters:2023-06-08.lede: Thomas Pieters is a Belgian professional who turned pro in 2013 and built his career on the DP World Tour, where he has collected multiple wins including the Czech Masters and the Made in Denmark. He represented Europe at the 2016 Ryder Cup at Hazeltine, posting four points as a rookie alongside Rory McIlroy, and has since moved his playing schedule to LIV Golf. The bag reads Titleist top to bottom outside the putter. A TSR2 driver at 10 degrees sits in a C2 SureFit setting with a Mitsubishi Tensei AV Raw Orange 75 TX, and the iron set runs a 620 CB/MB split, CB in the long irons (3, 4) and MB from the 5 through 9, all on Project X 6.5. The lone non-Titleist club up top is the TaylorMade Spider GT putter, a swap away from the Scotty Cameron TourType SSS SB2 logged in the prior snapshot. Pro V1 remains the ball.
thomas-pieters:2023-06-08.history_narrative: Across both snapshots Pieters has played Titleist from tee to green, with the driver moving from a TSi2 to a TSR2 as the platform generation advanced. The iron bag shifted from a T100 and 620 CB pairing to a 620 CB/MB combo set. The clearest personnel change is at the putter, where a Scotty Cameron TourType SSS SB2 gave way to a TaylorMade Spider GT, the only non-Titleist club in the current setup.

matthieu-pavon:2025-06-05.lede: Matthieu Pavon is a French professional who came up through the Challenge Tour and DP World Tour before earning PGA Tour status, where he became the first Frenchman to win on the PGA Tour in nearly century with his 2024 Farmers Insurance Open victory at Torrey Pines. That breakthrough launched him into a Masters debut and a run of contention in elite fields through 2024. The bag reads as a PING build from tee to green. The driver is a PING G440 Max at 9 degrees with a Fujikura Ventus TR Blue 6 X, an update from the PING G430 Max logged in early 2024. Irons have held steady at PING i230 from 3 through pitching wedge across both snapshots, now spec'd with Nippon Modus3 Tour 120 X. The putter moved within the PING family, from a Cadence TR Tomcat C in 2024 to a PLD DS 72 milled model in the current setup. Titleist Pro V1 has been the ball throughout.
matthieu-pavon:2025-06-05.history_narrative: Across the two snapshots, Pavon has stayed entirely in PING for the long game and short game, with the driver progressing from the G430 Max to the G440 Max and the irons remaining PING i230 throughout. The putter shifted within PING, trading the Cadence TR Tomcat C for a PLD DS 72. Titleist Pro V1 has been the constant on the ball.

cameron-davis:2025-01-20.lede: Cameron Davis is an Australian professional on the PGA Tour with two wins at the Rocket Mortgage Classic, taking the title in 2021 and again in 2024. He turned professional in 2017 after capturing the Australian Open as an amateur-era closer, and has represented Australia at the Olympics. The current bag is a full Titleist build, anchored by a GT3 driver at 9 degrees in the D4 SureFit setting with a Fujikura Ventus TR Black 7 X. The 620 CB irons from 4 through pitching wedge have been a fixture since the 2021 snapshot, paired now with a U505 driving iron in the 3 slot after earlier runs through the U-500 and T100 utility long irons. Driver has stayed Titleist across every snapshot on record, moving TSi3 to TSR3 to GT3. The Pro V1 has been in play since 2022, after a Pro V1x run in 2021. Putter remains a Scotty Cameron, currently a Newport Tour Prototype.
cameron-davis:2025-01-20.history_narrative: Across five snapshots from 2021 to 2025, the bag has stayed entirely Titleist top to bottom. Driver moved TSi3 to TSR3 to GT3, with the 620 CB blades holding their spot since 2022 after a 620 MB run in 2021. Long iron duties have rotated through U-500, T100, and now the U505, and the ball switched from Pro V1x in 2021 to Pro V1 from 2022 onward. Putter has cycled through several Scotty Cameron models, currently a Newport Tour Prototype.

francesco-molinari:2024-11-26.lede: Francesco Molinari is an Italian professional who plays the PGA Tour and DP World Tour. He won the 2018 Open Championship at Carnoustie, captured the 2018 Race to Dubai, and went 5-0-0 as a Ryder Cup player at Le National that same year, the first European to sweep all five sessions. His 2010 WGC-HSBC Champions title and multiple BMW PGA Championship wins round out a résumé built on precision iron play. Callaway has stamped the driver slot across every snapshot on file, moving from the Epic Flash Sub Zero Triple Diamond in 2020 to the Rogue ST Triple Diamond Proto in 2022, the Paradym Triple Diamond in 2023, and the current Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond at 9 degrees with a Ventus Black 6 X. The iron setup pairs a Callaway Apex Pro 4-iron with Apex TCB through the wedges, and the Odyssey Toulon Madison is back in the putter slot.
francesco-molinari:2024-11-26.history_narrative: Callaway has held the driver across all four snapshots, cycling through the Triple Diamond line from Epic Flash Sub Zero to Rogue ST Proto to Paradym and now Paradym Ai Smoke. The Apex TCB irons have been a constant since 2022, with the current build adding an Apex Pro 4-iron at the top of the set. The putter moved from a Toulon Austin Prototype in 2020 to the Tri-Hot 5K One in 2022, then settled on the Toulon Madison from 2023 forward.

abraham-ancer:2023-06-13.lede: Abraham Ancer is a Mexican professional who came up through the Web.com Tour, broke through on the PGA Tour with a win at the 2021 WGC-FedEx St. Jude Invitational, and represented the International side at the 2019 and 2021 Presidents Cups before leaving for LIV Golf in 2022, where he anchors the Fireballs GC roster. The Paradym Triple Diamond at 9 degrees, bent to 10, runs a Mitsubishi Tensei CK Pro Blue 60 TX, continuing a Callaway-only driver run across every snapshot on file. The Miura TC-201 blades have been a fixture since 2021, now built on MMT Taper Iron 105 TX shafts, and the Pro V1x has never moved. The notable wrinkle is the bag carrying two Odyssey putters, a White Hot No. 5 alongside a Tri-Hot 5K Double Wide, the latest iteration of a No. 5 shape Ancer has leaned on for years.
abraham-ancer:2023-06-13.history_narrative: Across four snapshots from April 2021 to June 2023, Callaway has been the only driver brand in the bag, moving from the Epic Speed Triple Diamond LS through a brief Rogue ST Triple Diamond LS pairing in early 2022 and into the current Paradym Triple Diamond. The Miura TC-201 irons and Titleist Pro V1x ball are present in every snapshot. The Odyssey putter line has stayed constant in family, with the White Hot No. 5 Stroke Lab giving way to a White Hot No. 5 and a Tri-Hot 5K Double Wide now sharing the bag.

nick-dunlap:2025-03-05.lede: Nick Dunlap is the Alabama product who became the first amateur to win on the PGA Tour since 1991, taking The American Express in January 2024 before turning professional days later. He added a second Tour title at the Barracuda Championship that summer, joining a short list of players to win as an amateur and a pro in the same season. The driver is the headline movement in the bag: a PING G430 LST with a Project X HZRDUS 60 TX has replaced the TaylorMade Qi10 LS he won with as an amateur, a change visible by the September 2024 snapshot and carried into 2025. Everything around it has held. The TaylorMade P7MC blades (4-9), Odyssey O-Works #7 Tank, and Titleist Pro V1 have been fixtures across every snapshot on file, and the Srixon utility iron at the top of the set has remained a Srixon build, currently the ZXiU with a Modus3 GOST X.
nick-dunlap:2025-03-05.history_narrative: Across three snapshots the bag tells a simple story: one brand swap at the top, total stability everywhere else. January 2024 had a TaylorMade Qi10 LS driver; by September 2024 that slot moved to PING G430 LST, and the 2025 build keeps the G430 LST with a Project X HZRDUS 60 TX spec on record. The P7MC irons, Srixon utility, O-Works #7 Tank, and Pro V1 have been constants throughout.

cameron-champ:2025-06-25.lede: Cameron Champ is an American professional on the PGA Tour with three Tour victories, the Sanderson Farms Championship in 2018, the Safeway Open in 2019, and the 3M Open in 2021. He arrived on Tour with one of the highest clubhead speeds in the professional game and has built his career around that distance profile. The current setup runs Titleist top to bottom in the long game, a GT2 driver at 10 degrees on a Tensei 1K Red 80 TX, a U505 utility at the 3, a T100 at the 4, and 620 MB blades from the 5 through pitching wedge. The snapshot history shows a full driver change from PING, with G425 LST and G425 Max builds through 2022 and a G430 Max 10K logged late in 2023, over to the Titleist GT2 by mid 2025. The Pro V1 ball has been in play across every snapshot dating back to late 2021.
cameron-champ:2025-06-25.history_narrative: Across the six snapshots, Champ ran PING drivers from April 2021 through December 2023, moving from the G425 LST to the G425 Max and then the G430 Max 10K. The iron stack stayed inside the PING family for that stretch as well, cycling through i210, i500, iBlade, i525, Rapture, and Blueprint S builds. The current 2025 bag marks a full move to Titleist in the driver and iron slots, paired with a TaylorMade Spider Tour X putter. The Pro V1 has been the ball in every logged bag since the Srixon Z-Star dropped out after the 2021 snapshots.

harry-higgs:2023-12-21.lede: Harry Higgs is an American professional who came up through the Korn Ferry Tour, earning his PGA Tour card after a strong 2018 season on the developmental circuit. He has contended in a major, finishing tied for fourth at the 2021 PGA Championship at Kiawah, and is known on tour for a throwback look and a willingness to talk equipment. The driver is the headline shift in his current setup: a PING G430 Max at 9 degrees with a HZRDUS T1100, ending a run of TaylorMade drivers that included the Stealth Plus in 2022 and the SIM in early 2023. The irons stayed in the TaylorMade family, now a P770 and P7MC blended set with Dynamic Gold 105 X100s, replacing the P790 long irons seen in the February 2023 bag. The Spider GT Rollback putter has been the constant through the most recent snapshots, paired with a TP5x ball.
harry-higgs:2023-12-21.history_narrative: The 2022 snapshot shows a full TaylorMade setup led by the Stealth Plus driver and a Spider Tour putter, with P770 irons in the bag. By February 2023 the putter had moved to a Spider GT Rollback and the iron set expanded into a P790, P770, P7MC blend behind a TaylorMade SIM driver. The current bag keeps the TaylorMade irons, ball and putter intact while moving the driver slot to a PING G430 Max, the only non-TaylorMade club in the setup.

will-zalatoris:2025-01-14.lede: Will Zalatoris is an American professional on the PGA Tour, known for a ball-striking profile that produced a runner-up at the 2021 Masters, a runner-up at the 2021 PGA Championship, a playoff loss at the 2022 PGA, and a runner-up at the 2022 US Open before he broke through for his first Tour win at the 2022 FedEx St. Jude Championship. Back surgery cost him much of the 2023 season. The driver head is a Titleist GT2 at 9 degrees in the A1 SureFit setting, fronting a Fujikura Ventus TR Black 7 X, and the iron set runs a three-model Titleist mix: T350 long iron, T200 utility-style 4, and T150s from 5 through pitching wedge. The L.A.B. MEZZ.1 Max has held the putter slot since the 2024 snapshots, and the Pro V1x is the current ball. Across every snapshot on file, the driver, irons, and ball have stayed inside the Titleist family.
will-zalatoris:2025-01-14.history_narrative: The driver line traces TSi3 in 2021 and early 2022, TSR3 across the 2022 and 2023 snapshots, then TSR2 in January 2024 before the move to the GT2 logged in August 2024. The iron build has steadily blended Titleist T-series models, shifting from a T100/U-500 pairing in 2021 to T100/T200 through 2023 and on to the current T150/T200/T350 mix. The putter changed from an Odyssey White Hot Pro #7 in 2021 to a Scotty Cameron Phantom X 11 prototype through 2023, with the L.A.B. MEZZ.1 Max in place by the 2024 snapshots. The ball moved from Pro V1 to Pro V1x between the August 2022 and February 2023 snapshots and has stayed there.

louis-oosthuizen:2022-02-08.lede: Louis Oosthuizen is a South African professional who won the 2010 Open Championship at St Andrews by seven shots and has since assembled one of the more decorated runner-up records in major championship golf, with second-place finishes across all four majors. He has represented the International side at multiple Presidents Cups and built his career primarily on the European Tour and PGA Tour. The current setup runs two PING drivers in the bag, a G400 at 9 degrees with a HZRDUS Smoke Blue RDX shaft alongside a G425 LST at 9 degrees shafted with Diamana D-Limited. Irons are a PING split, an i210 4-iron leading into Blueprint 5-PW, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. Two putters are listed, a PLD Anser 2 Prototype and a Vault 2.0 Voss. A Pro V1 is the ball. Across every verified snapshot, PING has been the only driver brand on record.
louis-oosthuizen:2022-02-08.history_narrative: The April 2021 and June 2021 snapshots show a settled PING build, G400 driver, Blueprint irons, PLD Voss prototype putter, Pro V1 ball. The February 2022 bag keeps the PING framework intact but expands it, adding a G425 LST alongside the G400, splitting the iron set with an i210 4-iron, and listing a PLD Anser 2 Prototype next to a Vault 2.0 Voss. PING is the only driver brand across all three snapshots.

zach-johnson:2022-03-17.lede: Zach Johnson is a two-time major champion, taking the 2007 Masters and the 2015 Open Championship at St Andrews. He has logged twelve PGA Tour wins across a career that also included a Ryder Cup captaincy at Marco Simone in 2023. The current setup is full-bag PXG, anchored by the 0811 XF Gen4 driver at 9 degrees with a Mitsubishi Kai'li 60 TX, 0311T Gen5 irons from 5 through 9 on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100, and a Proto 5.18 putter. The 2020 snapshot shows the same architecture a generation earlier: 0811 Prototype driver, 0311T Gen1 irons, a PXG prototype putter. Across both verified snapshots the ball has been the Titleist Pro V1x, and every other club in the bag has carried a PXG stamp. The progression reads as iterative within one brand rather than any meaningful equipment shift.
zach-johnson:2022-03-17.history_narrative: Two snapshots, one equipment house. The 2020 bag ran the 0811 Prototype driver, 0311T Gen1 irons, and a PXG prototype putter, and by 2022 each of those slots had moved forward a generation to the 0811 XF Gen4, 0311T Gen5, and the Proto 5.18. Titleist Pro V1x has been the ball in both snapshots. No brand changes are visible in the data, only internal model updates within PXG.

jazz-janewattananond:2022-07-05.lede: Jazz Janewattananond is a Thai professional who came up through the Asian Tour, where he has won multiple times including the 2019 SMBC Singapore Open, and has competed in major championships including the Open and the PGA Championship. He held Asian Tour Order of Merit honors in 2019 and has carried status across the Asian Tour and DP World Tour. The current setup is full Titleist at the long end and on the green: a TSR2 driver built at 8 degrees with a 0.75 degree flat lie and B1 setting, paired with a Mitsubishi Tensei CK Pro Orange 60 TX. T100s irons run 4-PW on KBS Tour-V 120 X, and the putter is a Scotty Cameron TourType SSS Circle T FB-1.5 feeding a Pro V1. The 2020 bag was a Callaway driver with Mizuno and Callaway irons, so the move since then has been a consolidation toward Titleist from driver through ball, with Scotty Cameron the throughline on the putter.
jazz-janewattananond:2022-07-05.history_narrative: The 2020 snapshot showed a mixed bag built around a Callaway Mavrik Max driver, Callaway Apex Pro UT and Mizuno JPX919 Tour irons, and a Scotty Cameron GSS Custom putter. By mid-2022 the driver had moved to a Titleist TSR2, the irons to Titleist T100s, and the ball to Pro V1, with a Scotty Cameron TourType Circle T FB-1.5 in the putter slot. The arc across these two snapshots is a shift from a multi-brand setup to a Titleist-led bag, with Scotty Cameron the consistent putter brand throughout.

adam-svensson:2024-06-28.lede: Adam Svensson is a Canadian professional who turned pro in 2015 and earned his PGA Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour, where he posted three wins in the 2018 season. His breakthrough on the PGA Tour came at the 2022 RSM Classic, his first win at golf's top level, and he has represented Canada at the Presidents Cup. The current setup leans full Callaway through the long game and irons, anchored by a Paradym Triple Diamond driver bent to 9.5 degrees with a Ventus Black 6 TX, a split iron set running an Apex 4-iron into Apex MB blades from 5 through 9. Across the two verified snapshots, the driver line has moved from Rogue ST Triple Diamond to Paradym Triple Diamond, the MB blades have stayed put, and the putter has shifted from a Toulon Palm Beach to an Odyssey Ai-ONE 2-Ball mallet.
adam-svensson:2024-06-28.history_narrative: Across both verified snapshots, Svensson has stayed inside the Callaway driver family, moving from the Rogue ST Triple Diamond in late 2022 to the Paradym Triple Diamond by mid-2024. The Apex MB blades carry through both bags, while the long-iron slot shifted from an X Forged CB to an Apex utility. The putter changed hands within Odyssey, going from the Toulon Palm Beach to the Ai-ONE 2-Ball.

dustin-johnson:2024-05-20.lede: Dustin Johnson is a two-time major champion, winning the 2016 U.S. Open at Oakmont and the 2020 Masters at Augusta National. He has spent time at world number one, captured the FedEx Cup in 2020, and joined LIV Golf in 2022 as captain of 4 Aces GC. The P730 DJ Proto blades have been the constant, present in every snapshot dating back to 2018 and forged specifically for him. The driver has moved through the TaylorMade catalogue without leaving the brand, M1 to M4 to M5 to SIM to Stealth Plus and now Qi10 at 10.5 degrees set to 12.5, paired with the Fujikura Speeder 661 Evolution 2.0 Tour Spec in X-flex. The putter has cycled through the Spider family, Juno, Tour Black, Itsy Bitsy, Splitback, GT, and now the Spider Tour T3.0. The TP5x ball has not moved since 2017.
dustin-johnson:2024-05-20.history_narrative: Across nine snapshots from 2017 to 2024, every club and the ball carry a TaylorMade stamp. The P730 DJ Proto irons have anchored the bag since 2018, replacing the Tour Preferred MB seen in 2017, with a brief P790 long-iron pairing visible in 2019. Drivers have rotated through M1, M4, M5, SIM, Stealth Plus, and Qi10. Putter changes track the Spider line, from the TP Collection Juno through Tour Black, Itsy Bitsy, Splitback, GT, and the current Spider Tour T3.0.

kevin-streelman:2024-10-09.lede: Kevin Streelman is a PGA Tour veteran who turned professional in 2001 and grinded through mini-tour and Monday qualifier circuits before earning his card. He has two PGA Tour wins, the 2013 Tampa Bay Championship and the 2014 Travelers Championship, the latter punctuated by a closing run of seven consecutive birdies that set a Tour record for a final round. The current setup runs a two-driver configuration, a Titleist GT3 at 9 degrees alongside a PING G430 LST also at 9 degrees, both built on Fujikura Ventus Black profiles. Wilson irons have been a constant through every snapshot on file, moving from the FG Tour V6 blades in 2020 to the Staff Model CB build that still anchors the set, with a Staff Model Utility 3-iron up top. The driver arc reads PING to TaylorMade to Titleist, while the Scotty Cameron TourType SSS TG6 replaced a longstanding Newport 2 somewhere after the August 2023 snapshot.
kevin-streelman:2024-10-09.history_narrative: Across four snapshots, Wilson irons and a Pro V1x have never left the bag, with the iron model progressing from the FG Tour V6 in 2020 to the Staff Model CB by 2023 and onward. The driver slot has rotated through three brands, PING G425 LST in 2020, a PING G430 LST and TaylorMade BRNR Mini pairing in 2023, a Titleist TSR3 by April 2024, and the current GT3 plus G430 LST combination. The putter shifted from a Scotty Cameron Newport 2 used through August 2023 to the TourType SSS TG6 seen in the April 2024 and current snapshots.

danny-willett:2025-01-24.lede: Danny Willett is the 2016 Masters champion, the Englishman who closed in 67 at Augusta the year Jordan Spieth gave it back on the back nine. Seven European Tour wins sit alongside that green jacket, including the 2016 DP World Tour Championship and the 2019 BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth. Willett also represented Europe at the 2016 Ryder Cup at Hazeltine. The current setup marks a full move into Cobra at the long end, with the DS-ADAPT X driver paired with a Mitsubishi Diamana GT 70 TX and a King Tec Utility plus 3D Printed Tour irons running on Modus3 Tour 120 X. That ends a long Callaway driver run visible in every prior snapshot from 2019 through September 2024, which spans the Rogue, Rogue ST Max LS, Paradym and Paradym Ai Smoke Max. The putter has also shifted, from Odyssey across all five historical bags to a Scotty Cameron T-5 Tour Prototype.
danny-willett:2025-01-24.history_narrative: Across the five historical snapshots from 2019 to September 2024, Willett carried a Callaway driver and Callaway irons in every bag, with the X Forged CB the longest-running constant. The putter was Odyssey throughout that stretch, cycling through a Stroke Lab Tuttle, a Toulon Daytona, an O-Works 1W, a Versa 1W and finally Ai-ONE and Versa Double Wide heads in 2024. The January 2025 bag breaks both patterns, moving the driver and irons to Cobra and the putter to a Scotty Cameron T-5 Tour Prototype.

dylan-frittelli:2023-04-18.lede: Dylan Frittelli is a South African professional who turned pro in 2012 after a college career at Texas, where he was part of the 2012 NCAA Championship team alongside Jordan Spieth. He won three times on the European Tour between 2017 and 2019 and claimed the John Deere Classic in 2019 for his first PGA Tour title.
