The bag has stayed inside the Callaway ecosystem across both snapshots on file, with the Paradym Triple Diamond replacing the Mavrik Sub Zero Triple Diamond at the top of the bag and a Fujikura Ventus Blue 6 TX running through it. The Apex TCB irons remain in place from 2021, now paired with a Callaway X Forged UT at 22 degrees on a Mitsubishi MMT UT 100 TX. The putter has moved from an Odyssey Stroke Lab Ten 2-Ball Triple Track to an Odyssey Toulon Le Mans tour prototype.
dylan-frittelli:2023-04-18.history_narrative: Across the two snapshots, Frittelli has remained a full Callaway and Odyssey build. The driver progressed within the Triple Diamond line from Mavrik Sub Zero to Paradym, while the Apex TCB irons and an X Forged UT long iron carried over with minor spec adjustments. The putter changed family, from a Stroke Lab Ten 2-Ball Triple Track to a Toulon Le Mans tour prototype, but stayed under the Odyssey umbrella.

webb-simpson:2024-05-07.lede: Webb Simpson is a former U.S. Open champion, winning at Olympic Club in 2012, and a seven-time PGA Tour winner whose résumé includes the 2018 Players Championship. He has represented the United States in multiple Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup appearances and built his career on a tour staff arrangement with Titleist. The driver head is a Titleist TSR3 at 10 degrees in the A1 SureFit setting, fed by a Fujikura Ventus TR Black 6 X, and the iron setup runs a split build with T150 long irons in the 5 and 6 slots flowing into 680 muscle backs from 7 through pitching wedge, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. The ball has been a Pro V1 across every snapshot on file, and the driver has stayed inside the Titleist line through the TS3, TSi3, and now TSR3 generations. The putter shifted from the Odyssey Tank Cruiser V-Line to the Ai-ONE Jailbird Cruiser.
webb-simpson:2024-05-07.history_narrative: Across the 2020, 2021, 2023, and 2024 snapshots, the driver has been Titleist throughout, moving from TS3 to TSi3 to TSR3. The irons stayed in the Titleist muscle back family, with 620 MB in 2020 and 2021, T100 paired with 682.WS in 2023, and the current T150 and 680 split build in 2024. The Pro V1 has been the ball in every snapshot, while the putter held as the Odyssey Tank Cruiser V-Line through 2023 before the change to the Odyssey Ai-ONE Jailbird Cruiser.

martin-laird:2024-05-28.lede: Martin Laird is a Scottish professional who came up through Colorado State and turned pro in 2004, building his career on the PGA Tour with three wins: the 2009 Justin Timberlake Shriners Hospitals for Children Open, the 2011 Arnold Palmer Invitational, and the 2020 Shriners Hospitals for Children Open, the last ending a nine-year victory drought. He has also represented Scotland and made appearances in major championships throughout his career. The current setup leans Srixon through the bag, with a ZX U 4-iron at 18 degrees feeding into ZX7 MKII heads from 4 through pitching wedge, all built on Project X 6.5 shafts for a uniform load across the long stuff. Up top, the driver is a TaylorMade Qi10 at 10.5 degrees with a HZRDUS Smoke Black RDX 70 6.5 TX, a move from the PING G410 LST logged in the 2020 snapshot. The Odyssey Tri-Hot 5K Two handles the putter slot.
martin-laird:2024-05-28.history_narrative: The two snapshots show a driver progression from PING G410 LST in 2020 to TaylorMade Qi10 in the current build. Srixon irons have stayed in the bag across both checks, moving from the Z 785 to the ZX7 MKII with a ZX U long iron added on top. The putter slot turned over as well, from a TaylorMade Spider Tour in 2020 to the Odyssey Tri-Hot 5K Two now.

matthew-wolff:2022-02-22.lede: Matthew Wolff turned professional in 2019 after winning the NCAA individual title at Oklahoma State, and claimed his first PGA Tour victory at the 3M Open later that summer in just his third start as a pro. He went on to finish solo fourth at the 2020 U.S. Open at Winged Foot and tied for fourth at the 2020 PGA Championship, establishing himself among the more distinctive ball strikers of his draft class. The current setup runs full TaylorMade from tee to green, headlined by a Stealth Plus driver at 9 degrees with a Graphite Design Tour AD TP 7 TX shaft. The P7MC irons (3-9) with Project X 6.5 shafts and the Spider X putter have held across every snapshot on file, with the driver progressing from M1 460 to SIM to Stealth Plus over the recorded window. The ball has cycled within the TP5 family, landing on TP5x in the current build.
matthew-wolff:2022-02-22.history_narrative: Across three snapshots dating back to April 2021, the bag has been TaylorMade throughout, with the P7MC irons and Spider X putter holding station the entire stretch. The driver progression runs M1 460 to SIM to Stealth Plus, tracking TaylorMade's own release cadence. Ball model has moved within the TP5 line, from TP5 to TP5 Pix to the current TP5x.

camilo-villegas:2023-10-27.lede: Camilo Villegas is a Colombian professional who turned pro in 2004 and has won four times on the PGA Tour, including the 2010 BMW Championship and the 2023 Butterfield Bermuda Championship, the latter coming after a deeply personal stretch following the death of his daughter Mia in 2020. He is a former Presidents Cup International team member and once ranked inside the world top ten. The current setup leans Srixon through the irons, with a Z U85 utility at the 4, ZX5 MKII at the 4 and 5, and ZX7 MKII running 6 through pitching wedge, the long irons and mid-to-short irons sharing the same Project X HZRDUS Black 6.5 80 shaft for consistency. The driver remains Titleist, a TSi3 at 11 degrees in the C1 SureFit setting with a HZRDUS Yellow 6.0. The putter is the L.A.B. MEZZ.1 Max, and the ball is a Pro V1.
camilo-villegas:2023-10-27.history_narrative: The 2023-10-27 build is the only snapshot on file for Villegas in the database. What stands out is the mixed Srixon iron stack, a utility, a player-friendly cavity, and a tour cavity all in one set, paired with a torque-balanced L.A.B. MEZZ.1 Max putter.

charley-hoffman:2026-02-06.lede: Charley Hoffman is a four-time PGA Tour winner whose career resume includes a 2016 Ryder Cup appearance for the United States and a long stretch of consistent major championship contention, most notably the opening-round 65 at the 2017 Masters that put him atop the Augusta leaderboard. He has been a fixture on Tour since the mid-2000s and serves on the Player Advisory Council. The bag reads Titleist top to bottom, and it has read that way at every snapshot on file. The T100 has anchored the iron set across four years of data, now paired with T250 long irons in a combo build rather than the blade-heavy mix of the 2020 and 2022 bags, which ran 714 MB at the bottom of the set. Driver has progressed through the Titleist line from TS3 to TSi3 to TSR2 to the current GT2 at 9 degrees. The Scotty Cameron T8 Prototype putter has been in play since at least 2024.
charley-hoffman:2026-02-06.history_narrative: Across the four snapshots, Hoffman has stayed entirely in Titleist, with the driver moving through the brand's generations from TS3 in 2020 to TSi3 in 2022, TSR2 in 2024, and the GT2 currently. The T100 iron has been a constant since 2020, joined by 714 MB long irons in the earlier bags before the switch to a T250/T100 combo by 2026. Putter shifted from a Scotty Cameron GoLo in 2020 to an F5 in 2022, then to the T8 Prototype that remains in the bag. Ball has been a Pro V1x in three of four snapshots, with a Pro V1 logged in 2022.

lee-westwood:2021-03-13.lede: Lee Westwood is an English professional who has spent decades at the top of the European game, including a stint at world number one in 2010 and Race to Dubai titles spanning multiple decades. He has logged more than 40 professional wins worldwide and remains a fixture in Ryder Cup rosters, both as a player and vice captain, though a major championship has eluded him despite numerous top-three finishes. The driver is a PING G425 LST at 10.5 degrees, set 8.75 flat, with a Mitsubishi Tensei CK Pro Orange 60 TX in the hosel, a strong-player build sitting on top of a full bag of PING i210 irons from 3 through pitching wedge on PING JZ stiff steel. The short stick is a PING Sigma 2 Fetch, the ball a Pro V1x. PING runs the engine room here, from the longest club to the flat stick.
lee-westwood:2021-03-13.history_narrative: This March 2021 setup is the only snapshot on file for Westwood in the database. What stands out is the breadth of the PING commitment, driver through putter, with the i210 long iron through pitching wedge build serving the ball-striker profile he has leaned on for years.

sebastian-j-munoz:2022-03-22.lede: Sebastian Munoz is a Colombian professional who turned pro in 2015 and earned his PGA Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour. He broke through at the 2019 Sanderson Farms Championship, beating Sungjae Im in a playoff for his first PGA Tour title, and has represented Colombia at the Olympics and the World Cup of Golf. The driver slot tells the story: PING across every snapshot on file, with the G410 LST in 2020 giving way to the G425 Max at nine degrees by March 2022, sleeved with a Project X HZRDUS Yellow 6.5. The irons follow the same script, a PING-only setup that has expanded into a layered long-game build, a G410 Crossover 2-iron and an i200 3-iron feeding into the i210s from 4-PW. The putter is the lone changeover, a Kushin 4 replacing the Sigma 2 Valor that was in play in 2020. Ball has not moved off the Pro V1.
sebastian-j-munoz:2022-03-22.history_narrative: Across both snapshots Munoz has been an all-PING setup from driver through irons, with the headline change at the top of the bag being the move from the G410 LST to the G425 Max. The iron stack grew more specialized by 2022, adding a G410 Crossover 2-iron and an i200 3-iron ahead of the i210 mid and short irons that carried over from 2020. The putter switched from a Sigma 2 Valor to a Kushin 4, while the Pro V1 ball has been a constant.

luke-list:2024-03-13.lede: Luke List is a PGA Tour professional who broke through for his first Tour title at the 2022 Farmers Insurance Open, winning a playoff at Torrey Pines after more than a decade of grinding through the Korn Ferry Tour and Tour starts as one of the longest hitters in the field. A former Vanderbilt All-American and 2004 U.S. Amateur runner-up, he built his career on driving distance and a power game that translates well on setups demanding length off the tee. The PXG 0311 ST Gen4 blades with KBS Tour V 125 shafts have anchored the bag across every recorded snapshot, paired with a Pro V1 throughout. The driver tells the brand story: a TaylorMade SIM2 in early 2022 gave way to Titleist's TSR3 by late 2023, now spec'd at 9 degrees with a Diamana DF 80 TX. The Scotty Cameron FB+ replaced an Odyssey O-Works 1W somewhere along the way, completing a steady drift toward Titleist across the bag.
luke-list:2024-03-13.history_narrative: The 2022 snapshot shows a TaylorMade SIM2 driver and Odyssey O-Works 1W putter alongside the PXG 0311 ST Gen4 irons and Pro V1. By October 2023, the driver had moved to a Titleist TSR3 and the putter to a Scotty Cameron FB+, a configuration that carries into the current March 2024 bag with the TSR3 now listed at 9 degrees with a Mitsubishi Diamana DF 80 TX. The PXG blades, KBS Tour V 125 shafts, and Pro V1 are the constants across all three snapshots, while the driver and putter both shifted into the Titleist family.

nick-hardy:2023-04-23.lede: Nick Hardy is an American professional on the PGA Tour who turned pro in 2018 after a decorated amateur career at Illinois, where he was a multiple-time All-American and Big Ten Player of the Year. He earned his PGA Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour and has built his resume on tight, ball-striking-led golf. The bag reads full Titleist from tee to green, with a TSi2 driver set at 8 degrees running an Aldila Tour Green Graphene 70 TX, a setup that skews toward lower spin and a stiffer tip than most TX 70 builds on tour. The irons are a classic better-player split, a T100 4-iron for launch and forgiveness at the top of the set, transitioning into 620 MB blades from 5 through pitching wedge, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. A Pro V1x is in play. The lone outlier is the flatstick, a Swag Golf prototype anchoring an otherwise uniform Titleist setup.
nick-hardy:2023-04-23.history_narrative: The April 2023 bag is the only snapshot on record for Hardy, so there is no historical movement to track. What stands out is the construction itself, a single-OEM build broken only by the Swag prototype putter, with a split-iron setup that pairs a T100 utility 4 with a 620 MB run through the wedge.

charl-schwartzel:2021-03-01.lede: Charl Schwartzel is a South African professional whose career peaked at the 2011 Masters, where he closed with four straight birdies to win at Augusta National. The victory came twenty years after countryman and mentor figure connections to South African major history, and Schwartzel has added multiple European Tour and Sunshine Tour titles around that win, along with a stint on LIV Golf as part of the Stinger GC roster. The current setup leans on a TaylorMade SIM2 Max driver with a Fujikura Ventus Blue shaft, a fairly standard tour pairing for that head. The iron arrangement is the more interesting read: a Honma TW 747V long iron sitting in front of a Miura MB-001 blade set from the 4-iron down, both built on True Temper Dynamic Gold 120. The putter is a PXG prototype, kept off the retail catalog. Three distinct brands across the irons and putter, with no duplication.
charl-schwartzel:2021-03-01.history_narrative: The 2021-03-01 build is the only snapshot on record for Schwartzel, so there is no switch history to track here. What stands out in that single entry is the mixed-brand iron stack, Honma at the top and Miura through the scoring clubs, rather than a single OEM set.

jason-kokrak:2021-11-14.lede: Jason Kokrak is an American professional on the PGA Tour who broke through with his first Tour victory at the 2020 CJ Cup at Shadow Creek after years of consistent earnings without a win. He followed that with back-to-back wins at the 2021 Charles Schwab Challenge and the 2021 Houston Open, establishing himself as one of the more reliable closers on Tour during that stretch. The TaylorMade SIM driver has anchored the setup across every snapshot on file, set at 9 degrees turned down to 8.5 with an Accra TZ5 85 M5 Proto shaft. The Bettinardi Studio Stock 38 putter and Titleist Pro V1 ball have been equally fixed, present in all three logged bags. The lone visible change sits in the irons, with the PXG 0311T platform carrying through from Gen2 in the 2020 snapshot to Gen4 by mid-2021, then holding into the current build with True Temper Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 shafts.
jason-kokrak:2021-11-14.history_narrative: Across the three logged snapshots, the TaylorMade SIM driver, Bettinardi Studio Stock 38 putter, and Titleist Pro V1 ball stay in the bag without interruption. The only documented movement is at the irons, where the PXG 0311T model line updates from Gen2 in October 2020 to Gen4 by May 2021 and stays there through the current bag. The brand loyalty pattern is tight, with TaylorMade on the tee, PXG in the irons, and Bettinardi on the green throughout.

peter-malnati:2024-03-24.lede: Peter Malnati is a PGA Tour veteran whose breakthrough came at the 2015 Sanderson Farms Championship, a win he waited nearly nine years to follow up before capturing the 2024 Valspar Championship. Between those titles he built a reputation as one of the tour's more candid voices, eventually taking a seat on the PGA Tour Policy Board. The bag tells a single-brand story. Every club in the 2024-03-24 snapshot carries a Titleist stamp, anchored by a TSR3 driver at 10 degrees with a Project X Denali Blue 60 TX shaft and a Scotty Cameron TourType Special Select Masterful Tour Prototype on the greens. The iron build has grown more layered over time, now running a T200 4-iron into a T150 5-iron and T100s from 6 through 9, all on AMT Tour White S400. The Pro V1x Yellow remains the ball of record.
peter-malnati:2024-03-24.history_narrative: Across all three snapshots Malnati stays inside the Titleist ecosystem from driver through putter. The 2022 bag paired a TSi3 driver with a Newport Fastback Select putter and a simpler T200/T100 iron split. By 2023 the driver had moved to TSR3 and the putter to the Scotty Cameron TourType SSS, both of which carry into the 2024-03-24 build, where the iron set expands to include a T150 5-iron between the T200 and T100 blocks.

harold-varner-iii:2022-02-06.lede: Harold Varner III is an American professional who came up through the Web.com Tour before establishing himself on the PGA Tour, with an Australian PGA Championship title in 2016 and a Saudi International win in 2022 among his notable victories. He has logged multiple top finishes on the PGA Tour without a stateside victory, and later moved to LIV Golf as part of the league's initial wave of signings. The driver tells the brand story cleanly: a TaylorMade SIM Max anchored the 2020 bag, and by February 2022 the build had shifted to a Titleist TSi3 at 10 degrees on a HZRDUS Smoke Green 6.5. Irons stayed inside Srixon across both snapshots, moving from a Z 585 and Z 945 combo into a full ZX7 set on Dynamic Gold X100. The putter changed heads within Odyssey, from a White Hot Pro Rossie to a White Hot OG 7 S, with a Pro V1x in play throughout.
harold-varner-iii:2022-02-06.history_narrative: Across the two snapshots, the driver is the only category to change brands, going from TaylorMade SIM Max in June 2020 to Titleist TSi3 by February 2022. Srixon irons and Odyssey putters held through both bags, with the iron setup tightening from a Z 585 and Z 945 mix into a single ZX7 build, and the putter moving from a White Hot Pro Rossie to a White Hot OG 7 S. Titleist Pro V1x is the ball in both snapshots.

charles-howell-iii:2021-09-20.lede: Charles Howell III turned pro in 2000 out of Oklahoma State, where he won the 2000 NCAA individual title, and has built a long PGA Tour career with three wins: the 2002 Michelob Championship at Kingsmill, the 2007 Nissan Open, and the 2018 RSM Classic. He has logged more than 20 top-ten finishes in his career and was a fixture inside the FedExCup field for nearly two decades before moving over to LIV Golf. The driver head is the only meaningful change in the recorded data, with the TSi3 from April 2021 swapped to a TSi2 at 10.0 degrees by September, tuned to 9.25 via SureFit and built around a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 X. The T100 long irons stayed put while the 620 CB blades dropped out in favor of a full T100 set through the pitching wedge on Modus3 Tour 130. The Odyssey 2-Ball also exited, replaced by a Scotty Cameron Phantom X T5.5 Prototype, keeping the bag fully Titleist from tee through green with a Pro V1.
charles-howell-iii:2021-09-20.history_narrative: Across both snapshots Howell stayed with Titleist at the driver, moving from the TSi3 in April 2021 to a TSi2 at 10.0 degrees by September. The iron setup consolidated from a T100 and 620 CB combo into a straight T100 4-PW build. The putter is the other notable swap, with the Odyssey White Hot OG 2-Ball giving way to a Scotty Cameron Phantom X T5.5 Prototype, leaving the bag entirely Titleist-family by the September snapshot.

kyounghoon-lee:2022-05-15.lede: Kyoung-Hoon Lee is a South Korean professional who reached the PGA Tour via the Korn Ferry Tour, where he posted multiple wins before earning his card. On the PGA Tour he broke through at the 2021 AT&T Byron Nelson, a result that secured his status and moved him into the world's top 100. He has also represented South Korea in international team play. The Callaway Epic Max LS at 10.5 degrees has carried over from the 2021 snapshot, anchored by a Graphite Design Tour AD DI 6 X. The iron setup remains a mixed Callaway build through the long end, with the X Forged CB 5-PW unchanged across both snapshots, though the long-iron slot has flipped from a Titleist U-500 utility to a Callaway Apex 4-iron, consolidating the set under one brand. Shafts stayed True Temper Dynamic Gold Tour Issue Mid X100. The putter changed from an Odyssey Toulon Design San Diego to an Odyssey Works Versa 2-Ball Fang, keeping him inside the Odyssey family. Ball remains Pro V1x.
kyounghoon-lee:2022-05-15.history_narrative: Across the two snapshots, the Epic Max LS driver and Pro V1x ball held. The iron build tightened under Callaway, with the Titleist U-500 utility replaced by a Callaway Apex 4-iron above the carryover X Forged CB 5-PW. The putter moved within Odyssey, from the Toulon Design San Diego to the Works Versa 2-Ball Fang.

martin-kaymer:2023-06-23.lede: Martin Kaymer is a German professional who turned pro in 2005 and reached world number one in February 2011. His major wins came at the 2010 PGA Championship at Whistling Straits and the 2014 U.S. Open at Pinehurst No. 2, where he led wire to wire. He also holed the clinching putt for Europe at the 2012 Ryder Cup at Medinah and won The Players Championship the same year as his second major. The current setup is a TaylorMade rack from tee to green minus the putter, fronted by a Stealth 2 Plus driver at 9 degrees on an Accra TZ6 Proto 65 M5 shaft. The irons are a full set of P7TW blades, 3 through 9, on Dynamic Gold AMT Tour White Tour Issue X100 shafts, a Tiger Woods signature profile Kaymer was already using in the 2020 snapshot. The putter is a PING PLD Prototype, the lone non-TaylorMade head in the bag.
martin-kaymer:2023-06-23.history_narrative: Across both snapshots, the driver head has stayed inside the TaylorMade line, moving from a SIM in 2020 to a Stealth 2 Plus in the current bag. The P7TW blades carry through both setups, with a P790 UDI filling the long-iron slot in 2020 and a 3-iron P7TW handling that role now. The putter is the only category to leave TaylorMade, shifting from a Truss TM1 to a PING PLD Prototype.

chez-reavie:2023-02-28.lede: Chez Reavie is a PGA Tour veteran whose career breakthrough came at the 2008 RBC Canadian Open, with a second win arriving more than a decade later at the 2019 Travelers Championship. Known for one of the tightest driving profiles on tour, he has built a long career on accuracy rather than distance. The current setup leans into that identity. A Titleist TSR2 at 9 degrees sits up front with a Fujikura Ventus TR Blue 6 X, a shift from the TaylorMade drivers logged in the 2020 snapshot. The irons are the more telling line item: New Level 623-CB blades from 5-PW, a small-shop OEM that rarely shows up on tour bags, shafted with True Temper Project X 125 6.5. A PING PLD Prototype handles the putting duties, replacing the Odyssey O-Works #7 from the prior snapshot, and the ball moved from Pro V1x to Pro V1.
chez-reavie:2023-02-28.history_narrative: Across the two snapshots on file, the driver brand moved from TaylorMade to Titleist, with the 2020 bag carrying both a SIM Max and an M2 before the current TSR2 took over. The irons shifted from TaylorMade P750 to New Level 623-CB, and the putter changed from an Odyssey O-Works #7 to a PING PLD Prototype. Titleist Pro V1x gave way to Pro V1 on the ball. The only constant across the two bags is the Titleist ball family.

c-t-pan:2024-07-18.lede: C.T. Pan is a Taiwanese professional who turned pro in 2015 after a decorated amateur career at the University of Washington, where he reached world number one in the amateur ranking. He broke through on the PGA Tour at the 2019 RBC Heritage and earned a bronze medal for Chinese Taipei at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics following a seven-for-one playoff. The current setup is full Titleist from tee to green, anchored by a GT2 driver at 9 degrees in the A1 SureFit setting with a Ventus Red 6 X. The iron build runs a U-505 utility at the top, a single T200 4-iron as a transition piece, then T150s from 5 through 9, all on KBS PGI 90 graphite shafts. A Scotty Cameron TourType SSS in the TG6.5 head and a Pro V1x round it out. The brand picture is uncomplicated: Titleist throughout the snapshot record.
c-t-pan:2024-07-18.history_narrative: The 2024-07-18 build is the only snapshot on file for Pan in the database. What stands out is the graphite KBS PGI 90 running through the entire iron set, paired with a steel HZRDUS Smoke Red shaft in the U-505 driving iron.

bubba-watson:2023-09-08.lede: Bubba Watson is a two-time Masters champion, winning at Augusta National in 2012 and 2014, and a twelve-time PGA Tour winner known for one of the most pronounced left-handed draws and fades in the modern game. He represented the United States in multiple Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup teams before moving to LIV Golf in 2022, where he captains Range Goats GC. The current bag is PING from tee to green outside the ball, with a G430 LST driver built to 9 degrees with the 17g CG shifter in neutral, Blueprint S blades 3 through PW on Dynamic Gold X100, and a PLD Custom Anser D putter. The shift from S55 to Blueprint S is the only meaningful change in the iron slot across the three snapshots on file. Driver has tracked the PING release cycle, G425 LST in 2021 and 2022 into the G430 LST for 2023, and the Pro V1x has been the ball throughout, with a yellow run in 2021.
bubba-watson:2023-09-08.history_narrative: Across the three snapshots, every club slot stays inside PING. Driver moves with the release cycle, G425 LST in February 2021 and April 2022, then G430 LST by September 2023. Irons step from the S55 used in 2021 and 2022 to the Blueprint S blades currently in play, and the putter transitions from a PLD Anser Prototype to the PLD Custom Anser D. The ball is Titleist Pro V1x throughout, logged in yellow in the 2021 snapshot.

chesson-hadley:2024-03-28.lede: Chesson Hadley is a PGA Tour veteran out of Raleigh, North Carolina, who broke through with a win at the 2014 Puerto Rico Open as a rookie and claimed Tour Rookie of the Year honors that same season. He earned a return to the PGA Tour through the Korn Ferry Tour Finals and has remained a fixture across both circuits, with multiple Korn Ferry wins padding the resume. The TSR3 driver at 10 degrees runs a Mitsubishi Diamana D+ 70 TX, a heavier, low-launch profile that pairs with the D1 SureFit setting. Irons split the standard Titleist combo: a T200 utility 3, 620 CB long irons in the 4 and 5, and 620 MB blades from 6 through pitching wedge, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 outside the Tour AD DI 105 X in the driving iron. Across the two snapshots on file, the driver has stayed Titleist, the blades have stayed 620 MB, and the Odyssey White Hot OG 2-Ball and Pro V1x have not moved.
chesson-hadley:2024-03-28.history_narrative: Two snapshots, 2021 and 2024, both show Titleist at the top of the bag and Titleist 620 MB blades in the iron set. The Odyssey White Hot OG 2-Ball putter and Pro V1x ball carry through both checks unchanged. The visible movement is the driver head update from TSi3 to TSR3 and the addition of a T200 utility and 620 CB long irons alongside the MB blades, with no brand changes across the data.

kevin-kisner:2025-02-06.lede: Kevin Kisner is a four-time PGA Tour winner whose résumé includes the 2021 Wyndham Championship and a runner-up finish at the 2018 Open Championship at Carnoustie, where he lost a four-man playoff. He reached the final of the WGC-Dell Technologies Match Play in back-to-back years, winning the title in 2019. Since stepping back from a full schedule, he has moved into a Golf Channel and NBC booth role while still teeing it up selectively. The current setup pairs two Callaway nine-degree heads, a Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond Plus and an Elyte Triple Diamond, both built with Mitsubishi Diamana PD 60 TX shafts. The irons flipped from Wilson Staff Model CB and Utility blades to a Srixon ZXi5 and ZXi7 combo on Dynamic Gold Mid 115 S300s, and the L.A.B. DF3 has given way to an Odyssey Ai-ONE Square 2 Square Jailbird. Driver has stayed Callaway across every snapshot, and the Pro V1 remains the ball of choice.
kevin-kisner:2025-02-06.history_narrative: Across six snapshots, Callaway has been the only driver brand in the bag, moving from the GBB and Great Big Bertha builds through the Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond Max and into the current Paradym Ai Smoke and Elyte Triple Diamond pair. The iron rotation went from Callaway Apex Pro and Apex UT through 2022, to Wilson Staff Model CB and Utility through 2024, then to a Srixon ZXi5 and ZXi7 combo in the current bag. Putter has cycled through several Odyssey models, a brief L.A.B. DF3 stint in 2024, and back to Odyssey with the Ai-ONE Jailbird. The Titleist Pro V1 has been the constant ball, with one Pro V1x snapshot in 2021.

matt-jones:2021-03-21.lede: Matt Jones is an Australian professional on the PGA Tour with two PGA Tour titles to his name, the 2014 Shell Houston Open and the 2021 Honda Classic, the latter a five-shot wire-to-wire win. He turned professional in 1997, came up through the Nationwide Tour, and has represented Australia at the Presidents Cup. The current setup leans classic: a Titleist 712 MB blade set running 4 through PW, paired with a Mizuno Pro Fli-Hi 2-iron at the top end, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue S400. Off the tee it is a Titleist TSi2 at 9 degrees with a Ventus Blue 7 X, and around the greens a Scotty Cameron Newport 2 GSS prototype handles putting duties. Pro V1x is the ball. Across the snapshots on file, driver has stayed in the Titleist family.
matt-jones:2021-03-21.history_narrative: The 2021-03-21 bag is the only snapshot on record in the database. What stands out is the mix of an older Titleist 712 MB blade set with a modern TSi2 driver, plus a Mizuno utility breaking up an otherwise all-Titleist setup.

paul-casey:2022-03-07.lede: Paul Casey is an English professional who has spent most of his career on the PGA Tour and DP World Tour, with multiple Ryder Cup appearances for Europe and a career that peaked at world number three. His résumé includes wins on both major tours, among them back to back Valspar Championship titles in 2018 and 2019, though a major championship has eluded him. The bag reads like a player who found a setup and stopped tinkering. The TSi3 sits at 9 degrees with a Diamana D+ Limited 60 TX, the iron build runs a Mizuno JPX919 Hot Metal Pro split at the top into MP-5 blades from the 5 down, and the Scotty Cameron GSS Prototype has not moved. Across the snapshots on file, driver, irons and putter all carry over unchanged. Titleist remains the only driver brand observed in the data, and the Pro V1 rounds out a setup built on continuity rather than rotation.
paul-casey:2022-03-07.history_narrative: Across the two snapshots on file, from January 2021 through March 2022, the core of Casey's bag holds steady. The Titleist TSi3 driver, the Mizuno JPX919 Hot Metal Pro long irons paired with MP-5 blades, and the Scotty Cameron GSS Prototype putter all carry through both bags. Titleist is the only driver brand observed in the data, and no model changes register across the period covered.

graeme-mcdowell:2022-04-21.lede: Graeme McDowell is the Northern Irishman who won the 2010 U.S. Open at Pebble Beach, ending a 40-year drought for European players at that championship. He holed the clinching putt at Celtic Manor later that year to seal the Ryder Cup for Europe, and has logged multiple wins on both the PGA Tour and DP World Tour across his career. The current bag is a full Srixon build from tee through long iron, anchored by a Z 785 driver bent to 10.5 degrees with a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 X. The Z 745 irons from 4 through 9 carry over from the 2020 snapshot, with a ZX5 utility now slotted at the 3 spot in place of the Z 585 long iron seen two years earlier. The Odyssey White Hot Pro #7 putter and Z-Star XV ball remain untouched between snapshots, and every driver observed in the data set has been Srixon.
graeme-mcdowell:2022-04-21.history_narrative: Across both snapshots McDowell has played a Srixon driver, Srixon irons, an Odyssey White Hot Pro #7, and a Srixon Z-Star XV. The Z 785 driver and Z 745 mid and short irons are constants between 2020 and 2022. The only visible change is at the top of the iron set, where the Z 585 long iron in the 2020 bag has been replaced by a ZX5 utility built with a Fujikura Atmos HB Tour Spec shaft.

ryan-palmer:2025-11-04.lede: Ryan Palmer is a four-time PGA Tour winner whose career stretches back to his rookie season in 2004, with victories at the 2004 FUNAI Classic, the 2008 Ginn sur Mer Classic, the 2010 Sony Open, and the 2019 Zurich Classic alongside Jon Rahm. He played on the 2019 Presidents Cup team and has been a fixture inside the Tour's veteran ranks for two decades. Srixon irons have been the through line across every snapshot on file, evolving from the Z 785 era into the current ZXi5 and ZXi7 split with a ZXiU long iron, all running KBS Tour 130 X in the cavity backs. The driver is the larger move: TaylorMade SIM in 2020 and 2022, then a shift to Titleist with the TSR2 in 2023 and 2024, now a GT2 at 9 degrees. A Titleist Pro V1x has been in play across every snapshot logged.
ryan-palmer:2025-11-04.history_narrative: Srixon irons are the constant across all five snapshots, with the build progressing from a Z 785 base in 2020 into a Z U85 plus Z 785 combo, then a ZX U with Z 785 and Z-Forged II in 2024, and now a full ZXi family setup. The driver arc moves from TaylorMade SIM in 2020 and 2022 to Titleist TSR2 in 2023 and 2024, landing on the GT2 in the current bag. Putter history runs through the Odyssey Rossie II, O-Works R-Line and Jailbird Mini, and back to the Rossie II before the recent switch to a TaylorMade Spider Tour S. Pro V1x is the only ball logged across the span.

brendan-steele:2021-01-25.lede: Brendan Steele is a three-time PGA Tour winner, with victories at the 2011 Valero Texas Open and back-to-back Safeway Open titles in 2016 and 2017. He played college golf at UC Riverside and has represented the United States at the Presidents Cup. The current setup leans on a TaylorMade SIM2 driver at 9 degrees with a Fujikura Ventus Black 7 X, a shaft and profile combination that became a Tour staple through 2020 and into 2021. The iron stack is a Wilson split: a Staff Utility 4-iron at 24 degrees on a SteelFiber 110CW X, then Staff Model blades from 5 through pitching wedge on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. A Scotty Cameron Phantom X handles putting duties, and the ball is a Bridgestone Tour B XS. Steele is one of the more visible Wilson Staff players on Tour, and the blade-plus-utility configuration reflects that.
brendan-steele:2021-01-25.history_narrative: The 2021-01-25 bag is the only snapshot on record in the database, so no brand movement can be tracked from this dataset alone. What stands out in that single entry is the full Wilson Staff iron commitment paired with a TaylorMade driver and a Bridgestone ball, a multi-brand build that is increasingly rare at the top of the game.

talor-gooch:2024-05-21.lede: Talor Gooch turned a 2021 RSM Classic title into a breakout 2021-22 PGA Tour season, then left for LIV Golf in 2022 and ran away with the 2023 LIV individual season points title on the back of three wins. He plays for the RangeGoats GC and remains a fixture in LIV's top tier. The current bag's headline is the driver: a PING G430 LST at 9 degrees with a Tensei 1K White 80 TX, the first non-Callaway driver across any of the recorded snapshots. The iron stack stayed loyal in the move, a Callaway X Forged UT at 22 degrees feeding into X Forged CB long irons and Apex MB scoring clubs, all on Modus3 Tour 125 X. The Odyssey Tri-Hot 5K Two carries over from 2023, the latest version of an Odyssey Two-style putter he has gamed since the Toulon custom in 2021.
talor-gooch:2024-05-21.history_narrative: Across the five snapshots, the driver brand arc runs Callaway to PING. Gooch ran Callaway Triple Diamond heads from the 2021 Epic Speed through the 2022 Rogue ST LS and into the 2023 Paradym before switching into the PING G430 LST by May 2024. The Callaway iron blueprint, X Forged long irons paired with Apex MB scoring clubs, held across every snapshot. The putter has been an Odyssey Two shape throughout, moving from the 2021 Toulon custom through the Tri-Hot Two prototype to the current Tri-Hot 5K Two.

brendon-todd:2024-02-22.lede: Brendon Todd is a three-time PGA Tour winner whose career was rebuilt around a precision short game and one of the tightest driving profiles on tour. His first win came at the 2014 Byron Nelson, followed by back-to-back victories at the 2019 Bermuda Championship and the 2019 Mayakoba Classic, the latter run vaulting him back inside the world's top 15 after years spent rebuilding his swing. The driver head has stayed in the PING family across every snapshot on file, moving from a G410 LST in 2020 to a G430 in 2023 and the current G430 Max at 10.5 degrees with a Fujikura Ventus TR Red 6 X. The Titleist 718 T-MB and 718 CB iron pairing has been a fixture going back to 2020, surviving multiple driver updates and a flatstick overhaul. The putter is where the bag has actually turned over, with the SIK Pro C-Series seen in 2020 and 2023 replaced by an Odyssey pairing, a White Hot OG Rossie and a Toulon Design San Diego.
brendon-todd:2024-02-22.history_narrative: Across the three snapshots, PING has held the driver slot throughout, progressing G410 LST to G430 to G430 Max. The Titleist 718 T-MB and 718 CB irons have been constant since 2020, with the T100 dropping out of the set after the earliest snapshot. The biggest change is at the putter, where the SIK Pro C-Series seen in 2020 and 2023 has given way to an Odyssey pairing of the White Hot OG Rossie and the Toulon Design San Diego in the current bag.

luke-donald:2022-03-20.lede: Luke Donald is the English professional who reached World No. 1 in 2011 and held the top ranking for 56 weeks across that year and 2012. He is the only player to top the money lists on both the PGA Tour and the European Tour in the same season, a feat he accomplished in 2011, and his Ryder Cup record as a player runs four appearances with multiple winning sides. The current setup leans hard into Mizuno, with the ST-Z driver at 9.5 degrees feeding a full Mizuno iron stack: a Pro Fli-Hi 2-iron up top, Pro 225 utilities through the mid irons, and Pro 221 blades from 6 through pitching wedge. Shafts are uniform Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 across the irons, with a Fujikura Ventus TR Blue 6 X in the driver. An Odyssey Works Versa 7H CS handles the putting, and the ball is a Pro V1x.
luke-donald:2022-03-20.history_narrative: The 2022-03-20 bag is the only snapshot on record in the database. What stands out is the Mizuno saturation from tee through pitching wedge, paired with a multi-model iron build that blends a driving iron, hollow-body utilities, and forged blades under one shaft spec.

kevin-na:2022-03-24.lede: Kevin Na is a five-time PGA Tour winner whose victories include the Justin Timberlake Shriners Hospitals for Children Open, the Greenbrier Classic, and the 2021 Sony Open in Hawaii. Born in South Korea and raised in California, he turned professional out of high school in 2001 and built a career known for elite short game and one of the more deliberate pre-shot routines on Tour. The bag is Callaway from tee through approach. The current driver is the Epic Speed Triple Diamond at 9 degrees with a Graphite Design Tour AD GP 6 TX, an update from the GBB Epic logged in the January 2021 snapshot. The iron setup has held: a Rogue Pro 4-iron paired with Apex Pro 16s from the 5 through pitching wedge, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue S400. The Odyssey Toulon Madison putter and Pro V1x ball carry over from the previous snapshot unchanged.
kevin-na:2022-03-24.history_narrative: Across both snapshots, Na has stayed inside the Callaway ecosystem at driver and irons, with the only documented change being the move from the GBB Epic to the Epic Speed Triple Diamond between January 2021 and March 2022. The Rogue Pro long iron and Apex Pro 16 mid and short irons remained in place across both bags. The Odyssey Toulon Madison putter and Titleist Pro V1x ball are constants on the record.

james-hahn:2025-06-20.lede: James Hahn is a three-time PGA Tour winner, with victories at the 2014 Northern Trust Open, the 2015 Wells Fargo Championship in a playoff over Roberto Castro, and the 2016 Wells Fargo Championship. He has spent the bulk of his career on the PGA Tour after working his way up through the Web.com Tour. The driver head has moved through three brands across the available snapshots, from TaylorMade Stealth Plus in 2022, to Titleist TSi3 and later GT3, and now a PING G440 at 9 degrees with a Fujikura Speeder 661 TR X shaft. The iron setup currently pairs a Callaway X Forged UT long iron with a TaylorMade P7MB blade run from 4 through PW on KBS Tour 125 S+, a mixed setup that reflects a willingness to cross OEMs through the bag. The L.A.B. Golf MEZZ.1 Max putter is the one fixed point in the recent record, carried over from the 2024 snapshot.
james-hahn:2025-06-20.history_narrative: The driver brand has rotated across every snapshot, TaylorMade Stealth Plus in 2022, Titleist TSi3 in 2023, Titleist GT3 in late 2024, and PING G440 in the current bag. Irons have moved between PXG 0311 ST Gen4 and Callaway X Forged builds more than once, with the current TaylorMade P7MB block representing a new entry. The putter shifted from a Scotty Cameron Timeless to a T12.5 Prototype before settling into the L.A.B. MEZZ.1 Max that has held through the last two snapshots. Ball has stayed in the Titleist Pro V1 family throughout, with the current spec back on Pro V1x.

adam-long:2022-02-02.lede: Adam Long is an American professional on the PGA Tour, best known for winning the 2019 Desert Classic as a rookie, holding off Phil Mickelson and Adam Hadwin down the stretch at PGA West. That victory secured his Tour card and remains the centerpiece of his résumé, with a handful of close calls and a runner-up at the 2021 Honda Classic filling in the years since. The bag is a TaylorMade build through and through, anchored by the Stealth driver at 9 degrees with a Project X HZRDUS Smoke Green 60 6.5 X shaft. The iron setup splits the difference between distance and feel, a P790 4-iron leading into P760s from 5 through pitching wedge, all on Project X 6.5 X. Compared to the 2020 snapshot, the driver moved from SIM Max to Stealth and the Scotty Cameron Futura X5R Tour gave way to a Phantom T-5 Proto, while the P790/P760 iron combo carried over unchanged.
adam-long:2022-02-02.history_narrative: Across both snapshots, TaylorMade has been the sole driver and iron supplier, with the P790 long iron and P760 mid-to-short iron pairing held over from 2020 into the current build. The driver progressed from SIM Max to Stealth, and the putter moved within the Scotty Cameron lineup from a Futura X5R Tour to a Phantom T-5 Proto. The throughline is a TaylorMade-and-Scotty setup that has been refreshed at the head, not rebuilt.

henrik-stenson:2022-02-26.lede: Henrik Stenson is a Swedish professional who turned pro in 1998 and built a career across the European Tour and PGA Tour. He won the 2016 Open Championship at Royal Troon, taking the Claret Jug with a final-round 63 in a duel with Phil Mickelson, and was the first Scandinavian man to win a major. He also captured the FedEx Cup in 2013, the Race to Dubai the same year, and represented Europe in five Ryder Cups. The current setup leans hard on Callaway, with an Epic Max LS driver at 9 degrees on a Project X HZRDUS Yellow Hand Crafted shaft and the Legacy Black irons running through the bag from 3-iron to pitching wedge on Nippon Modus3 Tour 120 X. The Odyssey 2-Ball Ten putter has held its slot across both snapshots, and the only meaningful change from the 2021 build is the ball, a switch from Pro V1x to Pro V1.
henrik-stenson:2022-02-26.history_narrative: Across both snapshots the framework is unchanged: Callaway Epic Max LS driver, Callaway Legacy Black irons, and an Odyssey 2-Ball Ten putter. Driver brand history shows Callaway throughout the data on file. The lone documented swap is at the ball, moving from Titleist Pro V1x in the 2021 snapshot to Pro V1 in the current build.

phil-mickelson:2025-06-12.lede: Phil Mickelson is a six-time major champion, with three Masters titles, a PGA Championship, an Open Championship, and the 2021 PGA that made him the oldest major winner in the game's history. He spent decades on the PGA Tour with 45 wins before moving to LIV Golf in 2022, where he captains HyFlyers GC. The driver head tells the current story: a PING G440 LST at 7.5 degrees, which marks a third manufacturer at the top of the bag across the snapshots on file. Earlier data shows Callaway drivers from the Mavrik Sub Zero through the Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond, with a TaylorMade BRNR Mini logged alongside the Paradym in 2023, before the move to PING. The Callaway X Forged irons have stayed in the set through every snapshot, now paired with a Rogue ST Pro 5-iron and an Odyssey White Hot XG PM blade back in the putter slot.
phil-mickelson:2025-06-12.history_narrative: From 2021 through 2024, the driver was Callaway across four snapshots, running Mavrik Sub Zero, Epic Speed Triple Diamond, Rogue ST Max LS, Paradym Triple Diamond, and Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond, with a TaylorMade BRNR Mini Driver logged in 2023. The current snapshot shows a PING G440 LST, the third driver brand observed in the data. Callaway X Forged irons appear in every snapshot, the most stable line in the bag. The putter has cycled through Odyssey milled and PM blades, a L.A.B. DF3 in 2024, and an Odyssey White Hot XG PM blade in the current setup.

stewart-cink:2024-06-27.lede: Stewart Cink is a veteran American professional who turned pro in 1995 and has spent his career on the PGA Tour. He won the 2009 Open Championship at Turnberry in a playoff over Tom Watson, and his résumé includes eight PGA Tour titles along with multiple Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup appearances. After a quiet stretch, he returned to the winner's circle at the 2020 Safeway Open and the 2021 RBC Heritage. The current setup is a full PING build from tee to green, anchored by the G430 Max 10K driver bent to 9.5 degrees with a Graphite Design Tour AD XC shaft. The iron stack is a three-model mix, i210 long irons into Blueprint T mid and short irons, with an i230 utility wedge closing the set. The Vault 2.0 Ketsch Stealth putter has been in the bag across every recorded snapshot, paired throughout with a Titleist Pro V1x.
stewart-cink:2024-06-27.history_narrative: Across four snapshots dating to 2021, Cink has stayed entirely within PING for driver and irons. The driver progressed from the G425 Max in 2021 and 2022 to the G430 Max in 2023 and the G430 Max 10K in the current build. Iron models have shifted between i200, i210, i230, and Blueprint T, but the brand has not. The Vault 2.0 Ketsch Stealth putter appears in three of four snapshots, with a PLD White noted in 2022, and the Pro V1x ball is constant throughout.

guillermo-mito-pereira:2021-09-17.lede: Guillermo Mito Pereira is a Chilean professional who came up through PGA Tour Latinoamerica and the Korn Ferry Tour, earning a 2021 PGA Tour card after a three-win Korn Ferry season triggered the tour's automatic promotion. He is best known to a wider audience for the 2022 PGA Championship at Southern Hills, where he held a three-shot lead on the 72nd tee before a double bogey dropped him into a playoff he ultimately lost. The driver is a PING G425 Max at 10.5 degrees with a Graphite Design Tour AD DI 7 X, a high-launch setup that fits a player who hits up on it and leans on carry. The irons are PING iBlade 3-9 on True Temper Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100, a forged blade build that has long since cycled out of PING's catalog but still shows up in the bags of better ball-strikers who never found a reason to leave it. The putter is a PING PLD Prototype. Ball is Pro V1.
guillermo-mito-pereira:2021-09-17.history_narrative: The September 2021 bag is the only recorded snapshot on file, captured during Pereira's Korn Ferry promotion season. Notable for being entirely PING from driver through putter, with a Pro V1 as the only non-PING component.

danny-lee:2022-11-15.lede: Danny Lee turned pro in 2008 after a decorated amateur run that included the U.S. Amateur title, and he has logged multiple PGA Tour wins, including the 2015 Greenbrier Classic. The New Zealander represented his country at the Olympics and has spent the bulk of his career on the PGA Tour, with stretches on the LIV roster as well. The Callaway thread runs through everything on the truck order. Both verified snapshots show a full Callaway driver and iron build, with Odyssey Toulon on the putter, though the specific models have all turned over between February and November of 2022. The driver moved from a Rogue ST Triple Diamond LS to an Epic Max LS at 9 degrees on a Mitsubishi Tensei CK Pro Orange 60 TX. The irons shifted from an Apex TCB and Apex MB pairing to a Rogue ST Pro 4-iron stacked into X Forged CB 5-9, all on KBS Tour-V 125. The Toulon Las Vegas gave way to a Toulon La Grange RS.
danny-lee:2022-11-15.history_narrative: Across both snapshots, the bag stays inside the Callaway and Odyssey Toulon ecosystem with no brand changes at driver, irons, or putter. The February 2022 setup paired a Rogue ST Triple Diamond LS driver with an Apex TCB and Apex MB iron combo and a Toulon Las Vegas putter. By November 2022, every model had turned: Epic Max LS driver, a Rogue ST Pro 4-iron into X Forged CB 5-9 on KBS Tour-V 125, and a Toulon La Grange RS in the bag.

tiger-woods:2024-05-14.lede: Tiger Woods is a 15-time major champion and 82-time PGA Tour winner, tied with Sam Snead for the all-time Tour victory record. His career Grand Slam was completed at the 2000 Open Championship, and he has spent more weeks at world number one than any player in the modern era. The Scotty Cameron Newport 2 GSS prototype putter is the through-line, present in every snapshot dating back to 2019 and carried into Augusta this spring. The irons are TaylorMade throughout, with the P7TW signature model anchoring the set and a P770 driving iron slotted in at the 3 since late 2022. Driver has cycled through the TaylorMade line, M5 in 2019, SIM in 2020, Stealth Plus from 2021 through 2022, and the Qi10 LS in the current build at 10.5 degrees set to 9.75. The ball moved from Tour B XS to Tour B X in mid-2022 and has stayed there.
tiger-woods:2024-05-14.history_narrative: Across eight snapshots from 2019 through May 2024, the driver has remained TaylorMade the entire span, progressing M5 to SIM to Stealth Plus to Qi10 LS. The P7TW irons and the Scotty Cameron Newport 2 GSS prototype putter are constants, with a TaylorMade P770 3-iron added by the December 2022 snapshot. The Bridgestone ball shifted from Tour B XS to Tour B X in the July 2022 snapshot and has not changed since.

ian-poulter:2021-09-26.lede: Ian Poulter is an English professional with more than a dozen wins on the European Tour and three PGA Tour titles, best known as one of the most decorated Ryder Cup performers of his era. His résumé includes runner-up finishes at the 2008 Open Championship and the 2012 WGC-HSBC Champions, along with a long stretch inside the world's top 50. He has played out of Titleist staff bags for the bulk of his career. The current setup leans heavily on that relationship: a TSi3 driver at 10 degrees with a Ventus Blue 6 S, a U-500 utility at the 4, a T100 at the 5, and 718 AP2s running 6 through 9, all on Project X LZ 7.0 shafts. A Scotty Cameron Phantom X 11 Prototype handles the putting, with a Pro V1x in play. Across the two logged snapshots, every category remains Titleist.
ian-poulter:2021-09-26.history_narrative: Across both snapshots on file, Poulter's bag is fully Titleist from driver to ball. The March 2021 entry and the September 2021 entry list the same TSi3 driver, U-500 utility, T100, 718 AP2 irons, Phantom X 11 Prototype putter, and Pro V1x. No category turnover is visible in the data.

scott-stallings:2022-08-17.lede: Scott Stallings is a three-time PGA Tour winner, with victories at the 2011 Greenbrier Classic, the 2012 True Life Open, and the 2014 Farmers Insurance Open at Torrey Pines. He earned his first Presidents Cup consideration after a strong 2023 campaign that included a runner-up finish at the WM Phoenix Open. The bag reads Titleist top to bottom. A TSi3 driver at 10 degrees, settings turned down to 9.25, runs a UST Mamiya LIN-Q M40X White 5F5 shaft, and the iron set splits a T200 4-iron into T100s from the 5 through pitching wedge, all on KBS $ Taper 130. The putter is a Scotty Cameron Newport 2.6 Prototype, and the ball is a Pro V1x. With only one snapshot on record, every observed club carries the Titleist script, a single-brand build from tee to green.
scott-stallings:2022-08-17.history_narrative: The 2022-08-17 build is the only snapshot in the database for Stallings, so there is no prior configuration to compare against. What stands out is the all-Titleist construction, the T200/T100 combo set on a single KBS $ Taper 130 spec, and the Scotty Cameron Newport 2.6 Prototype putter anchoring the short game.

grayson-murray:2024-01-14.lede: Grayson Murray is an American professional on the PGA Tour who turned pro in 2016 and broke through for his first Tour win at the 2017 Barbasol Championship. After several years of inconsistent results and an extended stretch on the Korn Ferry Tour, he reestablished full PGA Tour status and continued competing at the top level. The current setup leans heavily on Mizuno, with the ST-X 230 driver at 10.5 degrees feeding into a Mizuno Pro 225 utility 4-iron and Pro 221 blades from 5 through pitching wedge, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. The driver is built with a UST Mamiya LIN-Q M40X White 7F5, a stiffer profile that pairs with the ST-X's draw-biased head. Flatstick duty goes to a L.A.B. Golf LINK.1 fit with the Kinetixx Tuned Zero TRQ shaft, a torque-balanced answer to face rotation. Ball is the Titleist Pro V1.
grayson-murray:2024-01-14.history_narrative: Only one snapshot is on record in the database, dated 2024-01-14. What stands out is the full Mizuno top of the bag, driver and irons under one brand, which is uncommon on Tour and points to a tightly integrated build.

wyndham-clark:2026-05-24.lede: Wyndham Clark broke through in 2023 with his first PGA Tour victory at the Wells Fargo Championship, then won the U.S. Open at Los Angeles Country Club a month later. He followed that in early 2024 with a course-record 60 at Pebble Beach en route to winning the AT&T Pro-Am, cementing his status among the tour's top American players. The current bag marks a clean departure from where he started: a TaylorMade Qi4D driver now sits in the slot Titleist held across every prior snapshot, with a Project X Titan shaft underneath. The irons remain a Titleist split, T200s in the long end and T100s from the six down, shafted with Dynamic Gold X7. The putter is a PING Scottsdale TEC Ally Blue, ending a run of Odyssey Jailbird variants that anchored the bag from 2023 through late 2024. The Pro V1x has never moved.
wyndham-clark:2026-05-24.history_narrative: Across the six snapshots, the Pro V1x is the only constant. Titleist drivers (TSi3, then TSR3) held the slot from 2023 into late 2024 before the switch to the TaylorMade Qi4D shown in 2026. The iron setup cycled through several Titleist and Mizuno combinations before settling on the current T200/T100 pairing. The putter arc runs Odyssey Versa Jailbird to Odyssey Ai-ONE Jailbird to the PING Scottsdale TEC now in play.

jon-rahm:2026-06-16.lede: Jon Rahm is a Spanish professional with two major titles, the 2021 U.S. Open at Torrey Pines and the 2023 Masters, and multiple stints at world number one during his PGA Tour tenure before joining LIV Golf in December 2023. He has captured the DP World Tour's season-long Race to Dubai and represented Europe in the Ryder Cup on multiple occasions. The current driver is a Callaway Quantum Triple Diamond at 10.5 degrees playing to 11.5, on a Fujikura Ventus Black 7 X. The Apex TCB blades have been in the bag across every Callaway-era snapshot going back to 2021, run with Project X Rifle 6.5 shafts. The putter is an Odyssey White Hot OG Rossie, a return to the non-insert Ai-ONE Rossie S that occupied the bag through 2024 and 2025. The data shows a clean brand arc from TaylorMade in 2019 and 2020 to a full Callaway and Odyssey setup from 2021 onward.
jon-rahm:2026-06-16.history_narrative: The 2019 and 2020 snapshots show a full TaylorMade bag: M5 then SIM drivers, P750 irons, Spider X putter, TP5 ball. From March 2021 forward every snapshot is Callaway from tee to green, with Odyssey on the putter and a Callaway ball. The Apex TCB irons and a Rossie-shape putter have been constants across the Callaway years, while the driver has cycled through Epic Speed, Rogue ST, Paradym, Paradym Ai Smoke, Elyte, and now Quantum Triple Diamond heads. The ball moved from Chrome Soft X to Chrome Tour by the 2025 snapshot.

chris-gotterup:2026-06-03.lede: Chris Gotterup is a PGA Tour professional and former Rutgers standout who won the 2022 Fred Haskins Award as college golf's top player. He broke through on Tour at the 2024 Myrtle Beach Classic, then added a second title at the 2025 Genesis Scottish Open, edging Rory McIlroy at The Renaissance Club. That Scottish win came with a PING G440 LST in the bag, and the driver situation has since expanded rather than settled. The current setup carries three drivers: a TaylorMade Qi4D at 8 degrees alongside two G440 LST heads tuned to 9 and 7.5 degrees, all built on Project X HZRDUS shafts. The Bridgestone 220 MB irons, TaylorMade P770 3-iron, Spider X Tour putter, and Tour B X MindSet ball have carried through every snapshot on file. The one clear brand movement in the data is at the driver, where PING has been joined by TaylorMade rather than replaced.
chris-gotterup:2026-06-03.history_narrative: Across the July 2025, February 2026, and current snapshots, the Bridgestone 220 MB irons, TaylorMade Spider X Tour putter, and Bridgestone Tour B X MindSet ball have not moved. The driver is the only category showing change: PING G440 LST was the sole driver on file in both 2025 and early 2026, and the current bag adds a TaylorMade Qi4D and a second G440 LST at a lower loft. The observed brand arc at driver runs PING to PING plus TaylorMade.

tyrrell-hatton:2026-06-17.lede: Tyrrell Hatton is an English professional who joined LIV Golf's Legion XIII in 2024 after building his career on the DP World Tour and PGA Tour. His resume includes back-to-back BMW PGA Championship titles at Wentworth, an Arnold Palmer Invitational win at Bay Hill, multiple Ryder Cup appearances for Europe, and a run inside the world's top ten. The bag is a full PING build from driver through putter, currently anchored by the G440 LST with a Mitsubishi Diamana TB 60 TX shaft. The iron setup is a three-model combo, an iDi utility at the 3, i240s through the mid-irons, and Blueprint S from the 7 through pitching wedge, all on Nippon Modus3 Tour 120 X. Every verified snapshot dating back to 2021 shows PING metalwoods, PING irons, a PING Oslo-shape putter, and a Titleist Pro V1x. No brand has ever rotated out.
tyrrell-hatton:2026-06-17.history_narrative: Across five snapshots from 2021 to 2026, Hatton has played PING top to bottom with a Titleist Pro V1x. The driver progression runs G425 LST to G430 LST to G440 Max to the current G440 LST. Irons evolved from i210 to i230 to the present iDi/i240/Blueprint S combo, with Blueprint S appearing from the 2023 snapshot forward. The putter has stayed in the Oslo family throughout, moving from a Vault Oslo to PLD Oslo Prototypes and now the PLD Oslo 400 Prototype.

siwoo-kim:2026-05-26.lede: Siwoo Kim is a Korean-born, Virginia-raised professional who played collegiately at the University of Virginia before turning pro in 2019 and grinding through the Korn Ferry Tour ranks. His profile built on tidy ball-striking and a workmanlike short game, with Korn Ferry contention lines that eventually translated into a PGA Tour card. The bag reflects that identity. Kim runs a full Callaway build from tee to green, currently anchored by the Quantum Triple Diamond driver at 8.5 degrees on a Ventus Black 6 X, with a split-forged iron set pairing an X Forged 4-iron into Apex MB 5-PW, all on KBS Tour V 125. The Odyssey putter presence is the through-line across every snapshot on file, and the Chrome Tour ball rounds out the staff loyalty. Every driver logged in the historical data has been a Triple Diamond head, which is the cleanest signal in the bag.
siwoo-kim:2026-05-26.history_narrative: Across six snapshots dating to 2021, Kim has never left Callaway on the driver, cycling through Epic Speed, Rogue ST, Paradym, Paradym Ai Smoke, and now Quantum, all in the Triple Diamond spec. The iron progression moved from Apex Pro '19 Dot into X Forged CB, then a mixed X Forged UT and Apex CB build, before landing on the current X Forged 4-iron with Apex MB 5-PW. Odyssey has held the putter slot throughout, running Toulon Madison, 2-Ball Ten, a broomstick 2-Ball Ten Ten, and the current Prototype. The ball reads as Chrome Soft X in earlier snapshots and Chrome Tour in the current bag.

alex-noren:2026-06-06.lede: Alex Noren is a Swedish professional with ten DP World Tour victories, a resume that includes the 2016 BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth and a 2018 European Ryder Cup appearance at Le Golf National. He climbed as high as world No. 8 in the summer of 2018 and has spent the last several seasons based on the PGA Tour. The Odyssey O-Works 1W has anchored the bag across every snapshot on file going back to 2021, one of the more stable putter runs on tour. Callaway is the through line everywhere else too, with the driver progression moving from Epic Max LS to Rogue ST Max LS to Paradym and now the Paradym Ai Smoke Max D in the draw setting. The irons tell the same loyalty story, Apex Pro through 2022 before the switch to Apex TCB blades that has held from 2023 forward. Ball of choice moved from Chrome Soft X to the newer Chrome Tour.
alex-noren:2026-06-06.history_narrative: Six snapshots, one brand. Noren has played Callaway top to bottom across every recorded bag, cycling through the Epic, Rogue, and Paradym driver families while upgrading irons from Apex Pro to the Apex TCB blades between the 2022 and 2023 snapshots. The Odyssey O-Works 1W putter has not moved once. The ball transitioned from Chrome Soft X to Chrome Tour between the 2022 and 2023 snapshots and has stayed there since.

patrick-reed:2026-05-18.lede: Patrick Reed turned pro in 2011 and built his reputation on match play, anchored by a 2018 Masters title and a long run of Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup appearances for the United States. He collected nine PGA Tour wins before departing for LIV Golf in 2022, where he plays for the 4 Aces GC. The Grindworks irons are the through-line here. The PR-202 long iron and PR-101A set have held their slots since at least 2022, surviving every other change around them. The driver has moved around, Titleist to PXG to PING and back to Titleist, landing on the GT3 at 9 degrees with an Aldila Rogue Silver 130 shaft. The putter history swings between Scotty Cameron and Odyssey, with a Tour Rat 1.5 Prototype currently in the bag, echoing the original Tour Rat he gamed in 2021. The ball moved from Pro V1 to Pro V1x for the current season.
patrick-reed:2026-05-18.history_narrative: The driver arc runs Titleist TSi3 in 2021, PXG 0811X GEN4 in 2022, PING G400 in 2024, then back to Titleist with the GT3 in 2025 and 2026. Grindworks has supplied the irons across every snapshot, with the PR-202 and PR-101A pairing stable from 2022 forward and a Titleist 716 T-MB briefly in the mix in 2024. The putter cycles between Scotty Cameron and Odyssey, currently a Tour Rat 1.5 Prototype after a Timeless 2.5+ in 2025. Ball model shifted from Pro V1 to Pro V1x for 2026.

j-t-poston:2026-06-07.lede: J.T. Poston is a PGA Tour winner out of Western Carolina, with victories at the 2019 Wyndham Championship and the 2022 John Deere Classic, the latter closing bogey-free across 72 holes. He has represented the United States at the Presidents Cup and built a reputation as one of the tour's steadier ball-strikers and short-game operators. The bag reads Titleist top to bottom on the long clubs, with a GTS3 at 9 degrees on a Diamana BF 60 TX up front and a T150 driving iron leading into a T100 set from 5 through 9, all on Project X 6.5. Across every snapshot on file the driver has carried a Titleist badge, moving TS3 to TSR3 to GT3 and now GTS3. The larger change sits on the green, where the Scotty Cameron GoLo 5 Black Tour Prototype that anchored four straight snapshots has been replaced by a TaylorMade Spider Tour X.
j-t-poston:2026-06-07.history_narrative: Across five snapshots from 2020 to 2026, the driver stays Titleist throughout, progressing TS3, TSR3, TSR3, GT3, GTS3. The iron setup shifts inside the Titleist family, with a U-500 and 718 AP2 pairing in 2020 giving way to T100s over T100 combinations through 2024, then a T150 driving iron feeding a T100 5-9 in the current build. The Pro V1x ball line remains constant, with the current entry reading Left Dash. The putter is the outlier: a Scotty Cameron GoLo 5, then the Black Tour Prototype variant across four snapshots, now a TaylorMade Spider Tour X.

jason-day:2026-06-03.lede: Jason Day is an Australian professional who won the 2015 PGA Championship and has spent time at world number one, with double-digit PGA Tour victories across his career including a Players Championship. He turned professional in 2006 and has been a fixture on the PGA Tour since. The PING driver is the through-line: every snapshot on file runs a PING head at the top of the bag, moving from the G425 LST through the G410 LST, G430, G430 LST, and G440 LST before settling back on a G430 LST at 10.5 bent to 9.5, shafted with KBS TGBlack. The iron slot has been the volatile one, cycling through Mizuno MP-20 HMB and JPX921 blends, a run of TaylorMade combo setups spanning P790, P770, P7MC, P760, P7CB and P7TW, and now an Avoda Prototype V3 build from 4 through gauge wedge on KBS TGI graphite. Bridgestone Tour B X has been in play across every snapshot bar one.
jason-day:2026-06-03.history_narrative: Across eight snapshots the driver stays PING throughout, cycling model to model but never leaving the brand. The iron bag tells a different story, opening on Mizuno in 2021, moving into a long TaylorMade run of P-series combos from 2022 through 2025, and landing on Avoda Prototype V3 blades in the current build. The putter has stayed inside TaylorMade's Itsy Bitsy Spider family since 2023 after earlier stints with Odyssey and Scotty Cameron, and the ball has been Bridgestone Tour B X every snapshot since the 2021 Tour B XS entry.

keith-mitchell:2026-06-02.lede: Keith Mitchell is an American PGA Tour player who broke through with a win at the 2019 Honda Classic, closing with a birdie on the 72nd hole at PGA National. He has remained a fixture on Tour since, trading on one of the more reliable driving profiles in the field and posting multiple runner-up finishes in the years following that maiden victory. The current bag marks a meaningful shift up top: the Mizuno ST-Z 230 that anchored every snapshot from 2021 through late 2025 has been replaced by a TaylorMade Qi4D LS on a Project X Titan Yellow 6 X shaft. The irons stay in the Mizuno family, a Pro 225 utility at the 2 slot into Pro S-1s from 4 through 9, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. The Scotty Cameron J.A.T. Prototype that ran through 2025 has given way to an Odyssey Stroke Lab Exo 2-Ball. Ball remains Pro V1, as it has across every snapshot on record.
keith-mitchell:2026-06-02.history_narrative: Across seven snapshots, Mitchell's driver ran Mizuno from 2021 through late 2025, moving from the original ST-Z to the ST-Z 230 before the 2026 switch to the TaylorMade Qi4D LS. Irons have been Mizuno throughout, cycling from MP-20 into Pro 221, Pro 225, and now the Pro S-1 build with a 225 utility. The putter has been the most restless slot, rotating through a TaylorMade Spider Tour, a Scotty Cameron Kombi, back to Spider, into the Scotty J.A.T. Prototype, and now the Odyssey Stroke Lab Exo 2-Ball. Titleist Pro V1 is the one constant.

eric-cole:2026-06-01.lede: Eric Cole is a PGA Tour pro who turned pro in 2011 and spent years grinding through the Korn Ferry Tour before earning his PGA Tour card for the 2022-23 season. He posted a runner-up at the 2023 Honda Classic and was named to the PGA Tour's All-Rookie Team that year. His mother, Laura Baugh, was the 1971 U.S. Women's Amateur champion, and his stepfather, Bobby Cole, won on the PGA Tour. PXG runs the bag top to bottom on the long clubs. The current setup pairs a Lightning Tour Max driver at 9 degrees with a 0311 Gen8 driving 4-iron and 0317 ST irons from 5 through pitching wedge, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue Mid X100. The putter stayed inside the Battle Ready II family across both snapshots, moving from the Bat Attack shape to the Closer. Pro V1x has been the ball in both looks on file.
eric-cole:2026-06-01.history_narrative: Both snapshots on file show a full PXG build across driver, irons and putter, with Titleist Pro V1x as the constant ball. The driver moved from the 0311 Black Ops to the Lightning Tour Max, and the iron set shifted from a 0317 CB and 0317 ST pairing to a 0311 Gen8 4-iron feeding into 0317 ST heads through the pitching wedge. The putter stayed within the PXG Battle Ready II line, changing head shape from Bat Attack to Closer.

sungjae-im:2026-06-04.lede: Sungjae Im turned professional in 2015, earned Korn Ferry Tour Player of the Year in 2018, and captured PGA Tour Rookie of the Year honors in 2019. He has multiple PGA Tour victories, a runner-up finish at the 2020 Masters, and has represented the International Team at the Presidents Cup. The bag reads as a full Titleist build, and it has read that way in every snapshot on file. The TSi2 driver has been in play since 2021, replacing the TS3 seen in the 2020 snapshot, and it now sits at 8 degrees with a Graphite Design Tour AD DI 7 X. The T100 irons have been a fixture across every check-in, with a brief T200 long-iron pairing showing up in the 2021 snapshot before the set went full T100. Putter is the moving piece, currently a Scotty Cameron F5 Tourtype SSS with a Tour Prototype riding alongside it. Pro V1x throughout.
sungjae-im:2026-06-04.history_narrative: Across seven snapshots dating to 2020, the build has been Titleist end to end. Driver moved from TS3 in 2020 to TSi2 by 2021 and has stayed there since. Irons have been T100 throughout, with a T200 long-iron slot appearing only in the 2021 snapshot. The putter has cycled through several Scotty Cameron models, from the Phantom T6 STR in 2020 through Flowback 5 variants to the current F5 Tourtype SSS, now paired with a Tour Prototype. Pro V1x has been the ball at every check-in.

brooks-koepka:2026-05-19.lede: Brooks Koepka is a five-time major champion, with back-to-back U.S. Open titles in 2017 and 2018 and PGA Championship wins in 2018, 2019, and 2023. He reached World No. 1 during his peak PGA Tour run and joined LIV Golf in 2022, where he captains Smash GC. The Nike Vapor Fly Pro 3-iron has stayed in the bag across every snapshot on file, paired with Srixon ZX7 or ZX7 MKII blades from the 4-iron down. The driver has traveled a full loop: TaylorMade SIM2 in early 2021, a Srixon run from late 2021 through 2023, a return to TaylorMade with the Qi10 in 2024, and now a Titleist GT3 at 10 degrees on a Diamana D Limited 60 TX. The putter moved off Scotty Cameron between the 2025 and 2026 snapshots to a TaylorMade Spider Tour V. Ball is back to Pro V1x after a Srixon Z-Star Diamond stretch from 2023 through 2024.
brooks-koepka:2026-05-19.history_narrative: Across eight snapshots from February 2021 to May 2026, the Nike Vapor Fly Pro 3-iron and Srixon ZX7 family blades have been fixtures. Drivers cycled from TaylorMade to a multi-year Srixon block, back to TaylorMade in 2024, then to Titleist GT3 by 2025. The ball moved from Pro V1x to Srixon Z-Star variants during the Srixon driver years, then back to Pro V1x once the Titleist driver arrived. The putter carousel ran through several Scotty Cameron models before landing on a TaylorMade Spider Tour V in the current bag.

lucas-glover:2026-06-04.lede: Lucas Glover is a PGA Tour veteran best known for winning the 2009 U.S. Open at Bethpage Black, with additional Tour titles including the 2011 Wells Fargo, the 2021 John Deere Classic, and back-to-back wins at the 2023 Wyndham Championship and FedEx St. Jude Championship. He has represented the United States in Presidents Cup competition and remains a full-time PGA Tour player. The current desk holds a Titleist GTS2 driver at 10 degrees on a Ventus Blue 6 X, sitting behind a Srixon ZX5 4-iron and ZX7s from the 5 through pitching wedge, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. The Srixon iron pairing has been the constant, running from the ZX5 MKII and ZX7 MKII combo across the 2023, 2024, and 2025 snapshots into the current non-MKII ZX5/ZX7 setup. Drivers have moved Srixon to Titleist to PING and back to Titleist, and four putters are logged in the current bag, led by the L.A.B. MEZZ.1 Max that has been present since 2023.
lucas-glover:2026-06-04.history_narrative: The 2020 and 2021 snapshots show a Srixon Z 785 driver paired with Mizuno and Titleist irons, a Titleist Pro V1/V1x ball, and Argolf then Scotty Cameron putters. From 2023 forward the bag settles on Srixon irons and the Srixon Z-Star XV ball, with the L.A.B. MEZZ.1 Max entering as the primary putter and remaining through every snapshot since. The driver slot is the moving piece, cycling from Srixon Z 785 to Titleist GT2 in 2024, PING G440 Max in 2025, and Titleist GTS2 in the current build, while the 2026 snapshot also logs four putters on the truck.

cameron-smith:2026-05-22.lede: Cameron Smith is the 2022 Open Champion at St Andrews, a Players Championship winner, and a multiple-time PGA Tour winner who departed for LIV Golf in the second half of 2022, where he captains Ripper GC. The Australian has represented his country at the Presidents Cup and built a reputation as one of the best putters and short-game operators of his era. The Scotty Cameron 009M is the through-line: the same putter model logs across all eight snapshots, paired with a Pro V1x that has been in the bag every year on record. The driver has stayed Titleist across the arc, moving TSi3 to TSR2 to TSR3 and now to the GTS3 with a Ventus TR Blue 6 X. The iron setup is where the current bag departs from history, with the long-running Mizuno Pro Fli-Hi utility replaced by T250s in the 4 and 5, running into T100s from the 5-iron down on KBS Tour 130 X Custom Series shafts.
cameron-smith:2026-05-22.history_narrative: Across eight snapshots the Scotty Cameron 009M Prototype and the Pro V1x never leave the bag, and every driver logged is a Titleist, moving TSi3 through TSR2, TSR3, and into the current GTS3. The iron picture evolves around a T100 or T100 Black base, with a Titleist U-500 utility in 2021 giving way to a Mizuno Pro Fli-Hi that held its slot from 2022 through 2025. The 2026 bag drops the Mizuno utility entirely, going all-Titleist in the irons with T250s at the top and T100s from the 5 down.

matt-kuchar:2026-06-02.lede: Matt Kuchar is a nine-time PGA Tour winner whose résumé includes the 2010 Players Championship, a silver medal at the 2016 Rio Olympics, and multiple Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup appearances for the United States. The 1997 US Amateur champion turned pro in 2000 and has spent the better part of two decades as one of the more durable ball-strikers on Tour, known for a flat, homemade swing and a putting stroke that has cycled through arm-lock and conventional lengths. The Bettinardi DASS SS28 Tour Department is the throughline, present in the current bag and in the 2023 snapshot, with a DASS KM-1 arm lock filling the same slot back in 2021. The driver has moved from a Bridgestone Tour B JGR Proto in 2021 to Titleist across the two most recent snapshots, currently a GTS3 at nine degrees with a Ventus TR Blue 6 X. Irons tracked the same Bridgestone-to-Srixon path, landing on a ZXi5/ZXi7 combo with SteelFiber i110cw shafts. The Bridgestone Tour B X ball has stayed put.
matt-kuchar:2026-06-02.history_narrative: The 2021 snapshot shows a full Bridgestone build through the bag with a Bettinardi arm-lock putter and the Tour B X ball. ryan-palmer:2026-06-11.history_narrative: The driver seat tells the clearest story: TaylorMade SIM through 2022, Titleist TSR2 across 2023 and 2024, Titleist GT2 in late 2025, and the Callaway Quantum Triple Diamond in the current build. sam-burns:2026-07-01.lede: Sam Burns is an American professional on the PGA Tour who turned pro in 2017 after a decorated amateur career at LSU, where he won the Jack Nicklaus Award as national player of the year. sam-burns:2026-07-01.history_narrative: Across eleven snapshots from April 2021 to July 2026, Burns has stayed entirely within the Callaway and Odyssey ecosystem. scottie-scheffler:2026-06-29.lede: Scottie Scheffler is an American PGA Tour professional with two Masters titles in 2022 and 2024, the 2025 PGA Championship, back-to-back Players Championships in 2023 and 2024, and Olympic gold at Paris 2024. scottie-scheffler:2026-06-29.history_narrative: Across sixteen snapshots dating back to March 2021, the TaylorMade P7TW mid and short irons and the Titleist Pro V1 have never left the bag. chris-gotterup:2026-07-05.lede: Chris Gotterup came out of Oklahoma with the 2022 Haskins Award and turned pro that summer after a transfer from Rutgers. chris-gotterup:2026-07-05.history_narrative: Across four snapshots from July 2025 to July 2026, the Bridgestone 220 MB irons, TaylorMade Spider X Tour putter, and Bridgestone Tour B X MindSet ball have not changed. viktor-hovland:2026-06-29.lede: Viktor Hovland is the Norwegian who came through Oklahoma State with the 2018 U.S. Amateur, then became the first player from his country to win on the PGA Tour. viktor-hovland:2026-06-29.history_narrative: Across eleven snapshots the driver has been PING the entire way, G425 LST from 2020 through 2025 and G440 LST in the current build. keegan-bradley:2026-06-30.lede: Keegan Bradley won the 2011 PGA Championship in his first major start as a professional, has collected multiple PGA Tour titles since, and was named United States captain for the 2025 Ryder Cup while still active on tour. keegan-bradley:2026-06-30.history_narrative: Across eight snapshots from 2021 to 2026, the driver moved TaylorMade to PING to TaylorMade, opening on the SIM, settling into the G430 LST for roughly three seasons, then landing on the Qi4D LS in the current bag. michael-kim:2026-07-01.lede: Michael Kim is an American professional on the PGA Tour, best known for his eight-shot runaway at the 2018 John Deere Classic, his first and to date only PGA Tour victory. michael-kim:2026-07-01.history_narrative: Across the two logged snapshots, the driver has stayed in the Titleist family, moving from the GT2 in September 2025 to the newer GTS2 at 11 degrees by mid-2026.
