aldrich-potgieter:2026-07-06.lede: Aldrich Potgieter is a South African professional on the PGA Tour, a former Junior Open champion who turned pro as a teenager and broke through with his maiden PGA Tour victory at the 2025 Rocket Classic in a five-hole playoff. aldrich-potgieter:2026-07-06.history_narrative: The February 2025 bag was Titleist-heavy: GT3 driver, T100 and 620 MB irons, Scotty Cameron 009M, Pro V1x. By June 2025 the driver moved to a GT2 and the iron set expanded into T100, T150 and T250, with the 009M putter and a Pro V1x+ Prototype ball. chesson-hadley:2026-07-01.lede: Chesson Hadley is a PGA Tour veteran out of Georgia Tech who broke through at the 2014 Puerto Rico Open, earning PGA Tour Rookie of the Year honors that season. chesson-hadley:2026-07-01.history_narrative: Across three snapshots, the driver line has stayed Titleist top to bottom, cycling TSi3 in 2021, TSR3 in 2024, and GTS2 currently. The Odyssey White Hot OG 2-Ball putter and Titleist Pro V1x ball have not moved in any snapshot on record. graeme-mcdowell:2026-06-18.lede: Graeme McDowell is a Northern Irish professional who won the 2010 U.S. Open at Pebble Beach, holed the clinching putt for Europe at the 2010 Ryder Cup at Celtic Manor, and has represented Europe in four Ryder Cups. graeme-mcdowell:2026-06-18.history_narrative: Across the 2020, 2022, and 2026 snapshots, the Odyssey White Hot Pro #7 putter, Srixon Z-Star XV ball, and Srixon Z 745 short irons remain fixed. tom-kim:2026-06-30.lede: Tom Kim, born Joohyung Kim, is a South Korean professional who broke through on the PGA Tour with the 2022 Wyndham Championship and back-to-back Shriners Children's Open titles in 2022 and 2023, making him the youngest player since Tiger Woods to win multiple PGA Tour events before turning 21. tom-kim:2026-06-30.history_narrative: Across nine snapshots from August 2022 to June 2026, the bag has stayed entirely Titleist. cameron-young:2026-07-20.history_narrative: Every snapshot from 2022 forward shows a full Titleist bag, with no brand movement in driver, irons, putter, or ball. ryan-fox:2026-07-18.history_narrative: Across both verified snapshots Fox has stayed in Srixon woods, irons, and ball, with the driver progressing from the ZXi in June 2025 to the ZXi RKT LS+ by mid-2026. sam-burns:2026-07-18.history_narrative: Every snapshot from 2021 forward shows a Callaway driver, moving through Mavrik, Epic Speed, Rogue ST Triple Diamond, Paradym Triple Diamond and Paradym Triple Diamond S, and into the Quantum Triple Diamond by April 2026. bryson-dechambeau:2026-07-16.lede: Bryson DeChambeau is a two-time U.S. Open champion, winning at Winged Foot in 2020 and Pinehurst No. 2 in 2024, and a LIV Golf member captaining Crushers GC. bryson-dechambeau:2026-07-16.history_narrative: From 2021 through early 2023 the bag was a Cobra build around One Length irons, paired with the SIK armlock putter and a Bridgestone Tour B X ball. siwoo-kim:2026-07-18.lede: Siwoo Kim is a Korean-American professional who played collegiate golf at Virginia before working his way through the Korn Ferry Tour to earn PGA Tour status. siwoo-kim:2026-07-18.history_narrative: Across seven snapshots dating to January 2021, Kim has stayed inside the Callaway and Odyssey ecosystem without exception. neal-shipley:2026-07-21.lede: Neal Shipley is an American professional who turned pro in 2024 after a college career that finished at Ohio State. neal-shipley:2026-07-21.history_narrative: The 2026-07-21 build is the only snapshot on record for Shipley. sean-crocker:2026-07-17.lede: Sean Crocker is an American-born professional who came up through the University of Southern California program and built his career on the DP World Tour after turning pro in 2018. xander-schauffele:2026-07-29.history_narrative: Across twelve snapshots the driver head has changed five times but the brand has not, with Callaway supplying every driver from the 2021 Epic Speed through the current Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond. The Apex TCB irons appear in every bag on record, with brief Mizuno MP-20 and MP-20 HMB blade additions logged in early 2024 and mid 2024. The putter transitioned from the Odyssey O-Works #7 to the Toulon Las Vegas Prototype 7CH by the August 2023 snapshot and has held since. Ball progression moved from Chrome Soft X and its LS Prototype through the Chrome Soft X Prototype and Chrome Tour X, landing on the Chrome Tour in the current bag.

rasmus-hojgaard:2026-07-28.lede: Rasmus Hojgaard is a Danish professional on the DP World Tour with multiple wins on that circuit, including the 2024 Irish Open, and has earned PGA Tour status through his DP World Tour performance. He is the twin brother of Nicolai Hojgaard and has represented Europe in Ryder Cup consideration windows built on those tour victories. The current setup runs Callaway from tee through green, with the Paradym Ai Smoke Triple Diamond driver built to 9.5 degrees on a Mitsubishi Tensei 1K Blue 60 TX. The iron stack pairs an X Forged UT 3-iron on a Modus3 Hybrid graphite-on-steel prototype with X Forged 4-PW on KBS S-Taper 130, a mixed-shaft build that keeps the long iron workable without softening the mid and short irons. The ball is the Chrome Tour X, and the putter is the Odyssey Ai-ONE Milled Jailbird Mini T Versa 90 DB, a mid-mallet counterweighted through the grip.
rasmus-hojgaard:2026-07-28.history_narrative: The 2026-07-28 build is the only recorded snapshot in the DORMIED database for Hojgaard. Notable in that single entry is the full-Callaway construction paired with the split shaft philosophy in the irons, Nippon graphite composite in the utility, KBS steel from the 4-iron down.

matt-wallace:2026-08-01.lede: Matt Wallace is an English professional out of Hillingdon who took the long route to full status, winning six times on the Alps Tour in 2017 before collecting multiple DP World Tour titles, three of them inside the 2018 season. He added a PGA Tour win at the 2023 Corales Puntacana Championship, and his best major result remains a share of third at the 2019 PGA Championship. Two Scotty Cameron prototypes sit in the current bag, a TG6 and a P5 GSS, which puts the putter, driver and ball under one roof. The iron setup is split on purpose: Ping iDi in 2 and 3, a Titleist T250 4-iron, then Titleist 620 CB from 5 through 9. Fujikura Ventus Blue carries the driver and both Ping long irons, with Nippon Modus3 Tour 120 X under the scoring clubs. The full Callaway build that defined the earlier snapshots is no longer represented anywhere in the bag.
matt-wallace:2026-08-01.history_narrative: The 2021 and 2022 snapshots show a Callaway bag top to bottom: Epic Speed and then Rogue ST Triple Diamond S drivers, Apex TCB, Apex MB and X Forged CB irons, an Odyssey putter and the Chrome Soft X ball. The 2023 snapshot marks the transition point, with a Titleist TSR3 driver and a Scotty Cameron Circle T prototype in play while the Callaway X Forged CB irons stayed. The current bag finishes the move, running Titleist driver, irons and ball alongside two Scotty Cameron prototypes. Ping iDi long irons are the only non-Titleist clubs left, and the driver arc across the four snapshots reads Callaway to Titleist with no return.

rickie-fowler:2026-07-31.lede: Rickie Fowler turned professional in 2009 after reaching No. 1 in the world amateur ranking, and took PGA Tour Rookie of the Year honors in 2010. He owns six PGA Tour titles, headlined by the 2015 Players Championship, and has played on multiple Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup teams. No major championships. The current irons are a Cobra 3DP RF Prototype set built 4 through PW around AeroTech SteelFiber i125cw, a full graphite iron setup that few tour players run. Cobra is the constant across all eleven snapshots, every driver and every iron set, from the King F9 Speedback era through Darkspeed and DS-ADAPT to the OPTM X in the bag now. The churn sits elsewhere. The putter has passed through Scotty Cameron, Cobra, Odyssey and L.A.B. before landing back on a Scotty Cameron Phantom 5 Prototype, and the ball moved off the TaylorMade TP5 family to a Titleist Pro V1 between the December 2024 and May 2025 snapshots.
rickie-fowler:2026-07-31.history_narrative: Across eleven snapshots dating to June 2020, the driver and irons never leave Cobra, running from the King F9 Speedback and RadSpeed through LTDx LS, Aerojet LS, Darkspeed, DS-ADAPT X and now the OPTM X. The putter is the volatile slot: Scotty Cameron models in 2020 and early 2021, Cobra King Vintage Sport-45 and Stingray-20 through 2021 and 2022, Odyssey Versa Jailbird across 2023 and into 2024, L.A.B. Golf DF3 by late 2024, and a Scotty Cameron Phantom 5 Prototype in the current bag. The ball stayed inside the TaylorMade TP5 family, Pix and non-Pix, from 2020 through the December 2024 snapshot, then shows as a Titleist Pro V1 from May 2025 forward. The iron models have moved from blades and Speedback cavities to King Tour and finally the 3DP RF Prototype, all under the same badge.

matti-schmid:2026-07-31.lede: Matti Schmid is a German professional who arrived on tour with one of the strongest amateur resumes in Europe, winning the European Amateur Championship in both 2018 and 2019 and spending stretches ranked among the top amateurs in the world. He turned professional in 2020 and moved through the Korn Ferry Tour to a PGA Tour card, and he has played in majors and represented Germany in team competition. Two Cobra OPTM drivers sit at the top of the bag, a 9 degree Max-K and a 10.5 degree X, both built with the same Fujikura Ventus Blue 6 X, which makes the swap a question of head and loft rather than shaft feel. The irons run Cobra 3DP MB from 4 through 9 on Project X LS 7.0, a full blade set with no combo break at the long end. Cobra is the only driver brand on record. The putter and ball go outside that, an Odyssey Ai-One Cruiser 2-Ball Tour Lined and a Titleist Pro V1.
matti-schmid:2026-07-31.history_narrative: The 2026-07-31 build is the only snapshot in the database for Schmid, so there is no change history to trace yet. What it does record is a bag with a Cobra core through the driver slot and the full iron set, two OPTM heads carried on identical Ventus Blue shafts, and Odyssey and Titleist handling the putter and ball. Future snapshots will establish whether that structure holds.

jordan-smith:2026-08-02.lede: Jordan Smith is an English professional on the DP World Tour who came through the Challenge Tour, topping the 2016 Road to Oman rankings before winning the Portugal Masters in his first full season on the main circuit. He added the Bahrain Championship to that record in 2024. The 4-iron is where this bag separates itself: a Titleist T100 fitted with a Graphite Design Tour AD DI-105 Hybrid X, a graphite hybrid shaft in a long iron, sitting directly above 620 CB blades in 5 through 9 on Project X Rifle 7.0 steel. Two head models, two shaft materials, one iron set. The driver is a GTS3 at 8 degrees with the SureFit hosel in D1 and a Mitsubishi Kai'li Prototype 70 TX. Head to ball the build is Titleist, with a Scotty Cameron SSS 009.M Prototype on the putting end and a Pro V1 rather than the firmer Pro V1x.
jordan-smith:2026-08-02.history_narrative: The 2 August 2026 bag is the only snapshot on record in the database, so there is no change history to trace and no earlier build to compare it against. What it shows is a single-brand setup, Titleist driver through ball, with the variance pushed into the shafts: a graphite hybrid profile in the T100 4-iron, heavy steel under the 620 CB blades, and a prototype Mitsubishi in the driver. The putter is a Scotty Cameron SSS 009.M Prototype, a tour-only shape rather than a retail model.

christo-lamprecht:2026-08-02.lede: Christo Lamprecht is a South African professional who came out of Georgia Tech with the 2023 Amateur Championship, won at Hillside, and the major exemptions that came with it. He opened the 2023 Open Championship at Royal Liverpool with a 66 and held a share of the first round lead as an amateur, and he sat at number one in the world amateur ranking before turning professional in 2024. Two drivers sit in the bag on the only snapshot on record, a Ping G430 LST at 10.5 degrees and a Ping G440 Max at 12 degrees, both built on the same Mitsubishi Tensei 1K White 60 TX, one shaft spec carried across two heads rather than two separate builds. The irons run in three blocks, a Ping iDi 3, i240 in the 5 and 6, Blueprint S from 7 through 9, all on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. Ping through the driver, the irons and the Harwood putter. Ball is a Titleist Pro V1.
christo-lamprecht:2026-08-02.history_narrative: The 2026-08-02 bag is the only snapshot in the database, so there is no change history to trace here. What it does show is a fully Ping setup, two driver heads sharing an identical Tensei 1K White 60 TX build, and a three model iron blend that moves from the iDi long iron into i240 mid irons and Blueprint S blades, all on one shaft, the X100. No wedges are on record in this snapshot.

michael-thorbjornsen:2026-08-02.lede: Michael Thorbjornsen is an American professional from Wellesley, Massachusetts, who won the 2018 U.S. Junior Amateur and went on to a decorated four years at Stanford. He contended on the PGA Tour as an amateur, most notably a top-five finish at the 2022 Travelers Championship while still in college, and he turned professional in 2024 after finishing atop the PGA Tour University standings, which carried immediate PGA Tour membership. The bag is TaylorMade from the tee through the ball, with no other manufacturer represented at any position. The iron setup is the detail worth reading twice: a P770 3-iron, a P7MC 4-iron, then P7MB blades from 5 through pitching wedge, all built on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100, so the profile stiffens visually as the loft increases while the shaft spec never moves. The driver is a Qi4D LS at 9 degrees with a Ventus Black VeloCore+ 7 X, a low-spin head paired with a low-spin shaft. Spider Tour X on the green, TP5 in play.
michael-thorbjornsen:2026-08-02.history_narrative: The 2026-08-02 build is the only snapshot on record in the database, so there is no change history to trace yet. What it establishes is a full TaylorMade setup with a three-model iron blend and a single shaft spec across the entire iron set, which gives future snapshots a clear baseline to be measured against.

keita-nakajima:2026-08-03.lede: Keita Nakajima, born in Tokyo in 2000, spent much of his amateur career at the top of the World Amateur Golf Ranking and collected the Mark H. McCormack Medal as the leading amateur in both 2021 and 2022. His win at the 2021 Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship carried him into the Masters and the Open Championship, and he turned professional in 2023 after also claiming a Japan Golf Tour title while still an amateur. The bag on record is TaylorMade from the driver head to the golf ball, with no outside heads anywhere in the setup. The iron build is the detail worth noting: a P790 at the 4, then P7CB from 5 through 9, all on Nippon N.S. Pro Modus3 Tour 120 X, so one shaft profile runs the length of the set while the head shape changes at the top. Driver is a Qi4D at 9 degrees with Graphite Design Tour AD FI 6 X. Two putters sit on the record, the TP Reserve TR-B11 and the Spider Tour V, a blade and a mallet rather than a settled single choice. Ball is TP5.

gordon-sargent:2026-08-03.lede: Gordon Sargent came out of Vanderbilt with a resume built on amateur golf's biggest stages. He won the NCAA Division I individual title as a freshman in 2022, held the No. 1 spot in the World Amateur Golf Ranking, played the 2023 Walker Cup for the United States, and became the first player to earn PGA Tour membership through the PGA Tour University Accelerated program before turning professional. The bag is Titleist from the tee through the irons, with no second brand anywhere in the setup. Driver is a GTS2 at 9 degrees with a Mitsubishi Tensei 1K White 60 TX. The irons run three models deep: a T250 3-iron on a Nippon Modus3 Graphite on Steel Technology Hybrid X, T100 in the 4 through 6 slots, and 620 MB blades from 7 down through 9, all three of those on Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100. A Scotty Cameron Newport Prototype closes it out. Only one snapshot is on record, so there is nothing yet to compare against.
gordon-sargent:2026-08-03.history_narrative: The 2026-08-03 build is the only snapshot in the database for Sargent, which makes it a baseline rather than a trend. What stands out is how uniform it is: one brand across driver, irons, and putter, with the iron set stepping through three models, a T250 long iron, T100 in the middle, and 620 MB blades in the scoring end. The only shaft break from Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 is the graphite-on-steel Modus3 in the 3-iron. There is no switch history to trace here yet.

nicolai-hojgaard:2026-07-30.lede: Nicolai Hojgaard is a Danish professional and the twin brother of Rasmus Hojgaard. He won three times on the DP World Tour, including the 2023 Italian Open at Marco Simone, and returned to that same course weeks later as a rookie on Europe's winning Ryder Cup team. He has since competed on the PGA Tour. The Triple Diamond stamp is the through line in the driver slot, carried from the Paradym to the Paradym Ai Smoke to the current Quantum Triple Diamond Max, listed at 10.5 degrees and turned up to 11.5 on a Fujikura Ventus Black TR 6 X. Every snapshot is full Callaway from tee to green, with the Chrome Tour X ball unchanged throughout. The irons are where the movement is: Apex MB in the earliest snapshot, X Forged in the middle, and both in play now, an X Forged 4 iron on Project X Red Rifle ahead of Apex MB 5 through PW on Project X LZ. The putter is back to a Jailbird Mini shape after a stretch in an Ai-ONE Milled Eight T.
nicolai-hojgaard:2026-07-30.history_narrative: All three snapshots are Callaway across driver, irons, putter and ball, with no brand movement recorded at any point. The driver progresses through the Callaway Triple Diamond line, Paradym to Paradym Ai Smoke to Quantum Triple Diamond Max, and the Chrome Tour X ball holds steady across every snapshot. The irons alternate rather than settle, Apex MB in the oldest bag, X Forged in the middle one, and a combination of the two in the current setup. The putter follows a similar loop, an Odyssey Jailbird Mini in the earliest snapshot, an Ai-ONE Milled Eight T DB in between, and an Ai-ONE Jailbird Mini DB now.

doug-ghim:2026-08-04.lede: Doug Ghim left the University of Texas with one of the stronger amateur resumes of his class: the 2016 Western Amateur, runner-up at the 2017 U.S. Amateur, a place on the winning 2017 Walker Cup team, and low amateur honors at the 2018 Masters. He turned professional that summer and has worked between the PGA Tour and Korn Ferry Tour since, with his record built on contention and consistent status rather than trophies. The GTS2 driver is set at 10 degrees in the C1 SureFit position with a Mitsubishi Diamana BB 63 TX, a conventional weight and profile for that head. The iron set is split, a T250 4-iron ahead of T100s from 5 through 9, with Project X Rifle 6.5 shafts running through the whole set, so the flex and step pattern stay uniform across the transition. Putter is a Scotty Cameron Phantom 9R prototype, ball is a Pro V1x. Every logo in the recorded bag is Titleist or a Titleist company.
doug-ghim:2026-08-04.history_narrative: The 2026-08-04 bag is the only snapshot in the database for Ghim, so nothing here can be described as a change or a holdover. What it does document is a fully Titleist setup, a split T250 and T100 iron set on one shaft spec, and a Phantom 9R prototype putter rather than a retail model. Additional entries will be needed before any movement can be tracked.

michael-brennan:2026-08-05.lede: Michael Brennan came out of Wake Forest with a heavy amateur resume and turned it into a PGA Tour card in a hurry, winning the 2025 Bank of Utah Championship in one of his first professional starts on Tour. The win moved him straight into full status without the usual Korn Ferry apprenticeship. The bag is Titleist top to bottom, and the interesting part is how traditional it stays. A GT3 driver at 8 degrees in the C3 SureFit setting, a T150 3-iron as the long end of the set, then 620 CB blades from 4 through 9. Project X handles every shaft: HZRDUS Silver TX 70g in the driver, HZRDUS Black TX 105 HY in the 3-iron, Rifle 6.5 steel through the irons. The putter is a Scotty Cameron Circle T TG6 Prototype, tour issue only. Every driver on record for him carries the same badge, which is what a single manufacturer relationship looks like from the start rather than after a few years of shopping around.
michael-brennan:2026-08-05.history_narrative: The 2026-08-05 build is the only snapshot the database holds for Brennan, so there is no change history to trace yet. What it establishes is a full Titleist head setup with a single shaft house behind it, muscleback CBs in the scoring end, and a Circle T putter. Everything future snapshots get measured against starts here.

seamus-power:2026-08-06.lede: Seamus Power is from Waterford, played college golf at East Tennessee State, and represented Ireland at the 2016 Olympics in Rio before earning his PGA Tour card by way of the Korn Ferry Tour. He has two PGA Tour titles, the 2021 Barbasol Championship and the 2022 Butterfield Bermuda Championship, both won in playoffs. The PING G430 LST at 9 degrees is the head recorded in the three most recent snapshots, now behind a Project X HZRDUS Smoke Green 6.5 TX in 60 gram weight. Every driver on record here is PING, going back to the G410 in the 2021 snapshot, and the putter has never left the PLD line, moving from a PLD 3 prototype through a PLD 3 Mallet and a PLD Plus to the current PLD3. The iron setup is the part that has actually moved. What was once a three model stack is now a two model build, i240 in the 4 and 5 and Blueprint T from 6 through pitching wedge, all on Project X Rifle 6.5.

mark-hubbard:2026-08-06.lede: Mark Hubbard is an American professional out of Denver, Colorado, who played college golf at San Jose State and turned professional in 2011. He earned his way to the PGA Tour through the Korn Ferry Tour, where he has won, and has spent the bulk of his career on the PGA Tour without a major title. The PING G430 LST at 10.5 degrees sits in front of a full set of PING Blueprint T irons, 4 through W, a demanding blade from the same manufacturer that supplies the driver. PING is the only driver brand on record, and the iron set reinforces that. The shafts do not follow one another: Nippon N.S. Pro Modus3 105 X in the irons pairs a lighter weight class with an X profile, while the driver runs an Aretera AO2 Blue 65 S. Two Odyssey putters are logged, the Ai-One Jailbird Mini S and a TRTL Prototype, with a Titleist Pro V1 in play.
mark-hubbard:2026-08-06.history_narrative: The 2026-08-06 bag is the only snapshot in the database, so there is no change history to trace here. What it does show is a single-brand spine, PING driver through PING blades, with a blade set carried all the way down to the 4 iron. The two Odyssey putters on record are the one open question in an otherwise settled setup.

jordan-spieth:2026-08-07.lede: Jordan Spieth is an American professional on the PGA Tour with three major championships: the 2015 Masters, the 2015 U.S. Open, and the 2017 Open Championship. He reached world number one in 2015, won the FedEx Cup that same season, and the PGA Championship remains the only leg of the career Grand Slam outstanding. The Scotty Cameron Circle T 009 that appears in all nine historical snapshots is gone, replaced by a T.P. Mills Trad II. Everything else stays inside Titleist. The driver line runs TS3 to TSi3 to TSR2 to the current GTS2, 10 degrees at a D1 SureFit setting behind a Ventus Black 6 X. T100 irons have held the mid and short slots in every snapshot on record, with the long end rotating through a U-500, a T150, and now a T200 2-iron on a Tour AD DI 105 hybrid shaft. The ball moved from Pro V1x to Pro V1x Left Dash.
jordan-spieth:2026-08-07.history_narrative: Across ten snapshots the head brand never changes. Titleist covers the driver, the irons, and the ball throughout, with the driver progressing TS3 to TSi3 to TSR2 to GTS2 while the T100 irons hold their slots and the long iron position cycles through a U-500, a T200, a T150, and back to a T200. The putter is the outlier: a Scotty Cameron Circle T 009 in all nine historical entries, with a T.P. Mills Trad II listed in the current bag. The ball follows the same pattern of late movement, Pro V1x in every historical snapshot and Pro V1x Left Dash now.

brandt-snedeker:2026-08-07.lede: Brandt Snedeker is a nine-time PGA Tour winner who took the 2012 FedExCup with a victory at the Tour Championship, and he was named PGA Tour Rookie of the Year in 2007. He shot 59 in the opening round of the 2018 Wyndham Championship and won the tournament. He has represented the United States in both the Ryder Cup and the Presidents Cup. The full PING iron block is the notable piece of the current setup, an iDi 3 iron ahead of i240s in 4 through 9, with AeroTech SteelFiber i95 shafts under the set. The driver is a TaylorMade Qi4D, returning to a brand that appears in the 2021 snapshot after two straight snapshots built around a Titleist TSR2. Odyssey has held the putter slot in every snapshot, the White Hot XG Rossie earlier and a TRTL Prototype now, with a TaylorMade Spider Tour X also logged. Titleist Pro V1x has been the ball since the Bridgestone Tour B X period.
brandt-snedeker:2026-08-07.history_narrative: The driver line moves from a PING G410 Plus to a TaylorMade SIM2 Max, then two snapshots of the Titleist TSR2, and now the TaylorMade Qi4D. Irons turn over at every snapshot: Srixon Z 785, Miura CB-301, Bridgestone J15CB paired with Srixon ZX MKII, J15CB again paired with PXG 0317 T, and a straight PING build of iDi and i240 in the current bag. Odyssey is the one constant across all five snapshots, with the White Hot XG Rossie carrying four of them before the TRTL Prototype. The ball switched from Bridgestone Tour B X to Titleist Pro V1x and has stayed there since.

tony-finau:2026-08-07.lede: Tony Finau is an American professional on the PGA Tour, raised in Salt Lake City and of Tongan and Samoan descent. He has six PGA Tour victories, including wins in consecutive weeks at the 2022 3M Open and Rocket Mortgage Classic, and has represented the United States on three Ryder Cup teams. A major has not come yet, though he has posted top-10 finishes in all four. The Nike Vapor Fly Pro 3 iron is the piece that dates the bag. It sits in all twelve snapshots on record, a discontinued blade long iron kept in play long after Nike stopped building clubs, now on a Graphite Design Tour AD DI 105 Hybrid X shaft. Everything around it is PING. The driver runs G425 LST to G430 LST to the current G440 LST at 9 degrees set to 7.75, and the irons have followed PING's Blueprint line through the S and T variants. Only the putter has ever left the building.
tony-finau:2026-08-07.history_narrative: Across twelve snapshots the driver never leaves PING, progressing G425 LST to G430 LST to G440 LST, and the Nike Vapor Fly Pro 3 iron survives every single one of them. The irons move within one family, from Blueprint to Blueprint S to the Blueprint T now paired with KBS $-Taper 130 shafts. The putter is the only real outlier: a Piretti Elite Prototype in the earliest snapshot, then a long run of PING PLD Anser 2 and Anser 2D prototypes, and most recently the PING Scottsdale TEC Ally Blue. Ball play is Titleist throughout, with the Pro V1 Left Dot appearing early and settling in as the constant.

aaron-rai:2026-08-09.lede: Aaron Rai is an Englishman out of Wolverhampton who came up through the Challenge Tour and the DP World Tour before establishing himself on the PGA Tour. He won the Hong Kong Open in 2018 and the Scottish Open in 2020, then took his first PGA Tour title at the 2024 Wyndham Championship. He plays with a glove on each hand and sits among the most accurate drivers in the sport. The M6 head is the detail worth stopping on. It is a 2019 release and it is still in the bag at 9 degrees with an Aldila Synergy Blue 70 TX, present in every snapshot on record. The P7TW blades in 5 through 9 and the Titleist Pro V1 are just as fixed. Movement shows up at the two ends of the bag: a Titleist GT2 logged alongside the M6 in early 2025, and a putter slot where the TP Hydro Blast DuPage gave way to a Spider Tour V and then returned.
aaron-rai:2026-08-09.history_narrative: Across five snapshots dated August 2024 through August 2026, the TaylorMade M6 driver, the P7TW irons and the Titleist Pro V1 never leave the bag. The February 2025 snapshot is the only one showing a second driver, a Titleist GT2 recorded next to the M6, with TaylorMade holding the slot in every snapshot before and after it. The putter is the other variable: the TP Hydro Blast DuPage runs from 2024 through mid 2025, a Spider Tour V is in place by May 2026, and the DuPage is back in the current build.

alex-noren:2026-08-08.lede: Alex Noren is a Swedish professional who built his career on the DP World Tour, where he has won ten times, including the 2017 BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth. He played on the winning European Ryder Cup side at Le Golf National in 2018. His first PGA Tour title came at the 2025 Cognizant Classic. The Quantum Max D driver sits at 9 degrees in a draw setting with a Graphite Design Tour AD VF 6 X, the latest in an unbroken run of Callaway heads going back to the Epic Max LS in the 2021 snapshot. Across all seven records the bag has never left the Callaway and Odyssey ecosystem. The Odyssey O-Works #1W putter is in every one of them. The irons went from Apex Pro to Apex TCB between the 2022 and 2023 snapshots and have stayed there, and the ball record shows Chrome Soft X giving way to Chrome Tour. Draw bias is a recurring theme in the driver line, with Max D and Max LS heads dominating the record.
alex-noren:2026-08-08.history_narrative: Seven snapshots, one brand. Callaway driver, Callaway irons, Odyssey putter, Callaway ball in every record from 2021 forward. The driver moved through Epic Max LS, Rogue ST Max LS, Paradym, three straight snapshots of Paradym Ai Smoke Max D, and now Quantum Max D, while the irons shifted once, from Apex Pro to Apex TCB, between the 2022 and 2023 entries. The ball went from Chrome Soft X to Chrome Tour somewhere after the 2023 snapshot, and the O-Works #1W putter never changed at all.

asterisk-talley:2026-08-10.lede: Asterisk Talley is an American amateur out of Chowchilla, California, and one of the more decorated juniors to come through the state in recent years. She was runner up at the 2024 U.S. Women's Amateur, took the Girls Junior PGA Championship that same summer, and represented the United States in the 2024 Curtis Cup. She has also played her way into contention in LPGA majors as an amateur while still in high school. The bag is TaylorMade tee to green with no split allegiance anywhere in it: Qi4D driver at 9 degrees, P770 in the 4 and 5, P7MC from 6 through pitching wedge, Spider Tour V Torched putter, TP5x ball. The iron build is the detail worth sitting with. KBS TGI 100 graphite runs the full set, long irons and blades alike, instead of the steel most players at this level default to. One brand, one shaft spec, nothing mixed in.
asterisk-talley:2026-08-10.history_narrative: The 2026-08-10 setup is the only snapshot on record in the database, so there is no change history to read against it. What it shows is a fully committed TaylorMade bag with a two model iron set, P770 in the long irons stepping into P7MC blades at the 6, tied together by a single graphite shaft spec through all seven clubs.

shane-lowry:2026-08-11.lede: Shane Lowry is an Irish professional who won the 2019 Open Championship at Royal Portrush, taking the Claret Jug on home soil. He won the Irish Open as an amateur in 2009, added the WGC-Bridgestone Invitational in 2015, and has played Ryder Cup golf for Europe. He carries membership on both the PGA Tour and the DP World Tour. Two drivers sit in the current build, a Srixon ZXi LS+ and a Srixon ZXi RKT LS+, both at 9 degrees and both fitted with the same Mitsubishi Diamana x5ct 70 TX. Every driver across the nine snapshots is a Srixon, running from the Z 585 through the ZX5 family and into the ZXi generation with no brand deviation anywhere in the record. The irons split by shaft rather than by brand, Nippon Modus3 120 X in the ZXi5 long irons and KBS Tour 130 X through the ZXi7 scoring set. The Z-Star XV ball is the single unbroken line.
shane-lowry:2026-08-11.history_narrative: Across all nine snapshots the woods, irons and ball are Srixon, moving from the Z 585 and Z U85 era through the ZX and ZX MKII generations and into the current ZXi models, with Z-Star XV in play the whole time. The putter is the only piece to leave the pattern, an Odyssey Stroke Lab Exo 2-Ball in the earliest snapshots, an Odyssey White Hot OG 2-Ball in the 2023 and 2024 entries, and a TaylorMade Spider Tour Z from the February 2025 snapshot onward. A Srixon driving iron shows up in most of the record, listed as Z U85, ZX U, ZX U MKII and ZXiU, but no utility iron is logged in the current bag.

zach-bauchou:2026-08-11.lede: Zach Bauchou came out of Oklahoma State, where he was part of the 2018 NCAA Division I championship team alongside Viktor Hovland, Matthew Wolff and Austin Eckroat. The Virginia native turned professional after his college run and has worked the developmental ranks since, with starts on the Korn Ferry Tour and the circuits that feed it. The iron stack is the tell here: three separate Wilson Staff Model builds in one bag, a Utility 4 iron on a Mitsubishi MMT HY 100 TX, CB heads from 4 through 7, and the 2026 XB heads from 8 through pitching wedge, everything below the utility on Project X Rifle 6.5. That is a blended progression built for one player rather than a stock set pulled off a shelf. The driver is a PING G425 LST at 9 degrees with a Ventus Blue TR 6 X, a head several release cycles behind current, and PING is the only driver brand on record. Putter is a Scotty Cameron Newport 2 Prototype, ball is the Bridgestone Tour B X.
zach-bauchou:2026-08-11.history_narrative: The 2026-08-11 bag is the only snapshot in the database for Bauchou, so there is no change history to read against it. What stands out in that single record is the three-model Wilson iron progression and a PING driver head that has been superseded twice over in the retail line. Both point to a setup chosen on fit rather than on what is new.
